nodes.name: Paper editorial
nodes.summary: Warm off-white canvas that reads like paper, a serif display face over a quiet sans, hairline rules, one restrained accent.

nodes.name: Swiss grid
nodes.summary: Black, white and one accent on a visible grid; type does the work, nothing is decorated.

nodes.name: Monochrome engineering
nodes.summary: Greys with colour only where it means something, one sans for everything and mono for code, borders that are earned.
tells_to_avoid: mono for anything that is not data

nodes.name: Soft product
nodes.summary: Friendly product UI: large radius, soft layered shadows, a clear primary, airy cards, pill buttons.
tells_to_avoid: the same grey shadow under everything

nodes.name: Dark console
nodes.summary: Near-black neutral surfaces, hairline borders, mono labels for data, one restrained accent; the look of a good terminal.
tells_to_avoid: medium grey body text on black

nodes.name: Luminous dark
nodes.summary: Dark canvas with one glowing hue, blurred gradient light, glassy raised panels and product imagery doing the talking.

nodes.name: Quiet luxury
nodes.summary: Generous space, a refined serif, muted low-chroma palette, square corners and almost no chrome.

nodes.name: Neo-brutalist
nodes.summary: Flat saturated fills, thick dark borders, hard offset shadows, raw grotesque type; deliberately unpolished.

nodes.name: Playful geometric
nodes.summary: Bright flat colour blocks, geometric shapes, pill everything, bouncy motion; made to be liked.

nodes.name: Warm organic
nodes.summary: Earth tones, rounded forms, generous line height, photography with large radius; calm and human.
tells_to_avoid: cream and terracotta as a default

nodes.name: Glass layered
nodes.summary: Translucent panels over a coloured field, blur used only where a surface really floats over content.

nodes.name: Bento showcase
nodes.summary: A grid of unequal cells, each showing one real product capability with a small mono caption.
tells_to_avoid: cells with icons instead of product

nodes.name: Poster type
nodes.summary: Display type at poster scale is the image; everything else is small, aligned and quiet.
tells_to_avoid: one word in a different colour

nodes.name: Hazard Yellow

nodes.name: Sky & Tomato
nodes.notes: Bright sky blue primary with a tomato accent on cool white; playful geometric, kids, consumer apps.

nodes.name: Poppy & Cream
nodes.notes: Poppy red-orange primary with a leaf-green accent on cream; playful retail, food delivery, brutalist menus.

nodes.name: Fraunces / Figtree
nodes.notes: Fraunces' soft old-style curves carry the personality at display sizes while Figtree stays quiet and even in running text; keep Fraunces upright and under 64px to avoid the oversized-italic-serif tell.

nodes.name: Instrument Serif / Instrument Sans
nodes.notes: Drawn as a family, the condensed high-contrast serif and the neutral grotesque share proportions, so headlines feel sharp without the body fighting them; use the roman, not the italic, for H1.

nodes.name: Newsreader / Source Sans 3
nodes.notes: Newsreader's optical-size axis keeps headlines crisp and decks readable, and Source Sans 3's humanist rhythm matches its transitional body shapes for long-form reading.

nodes.name: Source Serif 4 / Public Sans
nodes.notes: Two workhorse faces with matched x-heights: Source Serif 4 gives documents authority, Public Sans keeps UI and forms plain and legible, the kind of pairing legal and fintech products can trust.

nodes.name: Libre Caslon Text / Work Sans
nodes.notes: Caslon's sturdy old-style forms give headlines a printed-book weight and Work Sans, an early-grotesque revival, is period-adjacent without competing in texture.

nodes.name: Playfair Display / DM Sans
nodes.notes: A Didone headline needs a low-contrast geometric body, which DM Sans supplies; the classic magazine contrast works because the sans has no calligraphic stress to argue with (never swap in a humanist sans).

nodes.name: Cormorant Garamond / Hanken Grotesk
nodes.notes: Cormorant's small x-height and long extenders read as refinement at large sizes, and Hanken Grotesk's plain, slightly narrow grotesque recedes so the serif and the whitespace carry the page.

nodes.name: Literata / Albert Sans
nodes.notes: Literata was drawn for long screen reading and its optical sizes keep headlines from going spindly; Albert Sans adds a soft geometric counterpoint for UI labels without stealing attention.

nodes.name: Lora / Nunito Sans
nodes.notes: Lora's brushy, moderate-contrast serif and Nunito Sans' rounded humanist forms share a gentle calligraphic stress, so the pairing feels warm and organic rather than corporate.

nodes.name: EB Garamond / Onest
nodes.notes: Old-style Garamond and a humanist sans descend from the same broad-nib stress, so unlike Didone + humanist this is harmonious; Onest's slightly larger x-height keeps body copy modern.

nodes.name: Young Serif / Rethink Sans
nodes.notes: Young Serif's heavy, low-contrast letterforms behave like a display face so one weight is enough; Rethink Sans' clean geometry keeps the page from tipping into kitsch.

nodes.name: Gloock / Manrope
nodes.notes: Gloock is a single-weight Didone built for poster sizes, so pair it with Manrope's even geometric strokes at 1.414 scale and keep it to one or two lines per page; a humanist body would clash with its vertical stress.

nodes.name: DM Serif Display / DM Sans
nodes.notes: Designed as siblings, DM Serif Display's Scotch-roman contrast and DM Sans' low-contrast geometry share a skeleton, which is why the heading and body feel like one voice at two volumes.

nodes.name: Inter Tight / Inter
nodes.notes: Inter Tight gives the headline the tight tracking Inter lacks at display sizes so the family stops looking like an unchosen default; only use it with a distinct accent colour and real product imagery.

nodes.name: Geist / Geist
nodes.notes: One sans for everything with Geist Mono reserved for code, paths and IDs is the Vercel design.md recipe; the discipline is in the restraint, not the face.

nodes.name: Bricolage Grotesque / Figtree
nodes.notes: Bricolage's optical-size axis turns on its wonky display details only at headline sizes, and Figtree's smooth geometry below it keeps the quirk from infecting the reading text.

nodes.name: Schibsted Grotesk / Inter
nodes.notes: A newspaper grotesque with real character at headline sizes over Inter at text sizes gives a Swiss-grid page two distinct voices without leaving the grotesque family.

nodes.name: Plus Jakarta Sans / Plus Jakarta Sans
nodes.notes: A single geometric family at two weights is the quietest way to get a soft product voice; the slightly rounded terminals read friendly without needing pill-shaped type tricks.

nodes.name: Outfit / Nunito Sans
nodes.notes: Outfit's pure circles and verticals suit bright colour blocks and big rounded cards, and Nunito Sans softens the body copy so the page stays likeable rather than cold.

nodes.name: Sora / Work Sans
nodes.notes: Sora's wide, slightly squared geometry reads as technical on a dark canvas, and Work Sans' plainer grotesque keeps paragraphs neutral under glow and glass effects.

nodes.name: Host Grotesk / Funnel Sans
nodes.notes: Two 2024-25 Google releases nobody has defaulted to yet: Host Grotesk's compact grotesque headlines over Funnel Sans' open geometric text avoid the Inter-everywhere tell while staying strictly neutral.

nodes.name: Chivo / Be Vietnam Pro
nodes.notes: Chivo's heavy grotesque weights give headlines the punch a visible grid wants, and Be Vietnam Pro's cleaner neo-grotesque keeps body text from going muddy at small sizes.

nodes.name: Atkinson Hyperlegible Next / Atkinson Hyperlegible Next
nodes.notes: Built for low-vision readers with unambiguous glyphs, this family at two weights is the safe choice for dense tables and forms where character confusion costs money.

nodes.name: Archivo / Archivo
nodes.notes: Archivo's width axis lets the heading run condensed and heavy while the body stays normal width, so one grotesque does both jobs on a visible grid with hard edges.

nodes.name: Roboto Flex / Roboto Flex
nodes.notes: Roboto Flex's optical-size and grade axes keep 12px table text and 40px titles equally crisp, and its tabular figures line up in tight rows; one variable file covers the whole dashboard.

nodes.name: Manrope / IBM Plex Sans
nodes.notes: Manrope's rounded geometric headlines carry the product personality and IBM Plex Sans' slightly engineered grotesque keeps settings pages and forms businesslike underneath.

nodes.name: JetBrains Mono / Inter
nodes.notes: Mono headlines at a modest 1.2 scale read like a good terminal prompt rather than a gimmick, and Inter below them keeps prose and tables legible on near-black surfaces.

nodes.name: IBM Plex Mono / IBM Plex Sans
nodes.notes: Plex Mono and Plex Sans share widths and weights, so mono headings, sans prose and mono data columns align on the same baseline grid without visual seams.

nodes.name: Geist Mono / Geist
nodes.notes: Leading with Geist Mono for titles and captions and dropping to Geist for sentences gives bento cells and dark consoles a data-first voice while staying one coherent superfamily.

nodes.name: Space Mono / Space Grotesk
nodes.notes: Space Mono's quirky retro terminals make a deliberately unpolished headline, and Space Grotesk (its proportional sibling) carries the same DNA; reserve it for brutalist pages since Space Grotesk alone is now a default tell.

nodes.name: Martian Mono / Public Sans
nodes.notes: Martian Mono's width axis gives compact mono headers and labels that sit over dense tables, and Public Sans' neutral neo-grotesque handles the surrounding UI copy.

nodes.name: Azeret Mono / Albert Sans
nodes.notes: Azeret Mono is a chunky display mono built to be set large with thick borders and hard shadows, and Albert Sans' plain geometry keeps the body copy from adding more noise.

nodes.name: Syne / Manrope
nodes.notes: Syne's extended heavy weights are the image at poster scale, so everything else is small Manrope aligned to the grid; one headline per screen is the rule.

nodes.name: Unbounded / Onest
nodes.notes: Unbounded's ultra-wide geometric display letters fill a hero on their own; Onest's compact humanist body is the counterweight that keeps the rest of the page readable.

nodes.name: Archivo Black / Archivo
nodes.notes: Archivo Black is the fat grotesque neo-brutalism wants for flat fills and thick borders, and regular Archivo is literally the same design at text weight so the hierarchy is seamless.

nodes.name: Anton / Work Sans
nodes.notes: Anton's tall condensed caps pack a long headline into a tight block, and Work Sans' wider grotesque text opens the page back up beneath it; set Anton tight and never in italic.

nodes.name: Clash Display / Satoshi
nodes.notes: Clash Display's wide, slightly squared display forms give poster-type headlines a distinct 2020s brand voice, and Satoshi (same foundry) is a neutral geometric that stays out of the way; self-host both via Fontshare.

nodes.name: Cal Sans / Hanken Grotesk
nodes.notes: Cal Sans is the single-weight display face Cal.com ships for headlines; over Hanken Grotesk's plain text it gives a product page a clear, non-default headline voice at low cost.

nodes.name: Roboto Slab / Roboto Flex
nodes.notes: Roboto Slab and Roboto Flex share a skeleton, so slab headings over a flexible neo-grotesque body give documentation and dense admin pages structure without any stylistic seam.

nodes.name: Zilla Slab / Lato
nodes.notes: Zilla Slab's soft slab serifs (Mozilla's brand face) and Lato's warm humanist sans both have a slight calligraphic warmth, so the pairing feels approachable rather than mechanical.

nodes.name: Bitter / Hanken Grotesk
nodes.notes: Bitter was drawn as a reading slab for screens, so its headings stay soft and even, and Hanken Grotesk's quiet grotesque body keeps long articles calm.

nodes.name: System UI / System UI
nodes.notes: Zero font requests and native rendering on every platform; the right call for app shells, glass companions and data tools where the OS face is the honest choice.

nodes.name: System Serif / System Sans
nodes.fallback_heading: ui-serif, 'Iowan Old Style', Georgia, 'Times New Roman', serif
nodes.notes: New York on Apple and Georgia elsewhere give an editorial headline with no webfont cost, over the platform sans; useful for content sites that must be fast on first paint.

nodes.name: Studio wrap
nodes.summary: A pale neutral canvas, one giant grotesque headline with alternating indents wrapping a single flat disc of saturated colour, square corners, almost no chrome; a designer's own site, not a product template.

nodes.name: Lab figures
nodes.summary: Near-black lab notebook: line-art isometric figures with mono captions (Fig 0.1), a two-tone statement paragraph instead of a headline and buttons, hairline column rules.

nodes.name: Split nav with live metadata
nodes.what: Navigation reduced to three things: the wordmark left, a mono line in the centre with the studio's city and local time ticking each second, and a single word 'Menu' on the right. No link row, no button.
nodes.implementation: Three-column grid; centre cell is mono 11px with letter-spacing .06em; a 1s setInterval updates the time; the menu word toggles an overlay.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Live metadata is specific to the owner and never appears in generated sites.

nodes.name: Menu word and full-screen overlay
nodes.what: The nav holds only the wordmark and the word 'Menu'. Clicking it opens a full-viewport overlay in the ink colour with four to six links at display size, each entering with an 80ms stagger, and a 'Close' word where 'Menu' was.
nodes.implementation: A dialog element or a fixed div with role=dialog; links at clamp(2.5rem, 7vw, 6rem); transform translateY(20px) to 0 with ease-out over 500ms; Escape closes; respect reduced motion by fading only.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Generated sites always show the link row; a word-only nav reads as designed.

nodes.name: Floating pill nav
nodes.what: A compact pill detached from the top edge by 16px, centred, holding the wordmark and three links, with a blurred backdrop only once content scrolls under it.
nodes.implementation: position: sticky; top: 16px; width: max-content; margin-inline: auto; border-radius: 999px; backdrop-filter: blur(12px) applied with a scroll-driven animation or a class toggled after 40px of scroll.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Common on 2024 Framer templates; acceptable on soft product sites, avoid elsewhere.

nodes.name: Numbered index rail
nodes.what: A thin left rail with section numbers 01 to 05 in mono; the current section's number is in text colour, the rest muted; clicking jumps. The main nav is a single line at the top.
nodes.implementation: position: fixed; left: 24px; top: 50%; translate: 0 -50%; IntersectionObserver sets aria-current; hidden under 1024px.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Rails tied to real sections show structure, which templates do not have.

nodes.name: Giant word ticker hero
nodes.what: The first screen is the brand name or a two-word claim at 18 to 22vw, repeated as a single-line marquee that moves at about 60px per second, with one sentence and one link set small beneath it.
nodes.implementation: A flex track duplicated once, animation: translateX(-50%) linear 40s infinite; prefers-reduced-motion pauses it; font-size clamp(5rem, 20vw, 22rem); line-height .8; letter-spacing -.05em.
nodes.ai_tell_note: A marquee of logos is a tell; a single giant moving word as the hero is a studio move, keep it to one.

nodes.name: Type specimen hero
nodes.what: The headline is presented like a foundry specimen: the sentence at display size with mono metadata around it (face name, size in px, weight, the date), hairlines above and below, and the alphabet or numerals in a strip beneath.
nodes.implementation: Grid with mono labels at 11px in the corners; display line at clamp(3rem, 8vw, 8rem); a second row with 0123456789 in tabular numerals at 24px.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Specimen furniture requires a real face choice and real values.

nodes.name: Manifesto hero
nodes.what: The first screen is one paragraph of 60 to 120 words at 28 to 44px, left aligned, with no headline and no buttons; a single inline link closes the paragraph. The paragraph says what the company believes, in first person plural.
nodes.implementation: max-width 34ch to 40ch; font-size clamp(1.6rem, 3vw, 2.75rem); line-height 1.2; text-wrap: pretty; margin-top 20vh.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Needs real prose; the template cannot fake it.

nodes.name: Three numbers hero
nodes.what: Three large numerals (96 to 160px, tabular) with a one-line caption each, set as the first screen; the product name is only in the nav. The numbers are sourced claims, never invented.
nodes.implementation: Grid of three; font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; captions mono 11px; count-up once when in view if motion is on.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Invented numbers are the tell; sourced ones are the proof.

nodes.name: Type larger than the viewport
nodes.what: The headline is set so large that its first and last letters bleed past the viewport edges; what remains legible is the middle of the word, and a small subhead sits in the exposed corner.
nodes.implementation: font-size clamp(8rem, 28vw, 30rem); white-space: nowrap; margin-inline: -0.12em; overflow-x: clip on the section; line-height .78.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Only a confident brand crops its own name; templates centre it.

nodes.name: Stacked words in alternating faces
nodes.what: Three to four words of the headline stacked one per line, alternating between the heading face solid and the same face outlined, or between the grotesque and a serif, with a hard left edge.
nodes.implementation: display: grid; each span line-height .9; outline lines use -webkit-text-stroke: 1px currentColor; color: transparent.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Serif-italic alternation is now common on templates; outline alternation reads fresher.

nodes.name: Marquee divider line
nodes.what: Between two sections, a single line of mono text (the real client list, the product nouns or the location and year) slides slowly, 40 seconds per loop, separated by small marks, pausing on hover.
nodes.implementation: Track duplicated once; animation 40s linear infinite; mono 12px uppercase off (sentence case), separators as 4px squares in primary.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Logo marquees are a tell; a slow mono text line with real words reads as a studio device.

nodes.name: Giant numerals index
nodes.what: Features or services listed with 01, 02, 03 set at 120 to 200px in muted ink (8 to 12 percent alpha) behind or beside a title and one sentence; hairline between rows.
nodes.implementation: Each row a grid: numeral column 1fr with font-size clamp(5rem, 12vw, 12rem) colour color-mix(text 10%); tabular nums; title at 2xl.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Numbers as the composition rather than as a tiny decoration.

nodes.name: Sticky stacking cards
nodes.what: Three to five full-width cards each sticky at the top; as the page scrolls, the next card slides over the previous one leaving a 16px lip of the earlier cards visible, each with its own surface colour.
nodes.implementation: Each card position: sticky; top: calc(96px + var(--i) * 16px); min-height 70vh; later cards get a slightly darker surface; no JS.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Frequent on Framer templates; works when each card holds a real product state.

nodes.name: Horizontal scroll strip
nodes.what: A row of cards or images that scrolls sideways with scroll snap; the last item is cut by the viewport edge so the overflow is obvious; a mono count '03 / 08' sits above.
nodes.implementation: display: flex; overflow-x: auto; scroll-snap-type: x mandatory; gap 16px; padding-inline-end 25vw; scrollbar hidden; each child scroll-snap-align: start.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Needs real items with different weights; the cut edge is the point.

nodes.name: Hover list with image reveal
nodes.what: Work or features as plain rows (title left, meta right, hairline between). Hovering a row reveals an image that follows the cursor with a 120ms lag; on touch the image sits beside the row.
nodes.implementation: A fixed img element positioned from pointermove with translate3d and a lerp of .12 per frame; rows carry data-image; reduced motion shows the image statically on the right.
nodes.ai_tell_note: The standard studio portfolio list since 2022, never generated by default.

nodes.name: Bordered cells with corner crosses
nodes.what: Content sits in a grid of cells divided by 1px hairlines in text colour at 10 percent alpha, with small plus marks (12px) drawn at the intersections; cells have different spans.
nodes.implementation: Grid with gap 1px and background set to the hairline colour; each cell background bg; crosses are absolutely positioned pseudo-elements at the cell corners.
nodes.ai_tell_note: The engineering grid of Vercel and Linear changelogs; the crosses are the signature.

nodes.name: Hairline accordion
nodes.what: Questions or services as hairline rows; a plus sign at the right rotates 45 degrees to a cross when open; the open row's answer sits at the reading measure; only one open at a time.
nodes.implementation: details and summary elements; summary::after content '+' in mono; transition rotate 200ms; name attribute groups them for exclusive open (Chrome 120, Safari 17.2).
nodes.ai_tell_note: Rows with a plus, not cards with a chevron.

nodes.name: One giant quote
nodes.what: One attributed quote at 40 to 64px in the heading face with hanging punctuation, the opening mark outdented into the margin, and a small attribution line; no carousel, no avatars.
nodes.implementation: hanging-punctuation: first (Safari) with a text-indent fallback of -0.4em; font-size clamp(2rem, 4.5vw, 4rem); max-width 24ch.
nodes.ai_tell_note: A carousel of three invented testimonials is the tell; one real quote at scale is the opposite.

nodes.name: Stat wall
nodes.what: A full-width row of three or four sourced figures at 96px or larger in tabular numerals, each with a one-line label and a footnote number that links to the source.
nodes.implementation: Grid of equal columns with hairline dividers; font-variant-numeric tabular-nums; sup elements link to a sources list in the footer.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Only sourced figures; otherwise this is the invented-stats tell.

nodes.name: Ticket call to action
nodes.what: The closing call to action is drawn as a ticket: a bordered strip with a perforated left edge, a mono meta line (date, seat, price or version) and the single action on the stub.
nodes.implementation: A bordered box with a dashed vertical rule; perforation via radial-gradient mask on the left edge; mono labels 11px.
nodes.ai_tell_note: A physical metaphor tied to real data (release date, plan price).

nodes.name: Colophon footer
nodes.what: A one-line footer in mono: the brand, the year, local time, coordinates of the studio, 'set in <face>', the version or commit hash, and the real links. Nothing else.
nodes.implementation: A single flex row at 11px mono with gap 24px wrapping; time via setInterval; version string injected at build.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Real metadata about the real site.

nodes.name: Film grain overlay
nodes.what: A fixed, full-viewport layer of monochrome noise at 4 to 8 percent opacity over the whole page, which kills the flat digital look and binds colours together.
nodes.implementation: An SVG with feTurbulence baseFrequency .9 numOctaves 3 as a background on a fixed div, pointer-events none, mix-blend-mode multiply on light and screen on dark; or a tiny PNG tile.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Rare on generated sites, common on studio and dark product sites.

nodes.name: Graph paper grid
nodes.what: A 24 or 32px background grid in text colour at 5 to 7 percent alpha behind the hero or the whole page, fading out at the edges.
nodes.implementation: background-image: linear-gradient(hairline 1px, transparent 1px), linear-gradient(90deg, hairline 1px, transparent 1px); background-size 32px 32px; mask-image radial-gradient for the fade.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Common on developer tools; keep the alpha low and the grid honest to the layout gutters.

nodes.name: Crosses at grid intersections
nodes.what: Small plus marks, 10 to 12px, drawn where section gutters meet, instead of full grid lines.
nodes.implementation: Pseudo-elements with two 1px bars; placed at section corners via position absolute; colour text at 30 percent.
nodes.ai_tell_note: The Vercel and Geist signature; hand-placed marks, not a pattern.

nodes.name: Scanlines
nodes.what: Repeating 2px horizontal lines at 6 to 10 percent alpha over dark imagery or a dark hero, giving a CRT register without a glow.
nodes.implementation: background: repeating-linear-gradient(0deg, transparent 0 2px, rgb(0 0 0 / .12) 2px 3px) on an overlay; disable under 420px wide.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Tied to hardware and terminal brands; never a default.

nodes.name: Outlined giant word
nodes.what: One word of the display line is drawn as a 1px outline in text colour with a transparent fill, next to solid words; the outlined word is the one the sentence hinges on.
nodes.implementation: span { -webkit-text-stroke: 1px currentColor; color: transparent; paint-order: stroke fill; }
nodes.ai_tell_note: A poster device that depends on type size and weight.

nodes.name: One word in a contrasting face
nodes.what: A single word in the headline switches to a contrasting face (a serif in a grotesque line, or the mono), set roman, same size, slightly lower baseline.
nodes.implementation: span.alt { font-family: var(--pf-font-mono or a serif); font-weight 400; } keep it to one word per page.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Instrument Serif italic as the accent word is a known generated-site tell; use a roman serif or the mono, once.

nodes.name: Vertical side labels
nodes.what: Section labels rotated to read bottom to top along the left gutter in mono 11px; the main column keeps a clean top edge.
nodes.implementation: writing-mode: vertical-rl; rotate: 180deg; position absolute left 0; letter-spacing .08em.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Print-derived; shows the grid has a margin column.

nodes.name: Mono index numbers
nodes.what: Every list item, figure and section carries a small mono index such as ( 01 ), 01 / 05 or Fig 2.3 at 11 to 12px with .06em tracking, in muted ink.
nodes.implementation: font-family var(--pf-font-mono); font-size 11px; letter-spacing .06em; font-variant-numeric tabular-nums; colour text-muted.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Measured on 17 of 47 admired sites; it signals the page was laid out, not generated.

nodes.name: Tight display type
nodes.what: Display lines at letter-spacing -0.04 to -0.06em and line-height .85 to .92, so a two-line headline forms a block; body stays at default tracking.
nodes.implementation: h1 { letter-spacing: -.05em; line-height: .88; text-wrap: balance; } only above 48px.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Templates leave display tracking at 0 or -0.02; the tight block is a typographic decision.

nodes.name: Bracket button
nodes.what: Buttons and links set in mono inside square brackets, [ Get started ], no fill and no border; hover swaps the brackets to filled bars.
nodes.implementation: a::before content '[ '; a::after content ' ]'; font-family mono; hover changes bracket colour to primary; focus ring stays visible.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Terminal and hardware brands; unmistakably chosen.

nodes.name: Fill-up hover button
nodes.what: An outlined button whose fill rises from the bottom on hover over 300ms while the label inverts; the pressed state drops the fill by 2px.
nodes.implementation: A ::before layer with scaleY from 0 to 1, transform-origin bottom, ease-out; label colour via color-mix; reduced motion swaps instantly.
nodes.ai_tell_note: A studio hover that depends on the outline treatment.

nodes.name: Pill with circled icon
nodes.what: A pill button whose label sits left and whose icon lives in a filled circle at the right end; on hover the circle grows to fill the pill and the icon turns 45 degrees.
nodes.implementation: Flex pill; the icon wrapper 32px circle in on-primary over primary; transition transform 250ms; icon from the direction's icon set.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Widespread on Framer templates; fine on soft and playful products, avoid elsewhere.

nodes.name: Offset underline links
nodes.what: Links and secondary actions are plain text with a 1px underline offset by .2em that thickens or shifts colour on hover; no arrows, no chevrons.
nodes.implementation: text-decoration-thickness 1px; text-underline-offset .2em; hover text-decoration-color primary.
nodes.ai_tell_note: The measured default on handmade product sites.

nodes.name: Line mask reveal
nodes.what: On load, each line of the headline rises into view through its own overflow mask, 700 to 900ms, staggered 80ms per line, with a quintic ease-out; nothing else on the page animates.
nodes.implementation: Wrap lines in spans inside overflow:hidden parents; animation translateY(110%) to 0; cubic-bezier(.22,1,.36,1); prefers-reduced-motion fades instead.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Once, on the hero only; the measured norm on studio sites.

nodes.name: Custom cursor dot and ring
nodes.what: An 8px dot that tracks the pointer exactly and a 32px ring that follows with lag; over links the ring grows to 56px and the system cursor is hidden; disabled on touch and under reduced motion.
nodes.implementation: Two fixed divs updated from pointermove with requestAnimationFrame and lerp .15; cursor: none on html when active; pointer: fine media query gate.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Studio sites only; on a SaaS site it reads as decoration.

nodes.name: Magnetic buttons
nodes.what: Primary buttons translate up to 8px toward the pointer when it is within 40px and spring back on leave.
nodes.implementation: pointermove on a wrapper computes the offset; transform translate with a 150ms ease-out; spring back with cubic-bezier(.34,1.56,.64,1); skip on touch.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Studio and portfolio sites; keep to one or two buttons.

nodes.name: Preloader counter
nodes.what: A full-screen curtain in the ink colour with a 0 to 100 counter in mono at the bottom left for about 1.2 seconds, then the curtain lifts and the hero lines reveal.
nodes.implementation: A fixed div; counter via requestAnimationFrame eased; curtain translateY(-100%) 600ms ease-in-out; only once per session (sessionStorage); never under reduced motion.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Showcase level only; on a product site it is a delay.

nodes.name: Count-up numerals
nodes.what: Figures count from 0 to their value once when they enter the viewport, 900ms with an ease-out, in tabular numerals so the layout does not jitter.
nodes.implementation: IntersectionObserver once; requestAnimationFrame interpolation; font-variant-numeric tabular-nums; reduced motion shows the final value.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Only on real figures.

nodes.name: Hover image swap
nodes.what: A product or project image swaps to its second shot on hover or focus with a 150ms crossfade; on touch the second shot is reachable by a swipe.
nodes.implementation: Two stacked images; opacity transition; the second has loading lazy; focus-visible triggers the same.
nodes.ai_tell_note: The commerce standard; honest when both images exist.

nodes.name: Scroll progress hairline
nodes.what: A 1px line at the very top of the viewport that grows with reading progress in the primary colour.
nodes.implementation: animation-timeline: scroll() on a fixed 1px div with transform scaleX from 0 to 1; transform-origin left; fallback none.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Content and documentation pages; invisible until it is useful.

nodes.name: Cross-page view transitions
nodes.what: Navigating between pages crossfades the page and morphs the shared wordmark and the clicked title into place over 250 to 350ms.
nodes.implementation: @view-transition { navigation: auto; } with view-transition-name on the wordmark and the title; reduced motion sets animation none.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Invisible craft; no generated site sets it up.

nodes.name: Dithered imagery
nodes.what: Photographs and artwork are rendered with ordered dithering (a 4x4 Bayer matrix) in two palette colours, bg and text or primary, so imagery becomes part of the type system.
nodes.implementation: A canvas or SVG filter pipeline; in a static draft the art module draws a dithered gradient; keep source images high contrast.
nodes.ai_tell_note: A 2024 to 2026 developer-brand device (Vercel Ship, Basement); rare and specific.

nodes.name: ASCII field artwork
nodes.what: Hero artwork is a field of mono characters whose density maps to a shape or a slow wave; characters are drawn from a small set (., :, +, #) in text colour at 40 percent and primary at the peaks.
nodes.implementation: SVG text rows or a pre element; in production a canvas sampling an image or noise; 12px mono; animation optional at motion level 3.
nodes.ai_tell_note: A terminal and developer-tool signature that stock imagery cannot imitate.

nodes.name: Duotone imagery
nodes.what: Photographs mapped to two palette colours (shadows in ink, highlights in bg or primary) so every image sits in the palette; colour returns on hover where it matters.
nodes.implementation: A greyscale filter and mix-blend-mode multiply over a primary surface, or an SVG feComponentTransfer; hover removes the filter over 200ms.
nodes.ai_tell_note: A tonal decision applied to real photography.

nodes.name: Captioned figures
nodes.what: Every image or artwork carries a caption in mono with a figure number and a short true statement of what it shows; captions sit under or beside the figure, never over it.
nodes.implementation: figure and figcaption; figcaption mono 11px muted with a hairline above; numbering by section.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Measured on Linear, Stripe Press, documentation; the opposite of a floating screenshot.

nodes.name: Rotated stickers
nodes.what: Short true labels (new, 2026, v2, open source) drawn as stickers with thick outlines and a hard shadow, rotated 4 to 12 degrees, placed on artwork or at a section corner.
nodes.implementation: Inline-block with border 2px text colour, box-shadow 4px 4px 0 text, rotate var(--r); never more than three per page.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Brutalist and playful brands only; honest words on them.

nodes.name: Colour-blocked sections
nodes.what: Consecutive full-bleed sections in different solid palette colours (bg, primary with on-primary text, ink with bg text); the nav inverts over each block; no gradients anywhere.
nodes.implementation: Each section sets its own --pf-color-text and background from the palette roles; nav uses mix-blend-mode difference or a class toggled by IntersectionObserver.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Colour as structure instead of decoration; templates use one background.

nodes.name: Inverted closing section
nodes.what: The last call to action and the footer sit on an ink background with bg-coloured text, so the page closes with weight.

nodes.ai_tell_note: A composed ending; templates fade out into a sitemap.

nodes.name: One hot colour
nodes.what: Near-black ink, an off-white paper and one saturated colour (international orange, acid green, cobalt, signal red) used on under 5 percent of the page: one button, one rule, one word.
nodes.implementation: primary is the hot colour; accent equals primary; every other role is a neutral; audit the page for primary coverage.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Discipline about coverage is what reads as designed.

nodes.name: Hanging punctuation
nodes.what: Opening quotation marks and bullets hang into the margin so the text edge stays straight.
nodes.implementation: hanging-punctuation: first allow-end; text-indent -0.4em fallback for blockquotes.
nodes.ai_tell_note: A typesetting detail no template ships.

nodes.name: Tabular numerals everywhere
nodes.what: Every number that could change (prices, counts, dates, times, versions) is set in tabular numerals so columns and counters never shift.
nodes.implementation: font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums on tables, stats, time, prices and nav meta.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Measured on every admired product site.

nodes.name: Plain one-line bar
nodes.what: One line: the wordmark left, three to four text links right, one quiet action; no logo mark, no button fill, 56px tall, hairline under it only after scrolling.
nodes.implementation: Flex row; links at 14px in text-muted turning text on hover; the border-bottom toggled by a scroll class or a scroll-driven animation.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Reads as default only when combined with a centred hero and a filled button; fine with any distinct hero.

nodes.name: Category tiles instead of hero
nodes.what: The page opens on a flat grid of six square-ish category tiles (Women's Outerwear, Men's Outerwear, Bags, Denim, New Arrivals x2), each a lifestyle photo with a one-line label and a small '› Shop' link, under a plain brand name heading. There is no campaign banner, no headline, no button pair.
nodes.why: Reads as a store index rather than an ad, and gets shoppers into a category in one click.
nodes.implementation: CSS grid of 3 columns, aspect-ratio 4/5 images with object-fit: cover; label as <h2> + small anchor with a '›' prefix; container queries drop to 2 columns under 60rem.
nodes.pitfalls: Tiles with identical crops and no label hierarchy look like a stock template; vary portrait and square.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Hero-less commerce openings are a deliberate editorial choice generated layouts almost never make.

nodes.name: Half photo, half overlay card
nodes.what: Hero is a 50/50 split: full-height photograph on one side, and on the other a flat cream card (#f7ecdd on an ivory #fffef2 page) containing a 30px heading, a 14px paragraph and one square-cornered button. Byredo does the same with a card labelled 'Discover the campaign' floating over a 16:9 campaign image.
nodes.why: Separates the image from the words so neither needs a gradient scrim or drop shadow.
nodes.implementation: grid-template-columns: 1fr 1fr; card background var(--surface); no border-radius; stack to one column under 48rem.
nodes.pitfalls: If the card gets a shadow and radius it becomes the generic 'glass card on photo' look.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Flat, opaque, square card with hairline edge is a Swiss editorial move, not a default.

nodes.name: Stacked drop banners, not carousel
nodes.what: Instead of one rotating hero, five full-width campaign banners are stacked vertically down the page, each with its own uppercase headline ('RUNNERS, STAY POSSESSED.', 'IT'S OK TO RUN IN COTTON'), a one-line sub and a single 'SHOP' button. Each banner ships a separate desktop (5120px) and mobile crop.
nodes.why: Every drop gets seen, and scrolling feels like flipping through a lookbook rather than waiting on a slider.
nodes.implementation: <picture> with media-query sources per banner; min-height: 80svh; headline clamp(2.5rem, 8vw, 7rem).
nodes.pitfalls: More than five banners with identical composition becomes a wall; alternate text alignment and crop height.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Generated drafts default to a carousel or a single hero; a stack of full-bleed drops is a merchandising decision.

nodes.name: Transparent nav floating on hero
nodes.what: The 70px-tall top bar has no background: lowercase wordmark and 23px weight-100 links in #e5e5e5 sit directly on the hero photograph; on Nothing the 11px uppercase mono links switch to white over dark photography. No border, no blur, no bar colour.
nodes.why: Removes the 'header box' and makes the first screen one image.
nodes.implementation: header{position:absolute;inset:0 0 auto;background:none} section[data-ink=light] ~ header or use :has() to flip --ink.
nodes.pitfalls: Fails on light photos unless you set the link colour per section; use a data attribute per band.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Generated layouts love a frosted sticky header; the honest version is simply transparent with per-section ink colour.

nodes.name: Drop numbers as navigation and hero
nodes.what: Collections are numbered drops; the nav has a 'Drops' menu listing Drop 7 to Drop 1, the mobile menu shows chips 07 to 01, the hero carousel shows a large '07', and the editorial section repeats a 01–07 index. Nothing is named by season or theme.
nodes.why: A numeric series gives the brand an archive feel and makes 'newest' obvious.
nodes.implementation: Ordered list reversed (<ol reversed>), 2-digit numerals via padStart; hero numeral at clamp(6rem,20vw,16rem) with tabular-nums.
nodes.pitfalls: Numbers need the editorial text alongside them or the shop reads as unlabeled folders.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Numbered-index navigation is a catalogue convention that default templates never pick.

nodes.name: Mega menu as thumbnail index
nodes.what: The Shop menu is a wide panel of five text columns (Shop, Apparel, Accessories, Footwear, More) where each link also carries a small square product thumbnail; Le Labo's equivalent lists all 21 fine fragrances by name plus 15 formats; Kith adds a 'Featured' image tile per column and a row of seasonal campaign tiles.
nodes.why: Turns the menu into the catalogue, so scanning the index replaces browsing a grid.
nodes.implementation: Use popover + anchor positioning for the panel; columns via grid-auto-flow: column; thumbs 40px square object-fit cover.
nodes.pitfalls: Thumbnails at different aspect ratios make the panel look like a bug; fix every thumb to 1:1 at 40px.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Mega menus are common, but the dense typographic index with a thumbnail per line is a store-specific choice.

nodes.name: Menu grouped by activity or style
nodes.what: Alongside the normal Clothing column the Men's panel has an 'Activities' column (Ski & Snowboard: Touring, Freeride, Resort; Trail: Run, Hike; Climb: Alpine, Rock, Boulder). Leica groups cameras under 'Photographic Styles' (Street, Film, Portrait, Architecture, Video) next to the system list.
nodes.why: Shoppers often know what they will do, not which garment type they need.
nodes.implementation: Two <nav> column groups in one panel with <h3> headings; same product collection filtered by a 'use' tag.
nodes.pitfalls: Duplicating products across activity and type columns needs a canonical URL plan.
nodes.ai_tell_note: An activity axis is domain knowledge, which generated navigation never includes.

nodes.name: Per-product dropdown with four verbs
nodes.what: Each product in the nav (Desktop, Laptop 12, Laptop 13, Laptop 16) opens a small dropdown with a thumbnail and exactly four links: Specs, Shop parts, Downloads and guides, Configure now. Support and About get their own panels; a USD selector with flag sits right.
nodes.why: Owners and buyers reach their task in one hop without a generic 'Products' page.
nodes.implementation: <details> or popover per product; links as a 2x2 grid; thumbnail 64px.
nodes.pitfalls: Breaks if a product lacks one of the four destinations; keep the slots and grey one out instead.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Task-verb menus (Configure, Downloads) come from a real support model, not a landing template.

nodes.name: Eleven-pixel uppercase navigation
nodes.what: Nav links are 11px uppercase grotesque, weight 400, letter-spacing 0, pure black on white, about 50–60px bar height, no border and no shadow; wordmark centred at about 19px. Bottega keeps everything at 14px with a 1px ink bottom border on a 44px bar.
nodes.why: Tiny caps read as labels, so the photography stays the largest thing on screen.
nodes.implementation: font-size:11px; text-transform:uppercase; padding:10px 15px; no hover underline, flip to inverse on hover.
nodes.pitfalls: Under 11px fails accessibility; keep tap targets 44px via padding, not font size.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Generated navs run 14–16px medium weight with an active pill; 11px caps is a fashion-house signature.

nodes.name: Live stock line in the header
nodes.what: The header carries a persistent 'Order now' button plus a plain text badge '✓ In stock · Ships in 3-5 business days'. Analogue stamps cards with 'Shipping Now', 'Ships Dec 2026' and 'Sold Out' as status labels; TE shows a persistent 'in cart' link.
nodes.why: Availability is the real question for hardware; answering it in the chrome removes a click.
nodes.implementation:
✓ In stock · Ships in 3–5 business days

at 12px next to the CTA.
nodes.pitfalls: Stale stock copy destroys trust; bind it to inventory data or omit it.
nodes.ai_tell_note: A middle-dot separated status line is a specific hardware-store habit.

nodes.name: Zero-padded cart count
nodes.what: The bag indicator reads 'Bag 00' or 'Cart 00 items' rather than hiding at zero; Telepathic shows 'BAG 0', TE shows 'checkout 0'. The two-digit count sits inline as text, no red bubble.
nodes.why: A visible 00 is a quiet typographic detail that feels like a ledger, and avoids the badge icon cliché.
nodes.implementation: String(count).padStart(2,'0') in a <span aria-live=polite>; font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums.
nodes.pitfalls: Must still announce count changes to screen readers; use aria-live.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Default commerce UI uses an icon with a coloured badge; text with a zero-padded count is handmade.

nodes.name: Account, help and bag as drawers
nodes.what: Account, Help and Bag each open as a right-side drawer with its own 'Close' control rather than navigating away: Help contains chat status ('Available Offline'), hours, phone and size guide; Bag shows an empty state with a 'Continue shopping' link to new arrivals.
nodes.why: Keeps the shopper on the grid while handling service tasks, so the page never reloads.
nodes.implementation: <dialog> opened with showModal(), translateX slide 240ms, width min(420px, 100%); use the popover API for non-modal variant.
nodes.pitfalls: Three drawers that look identical confuse; give each a distinct header label and width.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Drawers for help content, not just cart, show a service design decision.

nodes.name: One size, one weight
nodes.what: Bottega Veneta runs the entire site on 14px/22px with a 12px/18px small tier; hierarchy comes only from weight 700 and uppercase section labels, and no display size exists. Polestar uses a single weight 400 of its custom Unica77 at every size, sentence case throughout.
nodes.why: Extreme restraint reads as confidence and lets product imagery carry all the scale.
nodes.implementation: Define only --text-sm:12px and --text-base:14px; hierarchy via font-weight and text-transform; line-height 22px baseline.
nodes.pitfalls: Without strong imagery the page becomes a wall of same-size text; count on photos for scale.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Generated type scales always include a 48–72px display tier; refusing one is a visible human decision.

nodes.name: Three faces with strict roles
nodes.what: A dot-matrix face (Ndot) is used only for product names ('Phone (4a) Pro', 'Headphone (1)'), an ultra-light grotesque (NType82 at weight 100, 32px) only for editorial headlines and body, and a monospace (LatteraMono) at 11–14px uppercase only for labels, buttons and nav. No face ever crosses roles.
nodes.why: Each typeface signals a content type, so the eye knows what a line is before reading it.
nodes.implementation: @font-face for three families; .sku{font-family:var(--dot)} .label{font-family:var(--mono);text-transform:uppercase;font-size:11px}.
nodes.pitfalls: Substituting a pixel font for Ndot without the mono/light pairing just looks retro-gaming.
nodes.ai_tell_note: A pixel display face reserved for SKUs plus mono labels is a brand system, not a template.

nodes.name: All-lowercase hairline type
nodes.what: Everything, including the wordmark, nav and headlines, is lowercase; weights are capped at 300 with nav at 23px weight 100 and body at 19px weight 100; sizes are calc() expressions against 100vw so type scales fluidly from a 980px reference.
nodes.why: Lowercase plus hairline weight feels like an instruction manual, which matches engineering products.
nodes.implementation: html{text-transform:lowercase} on brand chrome only; font-size:calc(19 / 980 * 100vw); @media (resolution < 2dppx){font-weight:300}.
nodes.pitfalls: Weight 100 on a non-retina screen disappears; serve weight 300 below 2x DPR.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Default drafts use sentence case and medium weights; wholesale lowercase at weight 100 is rare and recognisable.

nodes.name: Sans names, light serif meta
nodes.what: Product name is 19px uppercase grotesque in pure black; the price, sale tag and colour count beneath are 15px Times-style serif at weight 100 in #888888. Body paragraphs are 20px serif weight 100 while headings and buttons are the grotesque, always uppercase.
nodes.why: Inverting the usual serif-headline rule makes the metadata feel like a magazine caption and the product name like a label.
nodes.implementation: .name{font:400 19px/1.37 var(--grot);text-transform:uppercase} .meta{font:100 15px/1.2 var(--serif);color:#888}.
nodes.pitfalls: Serif at weight 100 and 15px in grey is close to illegible on low-contrast screens; keep #888 only for 15px and above.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Serif-for-meta is the opposite of the generated 'serif display headline' tell, so it reads as editorial design.

nodes.name: Headlines that end with a period
nodes.what: Every section heading is a short declarative sentence ending in a full stop: 'The System.', 'The Crank.', 'The Season.', 'All for just $229.'; Norma does 'How it works.', 'Questions.'; Apple's lineup page does 'Explore the lineup.', 'Significant others.'
nodes.why: The period slows the reader and makes each heading sound spoken rather than labelled.
nodes.implementation: Content rule, no CSS; keep headings under 5 words and end each with '.'.
nodes.pitfalls: Only works with two to four word headings; long sentences with periods just look like paragraphs.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Generated copy writes 'Powerful Features for Modern Teams' with no terminal punctuation; the full stop is a voice choice.

nodes.name: Product names as technical designations
nodes.what: Products are named like part numbers with typographic punctuation: 'Phone (4a) Pro', 'Headphone ( 1 ) Pro', 'CMF Speaker M'; Telepathic uses an em dash ('Orchid ORC—1'); Jakobsen uses a slash ('MILLE / 3 Seater'); Carhartt's 'OG Master Pant' lists colour as 'dark navy rinsed'.
nodes.why: Designation-style names look like a catalogue index and let the typeface, not adjectives, carry the brand.
nodes.implementation: Store designation and descriptor as separate fields; render `${code} / ${descriptor}` with tabular-nums.
nodes.pitfalls: Needs consistent punctuation across the entire catalogue or it looks like data errors.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Parenthesised or slashed SKU naming is an industrial-design habit that AI copy avoids.

nodes.name: Caps headlines studded with ™
nodes.what: Headlines and card titles are uppercase and carry registered marks on invented material names: 'MothTech™', 'AmbientWarp™ Cordura® Trail Cap', 'Rippy™ Force Down Program', 'TechSilk™'; Arc'teryx writes 'System 0™'. Technology tiles pair the mark with a two-word caps tagline ('ADAPTIVE INSULATION').
nodes.why: Trademarks signal proprietary engineering and give the copy a spec-sheet tone.
nodes.implementation: Wrap marks in <sup> at 0.6em with vertical-align: super; keep headline letter-spacing 0.02em.
nodes.pitfalls: Fake ™ on ordinary words reads as parody; only mark names you actually own.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Generated copy never invents named fabric technologies with marks.

nodes.name: Negative-tracked display grotesque
nodes.what: Display sizes carry heavy negative tracking that scales with size: -2.82px at 47px and -2.64px at 53px (Analogue, Circular), -4.95px at 110px (Polestar), -3.75px at 100px and -2px at 53px (SSENSE); captions and nav stay at 0. Weights never exceed 500.
nodes.why: Tight large type feels machined, while zero tracking at small sizes keeps labels legible.
nodes.implementation: letter-spacing: calc(-0.045em * (var(--size) / 100)); or set per step: 47px:-0.06em, 110px:-0.045em.
nodes.pitfalls: Tracking below -0.05em at body sizes crushes words; apply only above 40px.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Generated CSS uses tracking-tight (-0.025em) uniformly; a size-dependent curve to -0.05em is a type designer's move.

nodes.name: Footnote glyphs on every claim
nodes.what: Marketing claims carry footnote markers that link to in-page notes: Framework uses a lightning glyph ϟ on its battery claim, Eight Sleep uses *, ◊, ⧫ and ‡ on sleep stats, Oura's '86% of Members' has a numbered footnote, Apple's lineup cards carry superscript numbers to a legal block.
nodes.why: Visible footnotes make bold claims feel audited and give the page a technical-document texture.
nodes.implementation:
ϟ; notes in
at 11px; use :target to highlight.
nodes.pitfalls: A footnote that links nowhere is worse than none; anchor each to a real note.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Generated copy asserts without sources; a footnote apparatus is a real-brand legal habit.

nodes.name: Ivory canvas, graphite ink, terracotta rule
nodes.what: Page background #fffef2, text and 1px hairlines and primary button fill all #333333 (never pure black), a warm taupe #f7ecdd for one hero band, and terracotta #945c26 used only as a border accent; no gradients, no shadows, 0px radii.
nodes.why: Warm off-white with near-black ink reads as paper and keeps brown product bottles from looking muddy.
nodes.implementation: :root{--canvas:#fffef2;--ink:#333;--band:#f7ecdd;--accent:#945c26} border:1px solid var(--accent) on featured tiles only.
nodes.pitfalls: Too many warm tints become beige mush; limit to canvas, one band tint and one accent.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Generated palettes pick cool neutrals plus a saturated primary; a terracotta border-only accent is a specific craft decision.

nodes.name: Hard black/white inversion bands
nodes.what: Sections alternate between pure #000 and pure #fff (or #f6f8f7 off-white) with hard edges and no gradient; depth comes from the inversion and 2px white hairlines rather than shadows. Liquid Death drops a white contest block into a black page; TE alternates black and off-white product tiles; Analogue puts #eaeaea review cards on black.
nodes.why: Inversion creates rhythm and focus without any decorative layer.
nodes.implementation: section[data-theme=dark]{--bg:#000;--ink:#fff} body{background:var(--bg);color:var(--ink)} no box-shadow anywhere.
nodes.pitfalls: Inverting every other section becomes a zebra; use inversion for one or two key bands.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Generated dark modes are #0f172a-ish with glowing accents; true #000 next to true #fff with no shadow is deliberate.

nodes.name: No brand colour at all
nodes.what: The UI palette is only black, white and greys (#333333, #888888, #e8e8e8, #f4f4f4); every chromatic moment comes from product photography. Nothing, Polestar and Analogue follow the same rule; Polestar's own sources describe 'no chromatic brand voltage'.
nodes.why: A grey UI makes a red jacket or a green car the only colour on screen, so merchandise does the branding.
nodes.implementation: Define tokens only in neutral steps; buttons are black fill or 1px black outline; links underline instead of colour.
nodes.pitfalls: Without strong photography the page is just grey; this only works when imagery is excellent.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Generated palettes always include a primary accent; refusing one is a visible brand decision.

nodes.name: Each SKU owns a hue
nodes.what: Every product has its own saturated colour taken from its packaging, and the site uses that colour as the full-bleed background of its section, as section dividers and as accents on its product page; the illustration-led packaging (Danny Miller) sits on plain fields of that hue.
nodes.why: Colour becomes wayfinding: you can tell which product you are looking at from across the room.
nodes.implementation: Store hue per product; section{background:var(--sku-bg)} with color-mix(in oklch, var(--sku-bg) 85%, black) for the divider.
nodes.pitfalls: Adjacent sections in clashing hues need a neutral band or the page strobes.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Generated colour is global; per-product colour fields require a packaging system.

nodes.name: One hot colour, action only
nodes.what: A single saturated colour is reserved for prices and CTAs and nothing else: TE orange #ff6600 (hover #e65c00) on white/black; Eight Sleep's Pulse Blue #4158ee appears only on links, focus rings and selected states; Liquid Death's gold #d2ac5a only on special links.
nodes.why: When the accent appears in exactly one role, the eye learns it means 'act here'.
nodes.implementation: --action:#ff6600 used only on .price and button; focus-visible outline uses the same token.
nodes.pitfalls: The moment the accent is used in a heading or icon the rule breaks and it becomes a theme colour.
nodes.ai_tell_note: An accent colour is standard; restricting it to a single functional role is the discipline that reads as designed.
avoid_words: accent used in headings and icons

nodes.name: Flat grey stage behind product
nodes.what: Product renders and cutouts sit on a flat light-grey stage, not white: Polestar hero #efefef, TE product tiles #f6f8f7 with black labels, Liquid Death grid #e3e3e3 'ash' behind cans, Analogue #eaeaea cards on black. The stage has no gradient or vignette.
nodes.why: A grey stage separates the product silhouette from the page without a card border or shadow.
nodes.implementation: .stage{background:#efefef;aspect-ratio:16/10;display:grid;place-items:end center}.
nodes.pitfalls: Grey that is too dark muddies white products; stay between #eaeaea and #f6f8f7.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Generated product sections put the object on a glow or gradient; a flat grey rectangle is a studio convention.

nodes.name: Everything portrait 4:5 on white
nodes.what: Product cards are 4:5 model shots on a forced white background (Cloudinary ar_4:5, b_white, c_fill); Arc'teryx crops tiles to 600x800 and 496x590; category tiles use 2:3. No square product images appear anywhere.
nodes.why: A single tall ratio makes the grid read as a contact sheet and shows garments full length.
nodes.implementation: img{aspect-ratio:4/5;object-fit:cover;background:#fff} grid 4-up desktop, 2-up mobile.
nodes.pitfalls: Accessories look lost in 4:5; crop them tighter but keep the frame ratio.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Generated grids default to square or 16:9 thumbnails.

nodes.name: Low-quality blur-up placeholder
nodes.what: Every tile first loads a tiny blurred version of the same image (Sanity params blur=10, q=20) and swaps to the full crop; Bang & Olufsen uses inline SVG data URIs with fixed dimensions plus 1x1 GIFs so layout never shifts.
nodes.why: Blur-up keeps the grid's colour composition visible during load and prevents layout jumps.
nodes.implementation: ; or CSS @starting-style for the fade.
nodes.pitfalls: A blur that never resolves on slow networks is worse than a grey box; set a timeout fallback.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Generated drafts use shimmer skeletons; image-derived blur placeholders are production craft.

nodes.name: Front, back, 'Model wears' gallery
nodes.what: Each product card carries a labelled image sequence: studio shots 'from the front' and 'from the back', then on-model shots labelled 'Model wears…' with size and height; cards swap or thumb through these on hover. Satisfy loads front, back, side and detail views per card.
nodes.why: Labelling views answers the fit question on the grid instead of on the product page.
nodes.implementation: Images in a scroll-snap row inside the card; :hover shows image 2 via opacity; alt text carries the view label.
nodes.pitfalls: Hover swap on touch devices needs a tap-to-cycle fallback or dots.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Labelled view sequences are a merchandising discipline, not a component default.

nodes.name: App readout overlaid on lifestyle photo
nodes.what: Lifestyle photographs carry small UI mockups from the product app: a dual-zone temperature readout (64° left, 76° right), a hot/neutral/cold slider scaled W0–W30, a snoring overlay with a timestamp. Oura collages app screens (Daytime Stress, Symptom Radar) next to the ring.
nodes.why: Pairing the physical object with its data proves the product does something.
nodes.implementation: position:absolute readout with font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; 12px radius matching the app; anchor positioning to the photo region.
nodes.pitfalls: Overlays must use the real app type and corner radii or they look like stock widgets.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Floating UI cards are a known tell; the handmade version is a single precise readout anchored to the photo's subject.

nodes.name: Full-viewport photo bands, text at bottom
nodes.what: Each product is a full-viewport, edge-to-edge photo band with 16px horizontal padding and 0 radius; the text stack (category tag, 24px light headline, dot-matrix product name, body, muted description) sits at the bottom of the band. There are no editorial sections between bands.
nodes.why: The device photo is the layout; the text behaves like a caption.
nodes.implementation: section{min-height:100svh;display:grid;align-content:end;padding:16px} img as background via object-fit; scroll-snap-type: y proximity.
nodes.pitfalls: Six identical bands with centred text is monotonous; alternate text left/right and vary band height.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Full-bleed sections exist in templates, but bottom-anchored captions with no scrim and no card are the brand version.

nodes.name: Hairline grid, no gutters
nodes.what: Product and spec grids use 1px dividers instead of gaps: TE separates tiles with 1px #b2b2b2 lines and spec grids use repeat(auto-fit, minmax(200px,1fr)) with a 1px gap so the black background shows through as rules; Aesop cards get a 1px #333 border and 0 radius.
nodes.why: Rules instead of gutters make the grid feel like a printed table or a circuit board.
nodes.implementation: .grid{display:grid;gap:1px;background:#b2b2b2} .grid>*{background:#f6f8f7;padding:10px}.
nodes.pitfalls: Needs cells of equal height or the rules end unevenly; use grid, not flex.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Generated grids always use gap and rounded cards; 1px rules via background bleed is a classic designer trick.
avoid_words: card grid with 24px gaps and shadows

nodes.name: Zero radius, hairline, no shadow
nodes.what: Every button, input, tile and card has border-radius 0, separation is a 1px hairline (#333 on Aesop, 2px white on Liquid Death, #e5e7eb on Nothing), and no element has a box-shadow or gradient; buttons are 40–48px tall with 12–24px padding. Only avatar dots get 50%.
nodes.why: Square edges and hairlines read as print and stay out of the way of photography.
nodes.implementation: *{border-radius:0} button{height:48px;padding:13px 24px 12px;border:1px solid var(--ink)} :focus-visible{outline:2px solid var(--ink);outline-offset:2px}.
nodes.pitfalls: Square inputs need a visible focus style since there is no shadow; use a 2px offset outline.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Generated UI defaults to 8–16px radii with soft shadows; a global 0 radius is the most reliable anti-tell.

nodes.name: Plain text panel between product tiles
nodes.what: In the middle of the tile grid a full tile slot is given to text only: a two-sentence story about the Shanghai store ('museum-shop first floor, construction-site second floor') with a 'Read more' link, then the grid resumes. Hardholy opens its whole site with an essay and a Bachelard epigraph before any object.
nodes.why: A text slot in a visual grid acts like a magazine spread and slows the scroll.
nodes.implementation: grid-column: span 1; padding: 24px; max-width 36ch; same hairline border as image tiles.
nodes.pitfalls: More than one text tile per screen looks like missing images.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Generated grids fill every slot with an image or card; a text-only slot is a human editorial choice.

nodes.name: Stacked editorial modules, no grid
nodes.what: The homepage has no product grid at all: eight stacked modules, each one image with a headline, one line and one or two text links (Sidewinder jacket, Kragg shoe, Thorium hoody, resale, a film). Polestar similarly stacks model blocks with a price line and two CTAs.
nodes.why: One product per screen gives each item a billboard instead of a thumbnail.
nodes.implementation: <article> per module with grid-template-columns: 1fr 1fr and :nth-child(even) reversing order.
nodes.pitfalls: Eight identical modules need alternating image side and varying height to avoid monotony.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Generated homepages always include a product card grid; a grid-less home is a brand-led decision.

nodes.name: Press score tiles in a row
nodes.what: A horizontal row of flat tiles, each showing a publication name, a numeric score and a one-line quote (Gizmodo 4.5/5, Wired 9/10, IGN 8/10), on #eaeaea cards with 18px radius over a black band; Daylight does a plain logo row (The Verge, Wired, TechRadar, Daring Fireball) with no scores.
nodes.why: Numeric scores from named outlets are more credible than star widgets.
nodes.implementation: Row of <a> tiles in a scroll-snap flex; score at 32px tabular-nums; quote 14px; loop with a marquee only if more than six.
nodes.pitfalls: Mixed scales (4.5/5 vs 9/10) must be shown verbatim, never normalised.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Generated social proof is avatars and stars; scored press tiles are a hardware-launch convention.

nodes.name: Clinical stat cards linking to studies
nodes.what: Three stat cards each carry a percentage, a one-line claim and a link to the study: 'up to 44% less time to fall asleep', 'up to 34% more deep sleep', '32% average rise in sleep quality'; Sonos uses a single '4000+ patented innovations' callout; Oura leads with '86% of Members see their health improve' plus footnote.
nodes.why: A measured number with a source is the strongest form of product proof.
nodes.implementation: Card with <data value=44>44%</data> at 56px weight 300, claim 16px, <a> to study; no icons.
nodes.pitfalls: Numbers without 'up to' and a source are legal exposure; keep the qualifier.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Generated stat rows show fake '99% uptime' counters; linked clinical numbers are specific.

nodes.name: Specs as grouped plain lists
nodes.what: The spec section is a set of small grouped bullet lists under bold labels (Battery, CPU, Storage, Size, Included, Wireless, Sound, Display, Inputs, Cost) in body type, not a styled table; TE places specs below the render, never overlaid; Norma's comparison table marks its own column with the product's disc icon instead of a brand colour.
nodes.why: Plain grouped lists are scannable and look like a manual, which suits hardware.
nodes.implementation: <dl> per group in a grid of minmax(200px,1fr); dt bold 13px, dd 13px; tabular-nums.
nodes.pitfalls: Groups of more than six lines need a two-column layout or the list gets tall.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Generated spec sections use icon cards; a typographic list in groups is a print habit.

nodes.name: Category links with item counts
nodes.what: Category navigation shows the count: 'All Products 29, Sofas 13, Lounge Chairs 7, Footstools 9' with a one-line blurb each; Funner states '21 products made to be mixed'; Norma's preset cards show 'Deep work, 7 apps'.
nodes.why: Counts set expectations and make a small catalogue feel curated rather than thin.
nodes.implementation: Sofas 13 with the count in tabular-nums at 0.8em and muted ink.
nodes.pitfalls: Counts must be live; a hard-coded '13' that drifts looks careless.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Counts next to category names are a library/archive habit generated nav lacks.

nodes.name: Card: tag, name, benefit line, price
nodes.what: Each product card stacks a small category tag ('Fortifying + Balancing'), the product name, a one-line benefit ('Your dark spot routine, upgraded'), then price; Liquid Death adds a datum instead (calorie count 0/5/10/20 under each can); Norma adds 'n apps'.
nodes.why: One line of benefit or data turns a thumbnail into an argument.
nodes.implementation: Card grid; .tag 11px uppercase; .benefit 14px max 40ch with text-wrap: balance; price tabular-nums.
nodes.pitfalls: Benefit lines longer than ~40 characters wrap and break the grid rhythm.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Generated cards show name and price only; a datum line is merchandising copy.
avoid_words: card with rating stars and badge pile

nodes.name: Colourway swatches with '+2'
nodes.what: Cards list colourways as small text links or swatches and collapse extras into '+2'; Le Labo shows '+2 sizes' under the size label; Satisfy cards show size chips or 'One Size' and swatch thumbnails directly on the grid.
nodes.why: Shows range without cluttering the card, and the '+n' invites the click.
nodes.implementation: Show first 3 swatches (16px squares, 1px border) then +{n}; swap card image on swatch hover.
nodes.pitfalls: Swatches under 16px are untappable; use text names on mobile.
nodes.ai_tell_note: A '+2' overflow is a detail from real inventory handling.

nodes.name: Whole cell tappable, overlay on hover
nodes.what: The entire product cell is the link and hover reveals a text overlay: 'Buy Now' on Drop Edition cards, 'Explore Product' on Telepathic tiles; SSENSE makes the whole cell tappable with no visible button at all.
nodes.why: Removing buttons from the grid keeps it clean while hover still signals action.
nodes.implementation: a.cell{display:block} .overlay{opacity:0} a:hover .overlay{opacity:1} @media (pointer:coarse){.overlay{opacity:1;position:static}}.
nodes.pitfalls: Touch users never see hover; keep a visible text link in the card footer on coarse pointers.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Hover overlays are common in templates but usually with a dark gradient; a flat text overlay or no button at all is the restrained version.
avoid_words: card with visible Add to cart button

nodes.name: Sold out stays visible
nodes.what: Out-of-stock items stay in the grid with the button swapped to 'Notify Me' (Le Labo) or 'Get notified when restocked' (Topicals) or a disabled 'Sold out' chip per size (Satisfy); Analogue labels a collab 'Sold Out' and keeps it visible as archive.
nodes.why: Keeping sold-out items visible shows demand and captures intent.
nodes.implementation: button[data-state=soldout]{background:none;border:1px solid var(--ink)} text 'Notify me'; size chips with aria-disabled.
nodes.pitfalls: A grid that is mostly 'Sold out' reads as abandoned; cap visible sold-out items.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Generated catalogues never model stock state at all.

nodes.name: Arrow text link instead of button
nodes.what: Primary actions are text links with a trailing arrow and no fill or border: 'Discover the car →', 'Learn more →' stacked in the hero; Freitag prefixes uppercase CTAs with a '≥' glyph ('≥ DISCOVER NOW'); Acne uses '› Shop'.
nodes.why: A typographic arrow keeps the page flat and makes buttons feel unnecessary.
nodes.implementation: a.cta::after{content:' \2192'} or ::before{content:'\2265 '} ; padding:5px 0 1px; text-decoration:none; hover underline.
nodes.pitfalls: Arrow links need generous padding (5px 0 plus line-height) to remain tappable.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Generated heroes always ship two filled buttons; an arrow link pair is a strong anti-tell.

nodes.name: Empty cart written in brand voice
nodes.what: The empty cart drawer carries real copy: 'YOUR CART IS EMPTY. THAT'S A CRIME. SHOP NOW →' (Liquid Death); 'Oops, your cart is empty! Time to refill it with silhouettes that hit different.' with 'See Homepage' and 'Go to Shop' (Drop Edition); Satisfy and Telepathic use a 'Continue shopping' button pointing at new arrivals.
nodes.why: Empty states are read more than hero copy by returning shoppers and are a free place for personality.
nodes.implementation:
Cart drawer empty state:

in display size + one link to /new; no illustration needed.
nodes.pitfalls: Jokes wear thin on repeat visits; keep it one line.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Generated drafts leave empty states as the platform default text.

nodes.name: Rotating announcement strip with a pause
nodes.what: The thin announcement bar cycles three messages ('New In | Shop Now', 'Join the RCC', 'Bundle & Save') and exposes a visible 'Pause' control; Bang & Olufsen puts the same pause control on its hero rotation; Analogue runs a marquee ticker 'New! 3DOS V1.5.1 out now!'; Norma's strip holds a 48h countdown.
nodes.why: A pause control turns a marketing ticker into an accessible, honest component.
nodes.implementation: CSS @keyframes marquee with animation-play-state toggled by a button; prefers-reduced-motion sets it paused.
nodes.pitfalls: Cycling faster than ~5s is unreadable; and never put the only path to a promo in the ticker.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Promo bars are everywhere; the pause button and plain text (no emoji, no gradient) is what keeps it from reading as generated.

nodes.name: Newsletter asks preferences, promises cadence
nodes.what: The sign-up form asks for Menswear/Womenswear checkboxes and a Riding Style selector (Road & Gravel or Mountain) alongside the email; Framework labels its cadence 'Monthly-ish' and 'a few times a month'; Daylight promises 'No spam'; TE heads its overlay 'hold on...' with 'surprise' copy.
nodes.why: Stating cadence and asking a preference makes the form a conversation rather than a capture.
nodes.implementation: Email input + two checkboxes + one <select>; label copy 'Monthly-ish'; inline success state, no modal.
nodes.pitfalls: More than two preference questions turns it into a survey.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Generated newsletter blocks are 'Subscribe to our newsletter' with one input.

nodes.name: Country switch warns about the bag
nodes.what: Changing country opens a modal that says the shopping bag will be emptied, with Continue/Cancel; Satisfy's 'Change Country?' modal groups regions (North America, Europe, Asia Pacific…) with currency codes and warns of a full page refresh; Eight Sleep's region modal is 560px wide with a blue checkmark on the selected row.
nodes.why: Being explicit about the consequence of a locale switch prevents the most common lost-cart complaint.
nodes.implementation: <dialog> with grouped <optgroup> list; warning paragraph; remember choice in localStorage.
nodes.pitfalls: A region modal on every visit is hostile; show once and remember.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Locale consequence copy is operational knowledge generated drafts skip.

nodes.name: Inputs as a single underline
nodes.what: Text inputs have no box: a 1px bottom hairline only (#aeaeae on Analogue's newsletter, #e5e5e5 on Polestar at 44px height, #ececec on Eight Sleep with a 2px #4158ee focus outline), transparent fill and 12px vertical padding.
nodes.why: An underline input sits inside typography instead of interrupting it with a box.
nodes.implementation: input{border:0;border-bottom:1px solid var(--hair);background:none;height:44px;padding:12px 0} :focus-visible{outline:2px solid var(--action);outline-offset:2px}.
nodes.pitfalls: Underline inputs need a visible label; placeholder-only fails once typed.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Generated forms use boxed inputs with 8px radius; underline-only is a typographic choice.
avoid_words: rounded filled inputs with inner shadow

nodes.name: Hover: image scales 1.04 in 200ms
nodes.what: On hover the product image scales from 1.0 to 1.04 over 200ms with cubic-bezier(0.4,0,0.2,1); the card itself does not lift or gain a shadow. Other cards swap to the second image (Jakobsen stacks two overlapping photos per card for this).
nodes.why: A small zoom inside a fixed frame signals interactivity without changing layout.
nodes.implementation: .frame{overflow:hidden} img{transition:transform 200ms cubic-bezier(.4,0,.2,1)} a:hover img{transform:scale(1.04)}.
nodes.pitfalls: Scale on a non-overflow-hidden frame causes layout bleed; clip the frame.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Hover zoom is common; the tell is lifting the card with a shadow, so keep the frame fixed.
avoid_words: card lift with shadow on hover

nodes.name: Cards tilt, illustrations wiggle
nodes.what: Product cards tilt a few degrees on hover, and hand-drawn SVG illustrations used as UI elements have a subtle JavaScript wiggle; buttons carry the retro offset shadow so the whole page moves like paper cutouts.
nodes.why: Small, imperfect motion matches a hand-illustrated brand better than easing curves.
nodes.implementation: a:hover .card{transform:rotate(-2deg)} @keyframes wiggle{to{transform:rotate(1.5deg)}} alternate 180ms, honouring prefers-reduced-motion.
nodes.pitfalls: Continuous wiggle is distracting; trigger it on hover or at most every few seconds.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Generated motion is fade-up on scroll; tilt and wiggle on illustrations is a character choice.

nodes.name: Horizontal strip of tall narrow tiles
nodes.what: A section scrolls horizontally through about a dozen tall, narrow artwork tiles (Sonos Radio stations) between normal vertical sections; Daylight names its assets 'h-scroll-vision'; On's category and story rows use Previous/Next plus skip-forward controls rather than dots.
nodes.why: A horizontal pocket inside a vertical page changes pace and suits many same-size items.
nodes.implementation: ul{display:flex;overflow-x:auto;scroll-snap-type:x mandatory;gap:12px} li{flex:0 0 140px;aspect-ratio:9/16;scroll-snap-align:start}.
nodes.pitfalls: Must stay a native scroller with visible overflow at the edge; hijacking the wheel is the failure mode.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Horizontal scrolling is in templates but usually hijacked; native scroll-snap with tall tiles is the restrained form.

nodes.name: Footer stays light with a hairline
nodes.what: The footer does not invert to dark: same canvas as the page, a 1px top border (#333333), 40px top padding, four link columns at 14px uppercase with links at weight 100 (SSENSE) or 18px bold heads (Aesop), and about five columns on Bottega. Polestar is the counterexample with #1a1a1a.
nodes.why: A light footer ends the page like the last sheet of a catalogue instead of a dark block.
nodes.implementation: footer{border-top:1px solid var(--ink);padding:40px 0 30px;display:grid;grid-template-columns:repeat(4,1fr)}.
nodes.pitfalls: Without the hairline the footer bleeds into the last section; keep the 1px rule.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Generated footers are dark slabs; a light hairline footer is an editorial decision.

nodes.name: Footer address and maker credits
nodes.what: The footer ends with a physical address and credits: Panic prints its Portland street address and phone; TE prints its Stockholm address; Hardholy credits 'Design by Atelier Dyakova, build by Cliff Studio'; Telepathic signs 'Made with Love And Money'; Daylight states 'A more caring computer company' and its public-benefit status.
nodes.why: An address and named makers prove a real company and a real design team stand behind the shop.
nodes.implementation: <address> element at 12px in the footer's last row; credits as plain links.
nodes.pitfalls: Credits in a larger size than the legal line look like an ad; keep them 11–12px.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Generated footers never include a street address or a design credit.

nodes.name: Lowercase run-on manifesto band
nodes.what: A textured full-width band carries one long lowercase sentence as a tagline: 'american heritage remixed with streetwear elements, oversized silhouettes, and feminine touches.'; UND stacks a lyrical headline in four short lines ('Sandwiched / Special, / Something / Starts.'); TE breaks product copy into poem-like short lines.
nodes.why: Lowercase and manual line breaks make copy sound like a note from the founder.
nodes.implementation:
p.manifesto{text-transform:lowercase;font-size:clamp(1.5rem,4vw,3rem);max-width:28ch;text-wrap:pretty} use
deliberately.
nodes.pitfalls: Run-ons longer than two lines on mobile lose the reader.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Generated taglines are title-case triads; lowercase manifestos with hand line breaks are voice.
