nodes.name: Deadpan or off-script button labels
nodes.what: Buttons say things other than Shop Now: 'HELL YES', 'JOIN THE CONTEST', 'MURDER YOUR THIRST' (Liquid Death); 'Shop Now_!!_' and 'Notify Me_!_' with underscore emphasis (Playdate); 'agree!' as the product CTA (TE); 'Begin a Conversation' (Jakobsen); 'Tap in' (Topicals).
nodes.why: A button in the brand's voice is read as copy, not chrome.
nodes.implementation: Content rule; keep button height and case consistent so the voice, not the styling, carries it.
nodes.pitfalls: Ambiguous labels hurt checkout; keep the literal verb for cart and pay buttons.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Generated CTAs are 'Get Started' and 'Learn More' in every draft.

nodes.name: Separate mobile crop per banner
nodes.what: Every hero and campaign banner ships two art-directed assets: a 2624x1300 desktop image and a 1200x1500 portrait mobile crop (Liquid Death), 5120px vs 2517px (Satisfy), 'hero6' vs 'hero6-m' (Drop Edition), 2:1 vs 1:1 (Freitag). The mobile asset reframes the subject, not just resizes.
nodes.why: Art-directed portrait crops make mobile the primary canvas rather than a squeezed desktop.
nodes.implementation: with matching width/height to avoid CLS.
nodes.pitfalls: Two assets per slot doubles production; reserve for heroes and campaign tiles.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Generated drafts use one image with object-fit; two deliberate crops are production craft.

nodes.name: Fixed bottom buy bar, mobile
nodes.what: On the product page a slim bar fixed to the bottom of the viewport holds the price and 'Add to bag' once the main buy module scrolls away; ETQ Amsterdam's version (by Build in Amsterdam, on Shopify) is a clean minimal strip tagged 'add to bag' and 'product photography'.
nodes.why: Keeps the one action reachable by thumb without a sticky column, which does not exist on mobile.
nodes.implementation: position:sticky;bottom:0 on the buy row; or IntersectionObserver toggles a fixed bar; padding-bottom:env(safe-area-inset-bottom).
nodes.pitfalls: Bar plus cookie banner plus chat bubble eats the screen; reserve the bottom edge for the bar only.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Sticky CTAs are standard; the restraint (price + one button, hairline top, no shadow) is what reads as designed.
avoid_words: full-screen sticky header plus bottom bar together

nodes.name: Bento grid feature tiles
nodes.what: A mixed-size rounded-card grid where each tile holds an icon, a short title and a line of copy; often with a 1-2-1 span rhythm and 16–24px radii.
nodes.why: It fills space quickly and looks organised, which is exactly why generators reach for it.
nodes.implementation: Do not build; use hairline-grid-no-gutters or full-bleed-photo-bands instead.
nodes.pitfalls: Reads as a template within seconds; none of the 30-plus commerce sites opened for this file use one.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Bento grids with icons are the single most recognised AI layout tell of 2024–2026; none of the surveyed stores use them.

nodes.name: Monospace eyebrow labels
nodes.what: Section eyebrows and small labels are set in a monospace face (Geist Mono, IBM Plex Mono, ABC Favorit Mono) at 11-12px, uppercase, +0.1em tracking, instead of a tracked sans-serif caption. Neon's extraction shows 'eyebrow-mono 12px/500/0.1em uppercase GeistMono'; Vercel uses GeistMono for 12px captions and 'no uppercase-tracked sans labels'; Arc uses ABC Favorit Mono eyebrows at 12px with 0.6-1.8px tracking.
nodes.why: It signals 'technical' with one glyph change and gives hierarchy without a second sans weight.
nodes.implementation: font-family: 'Geist Mono', ui-monospace; font-size:12px; letter-spacing:.1em; text-transform:uppercase; font-feature-settings:'tnum';
nodes.pitfalls: Using mono for body or titles turns the page into a wall of code; keep it to 11-13px labels.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Default generators reach for a tracked Inter caption; a mono eyebrow is a deliberate swap.

nodes.name: Light display, heavy negative tracking
nodes.what: Hero headlines are enormous but set at weight 400 (never bold) and pulled in with -2.5% to -4% letter-spacing: Vercel 128px/400/-3.2px, Neon 80px/400/-3.2px, Cursor 72px/400/-2.16px, Warp 64px/400/-1.6px, Mistral 84px/400/-1.5px. Tracking scales toward 0 by body size (Linear: -3.0px at 80px to -0.05px at 16px).
nodes.why: Size and tracking carry the hierarchy so the type reads engineered rather than shouted.
nodes.implementation: h1{font-weight:400;font-size:clamp(48px,8vw,128px);letter-spacing:-0.035em;line-height:1;text-wrap:balance}
nodes.pitfalls: At weight 400 the headline needs 1.0-1.1 line-height and a tight measure or it dissolves; never apply the tracking below 24px.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Generated drafts default to 700-weight Inter with normal tracking.

nodes.name: Editorial serif display, sans body
nodes.what: A high-contrast editorial serif is used only for display: Resend's Domaine Display Narrow at 96/96 with -0.96px tracking and ss01/ss04/ss11 enabled, Granola's Quadrant 68px/400, Mistral's PP Editorial Old 84px/400, Craft's Untitled Serif 66px/-1.98px. Body, UI and buttons stay sans (Favorit/Inter/Melange). Resend's own rule: 'Never use the Domaine font in bold'.
nodes.why: The serif supplies warmth and authority that a grotesk hero cannot, while the sans keeps the product feeling like software.
nodes.implementation: h1{font-family:'Domaine Display Narrow',Georgia,serif;font-weight:400;letter-spacing:-.01em} body,button{font-family:Inter,sans-serif}
nodes.pitfalls: The serif-italic single accent word (Instrument Serif) is now itself a tell; use the serif for whole headlines at weight 400, never one italic word.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Serif+sans pairing is spreading fast; it stays distinctive only with a specific, narrow or old-style face and strict display-only use.

nodes.name: Large serif body text
nodes.what: Anthropic sets running marketing copy in a serif at 24px/1.4 (body-lg) and 18px/1.5, with display headings in the same serif at weight 400 and a sans only for UI and labels. Reading columns are held to roughly 640-720px.
nodes.why: Reversing the usual roles (serif for reading, sans for chrome) makes the page feel like a journal rather than a dashboard.
nodes.implementation: p{font-family:'Tiempos Text',Georgia,serif;font-size:24px;line-height:1.4;max-width:34em}
nodes.pitfalls: Serif at 24px needs a narrow measure and generous leading; in a wide container it looks like a mistake.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Generated pages almost never put body copy in a large serif.

nodes.name: One font size, man-page hierarchy
nodes.what: PlanetScale's 2025 site uses a single font size in a monospace stack, like a terminal man page. Hierarchy comes only from greys, weight and underlines on h1-h3, plus an orange bar anchoring each h1. Solid rules mark the hero logo grid; dashed rules mark the footer as secondary. No screenshots, shadows or animation.
nodes.why: Removing the type scale forces structure into colour, rules and spacing, which reads as serious and engineering-led.
nodes.implementation: html{font:15px/1.6 'Berkeley Mono',ui-monospace} h1,h2,h3{font-size:inherit} h1{border-left:3px solid #f26b1d;padding-left:.75rem} h3{text-decoration:underline;color:#888}
nodes.pitfalls: Monospace is wide, so sidebars must be narrow and line lengths balloon at wide breakpoints; cap the measure.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Directly opposed to the generated default of a 6-step type scale.

nodes.name: One OpenType feature as signature
nodes.what: The brand is carried by a stylistic set rather than a custom font: Raycast enables Inter ss03 (single-story g) plus calt/kern/liga site-wide, 'without it the site looks like generic Inter'; Resend turns on Domaine ss01, ss04, ss11 for display; Warp's extraction notes slashed zeros (zero, tnum) in Hack terminal text.
nodes.why: A single alternate glyph makes a ubiquitous font feel proprietary at zero licensing cost.
nodes.implementation: body{font-feature-settings:'calt','kern','liga','ss03'} code{font-feature-settings:'zero','tnum'}
nodes.pitfalls: Enabling many sets at once (ss01-ss08) reads as noise; pick one and apply it globally.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Generated CSS never touches font-feature-settings.

nodes.name: Commission or pick an unseen grotesk
nodes.what: Top products run a single proprietary family across display and UI: OpenAI Sans (built with ABC Dinamo from a 'black dot', round O), Cursor Gothic, Linear Display/Text/Mono, Perplexity's pplxSans (weights held to 400-500, 'Don't bold weight beyond 500'), PostHog's RoundHog. One family, few weights, no second sans.
nodes.why: A face nobody else uses is the cheapest durable differentiator a product site has.
nodes.implementation: Choose a grotesk with a visible 'tell' (round O, single-story a/g); limit to 2-3 weights; @font-face with font-display:swap.
nodes.pitfalls: A quirky grotesk with no weights below 400 or no tabular figures fails in dashboards; check numerals first.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Inter/Geist/system-ui is the generated default; an unusual grotesk breaks the pattern instantly.

nodes.name: Highlighter marks on action verbs
nodes.what: Granola draws a yellow highlighter (#febe29, 4px radius, 2x4px padding) behind single verbs in headlines. Rules recorded: verbs only, never more than one per sentence, never as a full-bleed background. The second 'voltage' colour (olive #5b6f00) is reserved for the CTA.
nodes.why: It mimics a pen on paper, matching a note-taking product, and gives emphasis without bold or italic.
nodes.implementation: mark{background:#febe29;border-radius:4px;padding:2px 4px;box-decoration-break:clone}
nodes.pitfalls: More than one mark per sentence turns into a wall of yellow; keep it to one verb.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Generated emphasis is gradient text or bold; a scoped highlighter is handmade.

nodes.name: All-lowercase copy system
nodes.what: Entire sites written in lowercase: Warp's 2026 site ('request early access', 'download warp terminal', lowercase eyebrows like 'governance'), Inngest's hero 'make every / backend / unbreakable.', Midday's lowercase wordmark. Paired with mono labels and terminal glyphs ('>_', '⌗').
nodes.why: Lowercase reads like a prompt or a shell, which suits agent and terminal products and quietly rejects marketing tone.
nodes.implementation: text-transform:lowercase on headings only; write body in lowercase by hand; keep brand nouns intact.
nodes.pitfalls: Lowercase product names and acronyms (api, aws) look wrong; whitelist proper nouns.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Generated copy is Title Case or sentence case with exclamation energy.

nodes.name: Declarative headlines ending in a period
nodes.what: Headlines are short sentences closed with a full stop: Vercel's 'sentence case and end with a period' rule, Attio 'Free your reps to sell.', Mistral 'We host it. Or you do.', Convex 'Solved.', Antimetal 'Production that runs itself.'.
nodes.why: The period turns a slogan into a statement of fact and sets a calm, confident cadence.
nodes.implementation: Editorial rule, no CSS.
nodes.pitfalls: Combined with 'Unlock', 'Supercharge' or 'Seamless' it becomes the AI slogan with a dot; keep verbs plain.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Generated headlines rarely use terminal punctuation.

nodes.name: Heading that continues on line two
nodes.what: Polar sets every section heading as a bold title line followed by a second line that finishes the thought, e.g. 'Every token becomes revenue / the moment your model streams it.' Warp uses a two-line heading with an underline-style rule beneath; Craft forces line breaks ('Craft isn't just for one thing, / it's for your things.').
nodes.why: The enforced break gives rhythm and lets a long claim keep display size.
nodes.implementation: h2{max-width:22ch;text-wrap:balance} h2 span.lead{display:block;font-weight:600} h2 span.tail{display:block;color:var(--muted)}
nodes.pitfalls:
Hard
breaks collapse badly on mobile; use text-wrap:balance and a max-width instead of forced breaks below 600px.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Generated headings are single centred lines.

nodes.name: Bracketed 'fig.' captions on visuals
nodes.what: Warp labels its hero diagram '[ fig. 1 — the factory ]' and sections carry 'fig.' numbering, with a status legend under the figure like a paper or datasheet. PlanetScale pairs an italic caption under its latency chart.
nodes.why: It frames product visuals as evidence rather than decoration.
nodes.implementation: figcaption{font:12px ui-monospace;color:var(--muted)} figcaption::before{content:'[ '} figcaption::after{content:' ]'} figure{counter-increment:fig}
nodes.pitfalls: Numbering figures that are not diagrams (a testimonial as fig. 4) feels precious.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Generated drafts never caption imagery.

nodes.name: Strict UI microcopy ruleset
nodes.what: Liveblocks' published design.md codifies product copy: sentence case everywhere; buttons are verb+noun ('Create project', never 'OK'); toasts name the changed item, have no trailing period and never say 'successfully'; in-progress labels use the participle plus an ellipsis ('Saving…'); numerals for counts ('3 projects'); curly quotes; no 'please', superlatives or apologies.
nodes.why: Consistent microcopy is one of the strongest signals of a hand-built product.
nodes.implementation: Copy guideline; enforce via a review checklist or a lint on string literals.
nodes.pitfalls: Rules drift if not linted; encode them in a copy checklist.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Generated UI copy uses 'Successfully created!' and Title Case buttons.

nodes.name: Ink-only CTA, brand colour withheld
nodes.what: The primary button is pure ink, not the brand colour: Vercel's CTA is black with brand blue 'declared in CSS but unrendered above the fold'; Raycast's one white pill on #07080a; Resend's '#fcfdff pill with #000000 text, the brightest pixel on every viewport'; Polar 'refuses to render its declared brand color'; Craft's single black pill; OpenAI's black pill.
nodes.why: The CTA wins by being the highest-contrast element, so colour can be saved for meaning.
nodes.implementation: .btn-primary{background:#000;color:#fff;border-radius:999px;height:40px;padding:0 20px} @media(prefers-color-scheme:dark){.btn-primary{background:#fff;color:#000}}
nodes.pitfalls: On a grey canvas a black button needs a white or cream field behind it or it disappears.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Generated CTAs are always the brand colour with a hover darkening.

nodes.name: One accent rationed to three jobs
nodes.what: A single chromatic colour appears only in named places: Neon green 'rationed to the logo, the EARLY-ACCESS pills, code-syntax' with the rule 'Don't fill the primary CTA with green'; Cursor orange #f54e00 used 'scarcely' on CTA and wordmark; Perplexity teal reserved for Sign In and focus rings; Linear's #5e6ad2 on the mark, focus ring and one CTA per section.
nodes.why: Scarcity makes the accent read as a signal, not a theme.
nodes.implementation: Define --accent once; allow it on at most three selectors (logo, focus ring, one badge); lint everything else to currentColor.
nodes.pitfalls: Rationing fails if icons are tinted with the accent; keep icons ink.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Generated themes colour buttons, links, icons and cards with the same accent.

nodes.name: Two shades, two jobs
nodes.what: Neon uses #34d59a for type (code keywords, link text) and a brighter #00e599 strictly for data visualisation (graph spikes), with #39a57d for hover on light panels. Light panels are tinted mint #e4f1eb instead of white so the page never leaves the green family.
nodes.why: Separating 'text green' from 'chart green' keeps charts vivid without making links glow.
nodes.implementation: :root{--accent-text:#34d59a;--accent-data:#00e599;--accent-press:#39a57d;--panel-light:#e4f1eb}
nodes.pitfalls: Three or more shades of the accent re-creates the gradient-brand look.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Generated palettes use one accent token everywhere.

nodes.name: Warm cream canvas instead of white
nodes.what: Light sites avoid #fff: Cursor #f7f7f4 with ink #26251e ('warm near-black'), Anthropic #faf9f5/#141413, Arc #fffcec, Granola #f7f7f2 (white kept for raised tiles only), PostHog #eeefe9, Craft #fcf9f7, Perplexity #fdfbfa. Hairlines are warm too (#e6e5e0, #d1cfc5).
nodes.why: Tinted paper lowers glare and makes product screenshots the whitest thing on the page.
nodes.implementation: :root{--canvas:#f7f7f4;--ink:#26251e;--hair:#e6e5e0;--muted:#807d72} body{background:var(--canvas);color:var(--ink)}
nodes.pitfalls: Cool grey hairlines (#e5e7eb) on a warm canvas look dirty; tint every neutral the same direction.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Cream is spreading quickly in 2025-26 AI sites; stays distinctive only with warm ink and warm hairlines, not Tailwind greys.

nodes.name: Brown-tinted dark mode
nodes.what: Warp's dark canvas is #2b2622 (oklch(22% 0.004 84.6)), cards #383330, hairline #3f3a36, body text #c9c0ad, with off-white #f7f5f0 as the only 'voltage'. No chromatic accent: 'The brown-beige tint IS the brand'.
nodes.why: A warm dark surface separates the product from the sea of blue-black dev sites with no accent colour at all.
nodes.pitfalls: Brown darks need text at 80-90% opacity in a warm off-white; pure white text turns it muddy.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Generated dark modes are #0a0a0a or slate-900.

nodes.name: Surface ladder and hairlines, zero shadows
nodes.what: Depth comes from 3-4 stacked surface tones plus 1px hairlines, never box-shadow: Linear canvas #010102 → #0f1011 → #141516 → #18191a with hairlines #23252a/#34343a/#3e3e44; Raycast #07080a→#0d0d0d→#101111→#121212; Resend hairlines at rgba(255,255,255,.06) and .14; Cursor light 'No drop shadows anywhere'; Vercel's Geist guidance 'draw each border once'.
nodes.why: Flat tonal layering looks precise at any zoom and never produces muddy shadow halos.
nodes.implementation: :root{--s0:#010102;--s1:#0f1011;--s2:#141516;--s3:#18191a;--h1:#23252a} .card{background:var(--s1);border:1px solid var(--h1);box-shadow:none}
nodes.pitfalls: Without shadows, nested cards need alternating tones or they merge; never put same-tone card inside card.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Generated cards get shadow-lg and a border; a strict no-shadow ladder is a conscious choice.

nodes.name: Ten-step role-named colour scale
nodes.what: Vercel's Geist publishes 10 scales (gray, gray-alpha, blue, red, amber, green, teal, purple, pink + backgrounds), each with 10 steps whose roles are fixed: 100 bg, 200 hover bg, 300 active bg, 400 border, 500 hover border, 600 active border, 700 high-contrast bg, 800 its hover, 900 secondary text, 1000 primary text. Alpha variants only 'when the background should show through'. P3 on capable displays.
nodes.why: Role-by-step removes per-component colour decisions and keeps every hue at matching contrast.
nodes.implementation: --ds-gray-100..1000 via oklch(l c h); use 400 for borders, 900/1000 for text; @media (color-gamut:p3){ use color(display-p3 …) }
nodes.pitfalls: Copying the numbers without the roles produces random mid-steps on text; map roles first.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Generated palettes are Tailwind 50-950 with no role contract.

nodes.name: Theme generated from three LCH inputs
nodes.what: Linear rebuilt theming so every theme derives from base colour, accent colour and a contrast number (compared at 30 vs 100), replacing 98 variables per theme. Colours are manipulated in LCH ('perpetually uniform') and converted to RGB at the end; surfaces and elevations (panels, dialogs) are LCH offsets; chrome blue was clamped for a more neutral look; text darkened in light mode and lightened in dark mode.
nodes.why: Three inputs guarantee any user theme has consistent elevation and legible contrast.
nodes.implementation: :root{--base:oklch(18% .01 260);--accent:oklch(60% .15 275);--contrast:.6} .panel{background:oklch(from var(--base) calc(l + .06*var(--contrast)) c h)} (relative colour syntax, @property)
nodes.pitfalls: Pure LCH can push out-of-gamut; clamp chroma or use oklch with gamut mapping.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Generated themes hard-code hex per variable.

nodes.name: Syntax tokens as the only colour
nodes.what: On otherwise monochrome pages the brightest colours live inside code: Neon's Shiki tokens keyword #34d59a, parameter #ff990a, string #ffed9c on black; Warp's terminal accents prompt #a78bfa, success #86efac, error #fca5a5, warning #fde047 with lime #c2ff00 'only inside terminal screenshots'; Cursor's JetBrains Mono surfaces cover 'roughly half the page'.
nodes.why: Colour appears where developers expect it, so the chrome can stay grey.
nodes.implementation: Shiki/Prism theme with 3-4 token colours matched to --accent; pre{background:#000;border:1px solid #303236;border-radius:4px}
nodes.pitfalls: A rainbow Dracula theme in the hero undoes the restraint; limit to 3-4 token colours.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Generated code blocks use default Prism themes; curating 3 token colours to match brand is handmade.

nodes.name: Accents only as low-opacity radial washes
nodes.what: Resend never paints accent colours as solid surfaces; they exist as radial glows at 18-34% alpha (orange rgba(255,89,0,.22), blue rgba(0,117,255,.34), green rgba(34,255,153,.18), red rgba(255,32,71,.34)) behind sections, plus a 'rainbow border' linear-gradient(90deg, rgba(2,252,239,.44), rgba(255,181,43,.44), rgba(160,43,254,.44)) and a noise.png texture.
nodes.why: Colour as atmosphere keeps the dark page alive without competing with the white CTA.
nodes.implementation: .section{background:radial-gradient(60% 40% at 80% 0%,rgba(0,117,255,.34),transparent 70%),#000}
nodes.pitfalls: Centre-screen purple/blue blobs behind the hero are the AI tell; keep washes off-centre, single-hue per section, under 35% alpha.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Glows are a tell when centred, saturated and multi-colour; Resend's are faint, single-hue and anchored to section edges.

nodes.name: Opacity tiers instead of greys
nodes.what: PostHog's handbook sets paragraph text at 90% opacity, links at 95%, links on hover at 100% rather than minting new grey tokens. Resend's design.md does the same on dark: body rgba(252,253,255,.86), charcoal .7; Raycast on-dark-mute rgba(255,255,255,.72).
nodes.why: Opacity tiers stay correct on any background tint, so one ink works on cream and on dark.
nodes.implementation: p{color:color-mix(in oklab,var(--ink) 86%,transparent)} a{color:color-mix(in oklab,var(--ink) 95%,transparent)} a:hover{color:var(--ink)}
nodes.pitfalls: Opacity text over images or mixed surfaces changes colour unpredictably; use color-mix for fixed cases.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Generated systems use gray-500/600/700 tokens.

nodes.name: Cream and black full-bleed band alternation
nodes.what: Anthropic divides the page with alternating cream (#faf9f5) and pure black (#000) full-bleed bands; black bands carry 'cinematic' illustrations full width while cream bands hold a 640-720px reading column. No gradients, no shadows, borders #e3dacc.
nodes.why: Polarity flips do the sectioning work that dividers and cards usually do.
nodes.implementation: .band{padding:96px 0} .band--ink{background:#000;color:#faf9f5} .band--paper{background:#faf9f5;color:#141413}
nodes.pitfalls: More than three flips per page feels like a slideshow; two or three with long cream stretches between.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Generated pages alternate white and grey-50 sections, not black and cream.

nodes.name: Featured card inverts polarity
nodes.what: On light pages the highlighted pricing tier or feature card flips to the dark ink surface: Vercel's 'pricing featured card inverts to the dark ink surface'; Supabase's featured tier and code blocks are the only dark surfaces (#1c1c1c) on a white page; Cursor's IDE panes are the dark islands in cream.
nodes.why: One inverted card is louder than any accent border and costs no colour.
nodes.implementation: .tier--featured{background:#171717;color:#fff} .tier--featured .btn{background:#fff;color:#000}
nodes.pitfalls: Two inverted cards cancel each other; exactly one per row.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Generated 'Most popular' tiers use a coloured border and badge.

nodes.name: One full-bleed brand band
nodes.what: Arc's site uses brand blue (#3139fb) exactly once as a full-bleed press-quote band with 72px vertical padding; the blue never fills a button. Mistral runs a thin 'sunset stripe' gradient (#fa520f → #ffa110 → #ffd900 → #fff8e0, 20px padding) directly above the footer on every page.
nodes.why: A single saturated band gives the page a memorable moment while the rest stays paper.
nodes.implementation: .band-brand{background:#3139fb;color:#fffcec;padding:72px 0} .prefooter{height:48px;background:linear-gradient(90deg,#fa520f,#ffa110,#ffd900,#fff8e0)}
nodes.pitfalls: Making the band the hero turns it into a coloured header; put it mid-page or pre-footer.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Generated layouts colour the hero and leave the rest white.

nodes.name: Numbered 01-05 section system with anchors
nodes.what: Sections are numbered as a system rather than steps: Polar's five feature sections carry eyebrows 01-05 with a two-line heading each; Sanity's 'Everything your team needs' is a 01-05 list with anchor links and a four-image grid per item; Antimetal 01-04; Warp's feature cards 01-06 and 'layer 01-04' stack.
nodes.why: Numbers make a long page scannable and imply a complete, finite system.
nodes.implementation: 01… ; nav.index a[href='#meter']; counter-reset:sec; .eyebrow::before{content:counter(sec,decimal-leading-zero)}
nodes.pitfalls: Numbering three generic benefit cards is the AI 'how it works' pattern; numbers earn their place only with five-plus real sections and anchor navigation.
nodes.ai_tell_note: '01 02 03' over three icon cards is now a tell; it reads handmade when it indexes a long page with a sticky anchor list.

nodes.name: Website as a 1990s operating system
nodes.what: PostHog's September 2025 site renders as a desktop OS: pages open as draggable windows (several at once), window snapping, keyboard shortcuts, a bookmark app, a Windows-Explorer clone for the merch store, Outlook-Express-style forums and PowerPoint-style product pages. Credits cite Apple and Microsoft 1995-1998. Motivation: tab overload and 'what if we just made better ways to consume content?'
nodes.why: Turning navigation into a metaphor users already know makes a huge site feel like one place.
nodes.implementation: .window{border:1px solid #000;box-shadow:4px 4px 0 #000;resize:both;overflow:auto} titlebar via position:sticky; popover + anchor positioning for menus.
nodes.pitfalls: Breaks native browser behaviours (back button, find, reader mode); provide plain URL fallbacks and respect reduced motion.
nodes.ai_tell_note: No generator produces a window manager; even a single draggable 'window' card reads handmade.

nodes.name: Marketing cards shaped like product
nodes.what: Raycast's site reuses the command-palette geometry: rows at 6px radius, keycaps at 4px with #121212→#0d0d0d gradient, 16px mockup containers, so 'the marketing page is the product'. Campsite reproduces its sidebar lists as cards; Linear frames screenshots in 16px panels with 12px cards and nothing else.
nodes.why: Visitors learn the product's shapes before they install it.
nodes.implementation: Build feature cards with the same tokens as the app (row height 36px, radius 6px, hairline) rather than a marketing card component.
nodes.pitfalls: If the product UI is weak the page inherits it; mock only the best screens.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Generated feature cards are icon+title+text; product-shaped cards are specific.

nodes.name: Bracketed key-letter section index
nodes.what: Warp's 2026 homepage has a secondary index where each section is prefixed with a bracketed shortcut letter: '[C] Configuration', '[S] SDLC', '[Q] Quality loop', and pressing the key jumps there. Lazy's CTA reads '⌘ Get started with Lazy now'.
nodes.why: It advertises keyboard-first culture and doubles as a table of contents.
nodes.implementation: C configuration… ; keydown listener ignoring inputs; kbd{font:11px ui-monospace;border:1px solid var(--hair);padding:0 4px;border-radius:3px}
nodes.pitfalls: Hijacking single letters breaks find-as-you-type and screen readers; bind only when no input is focused and show the hint.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Generated navs are text links; a key-letter index is a deliberate device.

nodes.name: Binary radius: pill press, sharp read
nodes.what: Interactive elements are fully rounded while containers are nearly square, with no middle tier: Vercel's '5.6px sm is rare' with 100px marketing pills and 0px pillar cards ('the two scales never mix on the same screen'); OpenAI 6px cards vs 40px/9999px input and chips; Perplexity 'Pill as press, container as read'; Polar fully rounded buttons on sharp surfaces.
nodes.why: Shape alone tells users what is pressable.
nodes.implementation: :root{--r-press:999px;--r-read:4px} button,.chip{border-radius:var(--r-press)} .card,input{border-radius:var(--r-read)}
nodes.pitfalls: A 12px-radius card next to a pill button is the generated default; remove the middle value entirely.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Generated UIs use rounded-xl everywhere.

nodes.name: 4px radius technical voice
nodes.what: Neon resolves '63 of 73 captured radius events' to 4px, buttons included; Warp uses 3-4px on buttons and 4-6px on cards with only icon containers round; Sanity's 'sharp, technical grids'. Pills are reserved for GeistMono chips.
nodes.why: Near-square corners read as engineered and let 1px hairlines stay crisp.
nodes.implementation: :root{--radius:4px} *{border-radius:var(--radius)} .chip{border-radius:999px;font-family:ui-monospace}
nodes.pitfalls: 4px with soft shadows looks like Bootstrap; pair with hairlines and no shadows.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Generated defaults are 8-16px.

nodes.name: Accent button with near-black text
nodes.what: Supabase pairs its emerald #3ecf8e with near-black text (#171717) on buttons, 'never white', at 6px radius ('square-ish, never pill'). Green is the only chromatic element on the marketing pages.
nodes.why: Dark-on-bright passes contrast where white-on-green fails, and feels more like a physical key.
nodes.implementation: .btn{background:#3ecf8e;color:#171717;border-radius:6px;font-weight:500}
nodes.pitfalls: Only works with light accents (L > 70%); on a navy accent it is unreadable.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Generated buttons put white text on every accent.

nodes.name: One oversized CTA card
nodes.what: Arc's 'Try Dia' CTA is a 76px-tall black card with 22px radius and asymmetric padding 8px 22px 8px 8px, holding an icon tile on the left and text on the right, while every other button on the page stays a conventional 40px pill.
nodes.why: The one action that matters gets physical mass; everything else recedes.
nodes.implementation: .cta-card{display:flex;gap:14px;align-items:center;height:76px;padding:8px 22px 8px 8px;border-radius:22px;background:#000;color:#fffcec} .cta-card .icon{width:60px;height:60px;border-radius:16px}
nodes.pitfalls: Two oversized cards side by side become the generic 'App Store / Play Store' pair.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Generated heroes use two equal 44px buttons.

nodes.name: Empty state keeps the table's bones
nodes.what: Instead of a centred illustration, the empty table keeps its header row and the height the rows occupied (Guidewire/Segment guidance; Linear's no-results state offers one-click 'clear all filters'). Liveblocks' rule: 'Design empty, loading, dense, and error states before calling a component done' and 'skeletons must match the final layout'.
nodes.why: No layout jump and the user still sees what the table will contain.
nodes.implementation: Render <thead> always; tbody min-height from previous rowcount*rowHeight; one inline action button; aria-live announcement.
nodes.pitfalls: A header over nothing with no action is dead; include a single verb+noun action and a filter reset.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Generated empty states are a centred SVG and 'No data yet'.

nodes.name: Inverted-L chrome with removable history
nodes.what: Linear's 2024 redesign frames every view in an 'inverted L' (sidebar + top strip) whose labels, icons and buttons are aligned on one grid; previous/next, history and tabs are modular so they vanish in the browser build and follow Apple conventions in Electron. Notion Mail's sidebar can be permanent or hover-only and collapses with a shortcut.
nodes.why: A consistent frame lets the many view types (list, board, timeline, split) change underneath without disorientation.
nodes.implementation: grid-template: 'side top' 40px 'side main' 1fr / 240px 1fr; align every control to a 32px row; hide .history in non-Electron via :has or UA flag.
nodes.pitfalls: Mixing sidebar density with marketing-size type breaks the grid; set a 28-36px row rhythm and stick to it.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Generated dashboards use a 256px sidebar with large icons and no alignment grid.

nodes.name: Inbox grouped by type, faces first
nodes.what: Linear's redesigned inbox groups notifications by type and gives more weight to teammates' avatars; headers and filters were simplified and comment alignment reviewed. Attio's hero shows the same device: an agent thread with 'Thinking' and 'Ran 3 commands' steps interleaved with people.
nodes.why: Faces are faster to scan than icons and make a work tool feel social without noise.
nodes.implementation: Group by notification type with sticky group headers; 20px avatars with 2px ring; unread dot in accent only.
nodes.pitfalls: Avatars for bots and systems clutter; use a monochrome glyph for non-humans.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Generated inboxes are icon+text rows.

nodes.name: Saved views are first-class sidebar objects
nodes.what: Notion Mail treats inbox 'Views' like database views: each has a name, icon, filters, grouping and displayed properties, and grouped views spawn sub-views in the navigation. The sidebar lists Search, Views, Mail, Templates, Trash; chrome is 'unassuming black and white' with grey buttons.
nodes.why: Letting users mint navigation turns a fixed app into a personal tool.
nodes.implementation: Sidebar section rendered from user views[]; each view = {icon, name, filter, groupBy}; URL state synced per view.
nodes.pitfalls: Unlimited views need a cap or folding (Notion caps sidebar page counts) or the sidebar scrolls forever.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Generated sidebars are static link lists.

nodes.name: Tabular figures and locale-formatted money
nodes.what: Midday's transaction mockups show signed, locale-formatted amounts ('+2 450,00 kr' against '-1 820,50 kr') aligned in columns; Liveblocks mandates tabular numbers for counts, limits, billing and metrics and locale-aware dates and currency; Warp's Hack terminal text enables tnum and slashed zero.
nodes.why: Aligned digits are what make a table feel like finance software rather than a web page.
nodes.implementation: td.num{font-variant-numeric:tabular-nums slashed-zero;text-align:right} Intl.NumberFormat(locale,{style:'currency',currency,signDisplay:'always'})
nodes.pitfalls: Proportional figures in a right-aligned column still wobble; tnum is mandatory, not optional.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Generated tables use default Inter proportional digits and '$1,234.00' everywhere.

nodes.name: Live production numbers in the hero
nodes.what: The hero shows real, ticking numbers instead of a claim: Warp's figure legend '224 tasks · 0 active · 1,422 PRs shipped' advancing 'on a shared clock'; Mintlify shows agent traffic share 'live in the hero' plus live counters for pages read and searches; Dub's 'links created / events tracked / revenue tracked' counters.
nodes.why: A number that changes while you watch is proof, not copy.
nodes.implementation: <output aria-live='polite' class='num'>1,422</output>; update via SSE/poll every 5-30s; font-variant-numeric:tabular-nums; no easing count-up.
nodes.pitfalls: Fake 'counting up from 0 on scroll' is the generated version; show a real figure with a timestamp and let it tick slowly.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Count-up animations are a tell; a static real number with a 'since 09:00 UTC' label and tnum is not.

nodes.name: Install command is the primary CTA
nodes.what: The hero's main action is a copyable command rather than a button: Convex 'npm create convex@latest', Payload 'npx create-payload-app', Inngest 'npm install inngest' with a copy button beside 'Start free', Sanity 'npm create sanity@latest' as a code chip under the buttons, Clerk's inline install prompt, Trigger.dev leading with a TypeScript sample as the hero visual.
nodes.why: It respects the audience: the first click is already the first step.
nodes.implementation: ; navigator.clipboard; label swaps to 'Copied' for 1.5s.
nodes.pitfalls: A command with no copy affordance or a fake '$' prefix that gets copied is worse than a button.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Generated heroes use two buttons; a command chip with 'Copied' state is a dev-tool convention generators rarely pick.

nodes.name: Prompt input as the whole hero
nodes.what: Lovable, Bolt ('Let's build a prototype…' with Plan / Build now), v0 and OpenAI (no headline at all, a 40px-high input pill with cycling placeholder text and 32px suggestion chips) make a text input the above-the-fold element; mode tabs (Website, App, Slides) and 'or start from Figma/GitHub' sit under it.
nodes.why: The product is the prompt, so the landing page is a working instance of it.
nodes.implementation:
…
; auto-grow; cycling placeholder via setInterval respecting reduced motion.
nodes.pitfalls: If the box is a dead mock that redirects to signup, trust drops; make it submit something real or do not use it.
nodes.ai_tell_note: By 2026 the prompt-box hero is the category default for AI tools and reads generated unless the input actually works.

nodes.name: Centred gradient glow behind the hero
nodes.what: A soft purple/blue radial glow or mesh behind centred hero text (Bolt ships a 'glow' asset; Together.ai uses abstract translucent discs). Listed here only as the pattern to avoid.
nodes.why: It fills empty space cheaply, which is exactly why every generator does it.
nodes.implementation: Avoid. If unavoidable: one hue, <30% alpha, anchored to an edge, never behind the headline.
nodes.pitfalls: It is the single most recognisable AI-generated hero; if atmosphere is needed use low-alpha-radial-washes off-centre and single-hue.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Centred multi-colour blur blobs behind a two-button hero are the canonical generated look.

nodes.name: ASCII and block-character diagrams
nodes.what: Diagrams are drawn in text: Warp's hero 'fig. 1' is a grid of ▩ ■ ▨ □ cells with a status legend (queued, working, waiting, shipped); PlanetScale's homepage flowchart (VTGate fanning to primaries and replicas, ░ shading on the active node) was drawn in Monodraw and rendered as a code block.
nodes.why: Text diagrams are honest about being engineering artefacts and are selectable, searchable and tiny.
nodes.implementation:
…
with font-family:'Lilex','JetBrains Mono',monospace; line-height:1.2; animate cells by swapping characters on a timer.
nodes.pitfalls: Box-drawing characters need a mono font with full coverage (Lilex, Berkeley Mono, JetBrains Mono) or they fall back and misalign.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Generators produce SVG flowcharts with rounded nodes; ASCII is a deliberate choice.

nodes.name: Terminal cut deeper than card
nodes.what: Warp places real terminal captures on a #0e0e0e surface inside #1a1a1a cards on a #121212 page, so the terminal reads as 'a window cut into the page'; a 28px chrome strip with traffic-light dots (#ff5f57, #febc2e, #28c840), lime block cursor blinking with steps(1,end) at 1s, and the only saturated colour lives inside the terminal. Resend's code wells (#06060a shells with hairline dots) do the same.
nodes.why: Depth by darkness instead of shadow keeps the dark page flat while the product still pops.
nodes.implementation: .term{background:#0e0e0e;border:1px solid rgba(255,255,255,.06)} .card{background:#1a1a1a} .cursor{animation:blink 1s steps(1,end) infinite}
nodes.pitfalls: Traffic-light dots in brand colours or with drop shadows become the 'code window' clip art; keep dots hairline or greyscale.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Mac-window code mockups are common; the inset-darker surface and steps() cursor are what read handmade.

nodes.name: Mascot illustrations as marginalia
nodes.what: PostHog's hedgehogs sit in margins like 'marginalia in a textbook': thick outlines, strong shapes, limited saturated palette ('illustration is where color lives'), explicitly banning 'floating shapes, abstract blobs, isometric 3D' and AI art. Fly.io's Annie Ruygt sketchbook characters (Frankie the balloon) head every blog post; Mistral's footer has a black pixel cat GIF.
nodes.why: A character gives a technical brand a voice no gradient can, and it ages well.
nodes.implementation: Commission 6-10 spot illustrations as SVG; place with float or grid-area in margins at 120-200px; never as hero backgrounds.
nodes.pitfalls: Generic flat-vector people (Humaaans style) are a tell; the character must be drawn by one hand with a consistent line weight.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Generated illustration is isometric or blob abstraction; hand-drawn mascot with thick outline is the opposite.

nodes.name: Pixel-art marks for models or products
nodes.what: Mistral renders each model (Codestral, Voxtral, Ministral) as a small pixel illustration in vibrant colour 'designed to shine at small scale', extending the pixel-cat emblem into a system; the logo exists in gradient, black and white only and may not be framed or recoloured.
nodes.why: Pixel marks scale down to 16px favicons and up to posters without losing identity, and nod to early ML history.
nodes.implementation: Draw on a 16x16 or 24x24 grid; export SVG rects or PNG with image-rendering:pixelated; scale by integers only.
nodes.pitfalls: Pixel art with anti-aliasing or odd scales blurs; render on an integer grid with image-rendering:pixelated.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Generated icon sets are rounded line icons.

nodes.name: ASCII character as the hero mark
nodes.what: Ghostty's homepage opens with its ghost drawn in ASCII beside the Download and Documentation buttons, and the terminal ships a '+boo' command that plays the same ghost as an animation. The site is open source and 29% CSS.
nodes.why: For a terminal product the logo rendered in the medium itself is the most honest brand asset possible.
nodes.implementation:
…
; animate by cycling frames with setInterval, paused under prefers-reduced-motion.
nodes.pitfalls: ASCII art needs an accessible name and must not be the only logo; provide SVG for favicons.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Generators never produce text art.

nodes.name: Keycap glyphs as the illustration system
nodes.what: Raycast builds illustrations from keyboard keys (esc, F1-F12, modifiers) rendered as 4px-radius keycaps with a #121212→#0d0d0d gradient and hairline, including a full keyboard above the footer; Lazy's CTA starts with ⌘. The keycap also serves as the <kbd> style in docs.
nodes.why: The product is a keystroke, so keys are both decoration and instruction.
nodes.implementation: kbd{display:inline-grid;place-items:center;min-width:28px;height:28px;border-radius:4px;background:linear-gradient(#121212,#0d0d0d);border:1px solid #242728;box-shadow:inset 0 1px 0 rgba(255,255,255,.06)}
nodes.pitfalls: Glossy 3D keycaps with heavy bevels look like 2012 skeuomorphism; keep 1px hairline and a 1px bottom highlight.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Generated sites show ⌘K only as text.

nodes.name: Glass, metal and grain materials
nodes.what: Resend's 2025 rebrand grounds a digital product in physical materials: glass- and metal-inspired buttons, a backdrop-filter blur(25px) glass token, a noise.png overlay 'for hero backgrounds and atmospheric depth', 3D wallpapers of 'minimalist geometry and organic forms', and the long-running Rubik's Cube on the landing page.
nodes.why: Texture and weight make an API feel 'solid, trustworthy, and built to last' in Resend's words.
nodes.implementation: .glass{backdrop-filter:blur(25px);background:rgba(255,255,255,.05);border:1px solid rgba(255,255,255,.1)} .hero::after{background:url(noise.png);opacity:.08;mix-blend-mode:overlay}
nodes.pitfalls: Frosted panels over gradient blobs is glassmorphism, the tell; here glass sits on near-black with a 6% hairline and grain, never on colour.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Blur and gradients are generated staples; the difference is grain, hairline borders and black behind the glass.

nodes.name: Film grain on flat colour fields
nodes.what: A tiled noise PNG at low opacity over flat backgrounds: Resend's noise.png over black heroes; Lazy's 'grain-bkg.png' behind a text-only hero. Grain is the only texture; no gradient underneath.
nodes.why: Grain reads as print or film and breaks the vector flatness that makes generated pages look generated.
nodes.implementation: body::before{content:'';position:fixed;inset:0;background:url(noise.png) repeat 0 0/200px;opacity:.06;pointer-events:none;mix-blend-mode:overlay}
nodes.pitfalls: Animated grain or grain over gradients turns into the 'aurora' tell; keep it static at 4-10% on a solid colour.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Generated backgrounds are gradients, not grain.

nodes.name: Die-cut sticker: white border, hard shadow
nodes.what: PostHog defines its sticker aesthetic as a white border with a hard (non-blurred) drop shadow, used on merch, video thumbnails and graphic elements, while the website itself keeps 'smooth drop shadows on cards'. Thick outlines in illustration echo it.
nodes.why: A hard offset shadow is unmistakably hand-made and prints well.
nodes.implementation: .sticker{border:4px solid #fff;box-shadow:4px 4px 0 #000;border-radius:8px}
nodes.pitfalls: Applying hard shadows to every card becomes neo-brutalism cosplay; reserve for stickers, badges and windows.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Generated shadows are soft blurs.

nodes.name: Layered cut-out photos on tinted fields
nodes.what: Craft layers persona portraits as a coloured background image plus a foreground cutout; Granola crops meeting-participant photographs flush against the hero edges and scatters 'floating-items' (grey.jpg, explosion.jpg, green-poster.jpg); Sanity overlays a code editor across a face and uses pixelated or fragmented photo treatments.
nodes.why: Real photography treated as collage avoids both stock-photo blandness and abstract 3D.
nodes.implementation: figure{display:grid} figure>*{grid-area:1/1} .bg{background:#6b5cff} img.cut{object-fit:cover;clip-path:inset(0 0 0 0)} position some items partly off-canvas.
nodes.pitfalls: Smiling-at-laptop stock cutouts are a tell; shoot or source candid, oddly cropped, with hard edges.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Generated imagery is illustration or UI mockups, not cut-out collage.

nodes.name: Generative 3D object hero
nodes.what: Vercel Ship 2025 built its event identity around ferrofluid-inspired 3D visuals, exploring with Flux, Veo 2, Runway and Ideogram (15,000+ images) and shipping a themeable shadcn+Geist component library; Together.ai uses translucent blue discs and an orange hexagon render; Modal's logo is a faceted gradient shape.
nodes.why: A single rendered object gives an abstract product a tangible mascot.
nodes.implementation: Pre-render to WebP/video with poster; no live WebGL on marketing pages; reduced-motion shows the still.
nodes.pitfalls: Glossy blobs and chrome spheres are now the generated 3D look; ferrofluid worked because it is matte black on black with one lighting setup.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Floating 3D shapes behind a hero are among the most recognised generated patterns; only a very specific material and no gradient background escape it.

nodes.name: Four-step duration ladder with one easing
nodes.what: Liveblocks' design.md fixes durations by element class: 0ms for repeated actions (keyboard shortcuts, command menus, row selection, toggles), ~150ms state changes, ~200ms popovers and tooltips, ~300ms overlays, sheets and dialogs; reveal easing cubic-bezier(0.175, 0.885, 0.32, 1.1); animate only transform and opacity; origins from trigger (popover), edge (drawer), centre (dialog); everything interruptible. Warp's extraction: 100/180/320ms with cubic-bezier(.4,0,.2,1).
nodes.why: A ladder removes per-component motion decisions and makes the whole app feel like one material.
nodes.implementation: :root{--d-state:150ms;--d-pop:200ms;--d-overlay:300ms;--ease-out:cubic-bezier(.175,.885,.32,1.1)} .popover{transform-origin:var(--anchor);transition:transform var(--d-pop) var(--ease-out),opacity var(--d-pop)}
nodes.pitfalls: Overshoot easing (y > 1) on large dialogs looks bouncy; use it only on small reveals.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Generated CSS uses transition: all .3s ease.

nodes.name: No animation on high-frequency actions
nodes.what: Rauno Freiberg's principle: skip animation for frequent keyboard and mouse actions (command menus, app switchers) because repeated motion becomes cognitive burden; macOS context menus open instantly, fade out, and flash the selected item in the accent colour to confirm. Liveblocks codifies 0ms for command menus and toggles; cmdk ships unstyled so this is possible.
nodes.why: Instant response is what makes a tool feel fast; confirmation can come from a flash, not a transition.
nodes.implementation: [cmdk-root]{animation:none} .menu-item:active{animation:flash 120ms steps(2,end)} @keyframes flash{50%{background:var(--accent)}}
nodes.pitfalls: Zero motion on rare, spatial transitions (opening a sheet) feels broken; apply only to repeated actions.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Generated command palettes fade and scale in over 200ms.

nodes.name: Directional tab motion
nodes.what: Family's rule 'we fly instead of teleport': tapping a tab to the right slides content leftward, tapping left slides it right; a chevron morphs across multi-step flows; persistent components stay put rather than duplicating during the transition; in empty states only the changing text updates.
nodes.why: Direction encodes spatial memory, so users always know where they came from.
nodes.implementation: document.startViewTransition(); html.dir-left::view-transition-old(panel){animation:slide-out-left 180ms} ::view-transition-new(panel){animation:slide-in-right 180ms}
nodes.pitfalls: Sliding whole pages 300ms every tab tap is slow; keep it under 200ms and transform-only, or use View Transitions with a direction class.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Generated tab switches cross-fade.

nodes.name: Button label morphs through shared letters
nodes.what: Family animates 'Continue' into 'Confirm' by keeping the shared 'Con' in place and swapping only the tail, signalling a significant step; a wallet-add button's count and label adjust in place; pending-transaction spinners travel into the bottom nav to show where the item will live.
nodes.why: Morphing in place tells the user the button is the same object with raised stakes.
nodes.implementation: Split label into <span>s per glyph; cross-fade differing glyphs with 120ms opacity+translateY(4px); keep shared prefix static (or View Transitions with view-transition-name per span).
nodes.pitfalls: Per-letter animation on every label becomes a gimmick; reserve for one irreversible action.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Generated buttons swap text instantly or show a spinner.

nodes.name: Stacked trays of varying height
nodes.what: Family's tray system: bottom sheets open from buttons or notifications, each subsequent tray has a different height so the change is legible, each has a title and a dismiss/back icon, holds one action, darkens in dark flows, and can expand to full screen for long flows. Vaul (Emil Kowalski) implements this with the iOS curve cubic-bezier(0.32, 0.72, 0, 1), velocity-based dismiss (~0.11 px/ms) and scaled background.
nodes.why: Trays keep the parent screen visible so confirmations never lose context.
nodes.implementation: <dialog> with transform:translateY; height:auto per step; transition height via interpolate-size:allow-keywords or FLIP; easing cubic-bezier(.32,.72,0,1) 400-500ms; drag with pointer events.
nodes.pitfalls: Trays that are all the same height make steps feel like nothing happened; vary height by content and animate it.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Generated mobile flows use full-screen modals.

nodes.name: Stacked toasts, 14px offset
nodes.what: Sonner's pattern: new toasts push older ones back with a scale step and a 14px vertical offset so three remain visible as a stack, expanding on hover; enter and exit from the same edge so swipe-to-dismiss is intuitive; timers pause when the tab is hidden. Liveblocks' copy rules apply to the content.
nodes.why: Stacking shows history without covering content, and same-edge exit matches the swipe gesture.
nodes.implementation: .toast:nth-last-child(2){transform:translateY(-14px) scale(.95)} .toast:nth-last-child(3){transform:translateY(-28px) scale(.9)} visibilitychange pauses timers.
nodes.pitfalls: Stacks taller than three or toasts that never auto-dismiss become a notification centre.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Generated toasts replace each other in a corner.

nodes.name: Hover is silent, leaving animates
nodes.what: PostHog's handbook: hovering a button should not trigger animation, but leaving one can; a slight zoom on hover and a 'pressing down' feel on click are encouraged; character rigs animate shadows with the figure. Logo walls (Warp) sit at 0.6 opacity greyscale and rise to full colour on hover.
nodes.why: Reacting on exit avoids the jitter of pointer sweeps while still feeling alive.
nodes.implementation: .btn{transition:transform 180ms} .btn:hover{transition:none;transform:scale(1.02)} .btn:active{transform:scale(.98)} .logo{filter:grayscale(1);opacity:.6} .logo:hover{filter:none;opacity:1}
nodes.pitfalls: Scale on hover above 1.03 or with shadow growth is the generated 'card lift' tell.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Generated hover is translateY(-4px) plus shadow-xl over 300ms.

nodes.name: Progressive agent status labels
nodes.what: Agent-era products show work as a sequence of present-participle labels: Attio 'Thinking' then 'Ran 3 commands'; Antimetal 'Reading your code…', 'Drafting a fix…', 'Checks running', 'Antimetal is watching'; Cursor tags stages with five pastel pills (thinking #dfa88f, grep #9fc9a2, read #9fbbe0, edit #c0a8dd, done #c08532) that 'never appear outside agent timeline contexts'; Framer's 'Thinking...' with model label.
nodes.why: A visible log of verbs makes autonomous work legible and trustworthy.
nodes.implementation:
1. Reading your code…
    2. …; .pill[data-stage=read]{background:#9fbbe0} appear with 150ms opacity only.
nodes.pitfalls: Fake typing animations with random delays feel theatrical; reveal real steps with timestamps.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Shimmering 'Thinking…' is becoming standard; pastel per-stage pills and a real step log are still specific.

nodes.name: Shine sweep across heading text
nodes.what: PlanetScale's heading shine: background-clip:text with a 400% background-size gradient 'linear-gradient(110deg, currentColor, var(--orange-500) 60%, var(--orange-200) 65%, currentColor 75%)' giving a sharp front edge and a long light trail that sweeps once on reveal; the rest of the text stays currentColor.
nodes.why: A one-off sweep draws the eye without permanently gradient-colouring the headline.
nodes.implementation: h1{background:linear-gradient(110deg,currentColor,#f26b1d 60%,#fcd7bd 65%,currentColor 75%) 100%/400%;-webkit-background-clip:text;color:transparent;animation:shine 1.2s ease-out 1 forwards} @keyframes shine{to{background-position:0}}
nodes.pitfalls: A permanent purple-to-pink gradient text is the tell; the sweep must end on solid currentColor and run once.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Gradient text is generated; a single sweeping highlight that resolves to plain text is not.

nodes.name: Midline reveal, pause offscreen
nodes.what: PlanetScale triggers reveals with IntersectionObserver threshold 1 and rootMargin '0% 0px -50%' so elements animate only when they reach the middle of the screen; above-the-fold items get an initialValue to avoid flashing; looping animations pause via animation-play-state when offscreen; a sticky diagram shares one --top-position so cards stay centred from phone to 4K.
nodes.why: Midline triggering means users actually see the reveal, and pausing keeps scrolling smooth.
nodes.implementation: animation-timeline:view(); animation-range:entry 50% entry 60%; or IO{threshold:1,rootMargin:'0% 0px -50%'}; .loop{animation-play-state:paused} .loop.in-view{animation-play-state:running}
nodes.pitfalls: Fading every paragraph in from below is the generated AOS look; reveal only figures and section openers, and use opacity only.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Scroll fade-ups are a tell when applied everywhere; scoped to figures with midline timing they read considered.

nodes.name: Reduced motion swaps layout
nodes.what: PlanetScale under prefers-reduced-motion: the hero animation does not play and the canvas pixel grid becomes a static grid; the logo marquee stops and becomes a centred two-row wrapping layout; the diagram swaps multi-level animation for fades; the carousel cuts between panels with behavior:'instant'. Low-powered devices get the static grid regardless.
nodes.why: Designing a real alternative layout respects the preference instead of freezing a half-finished animation.
nodes.implementation: @media (prefers-reduced-motion:reduce){.marquee{animation:none;display:flex;flex-wrap:wrap;justify-content:center} .carousel{scroll-behavior:auto}}
nodes.pitfalls: Setting animation-duration:0.01ms globally leaves marquees as cropped single rows; author the fallback layout.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Generated sites ignore reduced motion or kill all transitions.

nodes.name: Native scroll-snap feature rail
nodes.what: PlanetScale's features carousel is a CSS grid with grid-auto-flow:column, scroll-snap-type:x mandatory and scroll-snap-align:center; a 1px ::before and a full-column-width ::after align the first and last slides, so no carousel library and no scroll-jacking. Long table-cell copy moves into tooltips to keep cells uniform.
nodes.why: Native snapping is accessible, swipeable and 0 KB.
nodes.implementation: .rail{display:grid;grid-auto-flow:column;grid-auto-columns:min(80vw,560px);overflow-x:auto;scroll-snap-type:x mandatory;gap:24px} .rail>*{scroll-snap-align:center} .rail::before{content:'';width:1px} .rail::after{content:'';width:min(80vw,560px)}
nodes.pitfalls: Mandatory snap on tall slides traps vertical scrolling; keep slides shorter than the viewport.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Generated carousels import Swiper.

nodes.name: Live mockups labelled 'Tap to interact'
nodes.what: Sanity marks product mockups with 'Tap to interact' / 'Click to interact' labels and runs a live 'Just now' notification inside an automation demo; Mux offers 'Try another video' and a 'Show the code' toggle with React / Web component / Iframe tabs; Cursor and Framer embed working demos rather than videos.
nodes.why: A mockup you can poke is proof the product is real and already teaches the UI.
nodes.implementation: ; hint fades on first pointerdown; keep the demo keyboard-operable.
nodes.pitfalls: An interactive mockup that only toggles one tab feels like a trick; wire at least one real state change and a code view.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Generated pages use static screenshots or autoplay video.

nodes.name: Receipt-style cost breakdown ending in $0
nodes.what: Mux lays pricing out as a receipt: line items in monospace, a dashed rule, 'Total: $0' at the bottom, followed by a calculator CTA. Polar's hero dashboard shows 'tokens metered / revenue / gross margin / inference cost' tiles with a revenue-vs-cost chart.
nodes.why: A receipt is the most familiar way humans read money and makes a free tier tangible.
nodes.implementation: <table class='receipt'> with font-family:ui-monospace;border-top:1px dashed; td:last-child{text-align:right;font-variant-numeric:tabular-nums}
nodes.pitfalls: A receipt that hides overages is read as deceptive; include the first paid line.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Generated pricing is three cards; a receipt is a specific device.

nodes.name: 'Replaces:' competitor logo row
nodes.what: Amie's product sections each carry a 'Replaces:' row of small competitor logos under the headline (calendar, notes, email tools), and the footer links an 'Alternatives' index. Midday's pain-point cards price admin in time ('45 minutes per week', '1 hour per week', summarised as '4-6 hours').
nodes.why: Naming the thing being replaced is a sharper value claim than any adjective.
nodes.implementation:
Replaces …

.replaces img{height:16px;filter:grayscale(1);opacity:.7}
nodes.pitfalls: Logos without permission or with wrong colours invite takedowns; use greyscale wordmarks at 16-20px.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Generated pages avoid naming competitors.

nodes.name: Wall of real signatures
nodes.what: Arc's farewell page ends with roughly 40 individually rendered staff signature images in a grid followed by the founder's signature; Fey's shutdown page closes with 'Signatures of the Fey founders'. HEY ends with a founder's letter in plain prose, signed.
nodes.why: Handwriting is the one asset no competitor or model can reproduce, and it makes a company legible as people.
nodes.implementation: Grid of inline SVG paths (currentColor, stroke 1.5) at 120-160px; optional stroke-dasharray draw-on under motion-ok.
nodes.pitfalls: Script fonts standing in for signatures are a tell; scan real ink as SVG paths.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Generators cannot produce real signatures.

nodes.name: Footer with clocks and status
nodes.what: Sanity's bottom bar shows the copyright, two local time zones and a system-status link; Payload's footer has an Auto / Light / Dark switcher; Midday ends with 'Toggle theme' and 'System status: Operational'; Baseten shows a live 'all systems normal' status; Inngest 'All systems operational'.
nodes.why: A footer that does something (time, status, theme) reads as a living console rather than a sitemap.
nodes.implementation:
……All systems normal
…
; Intl.DateTimeFormat with timeZone; tabular-nums.
nodes.pitfalls: A fake green dot with no status page behind it is worse than none; link to a real status feed.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Generated footers are four link columns and a copyright.

nodes.name: Dashed vs solid rules as hierarchy
nodes.what: PlanetScale encodes importance in line style: the hero customer-logo grid uses solid 1px rules because it is the hero element, while the footer uses dashed rules to signal secondary importance; the h1 carries a solid orange bar. Warp's two-line headings sit on an underline-style rule.
nodes.why: Line style is a hierarchy channel that costs no colour or size.
nodes.implementation: hr.primary{border:0;border-top:1px solid var(--ink)} hr.secondary{border-top:1px dashed var(--hair)} h1{border-left:3px solid #f26b1d}
nodes.pitfalls: Dashed borders on cards look like file-upload dropzones; use dashed only on horizontal rules.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Generated dividers are a single border-gray-200.

nodes.name: One pastel tint per block
nodes.what: Craft assigns each feature block a single pastel (mint #9bd8a9, amber #fde99b, periwinkle #b8caf5, sky #9ed4ef, peach #ffdbc5) on a beige-to-white canvas ladder with a 0 1px 2px shadow at most; Cursor scopes five pastels strictly to agent-timeline pills; Mistral uses a cream family (#fff8e0, #fffaeb, #fff0c2) for panels.
nodes.why: A single tint per surface keeps colour meaningful and avoids the rainbow-card grid.
nodes.implementation: .block{--tint:#9bd8a9;background:color-mix(in oklab,var(--tint) 35%,#fff)} .block .chip{background:var(--tint)}
nodes.pitfalls: Three pastel cards in a row with icons is the generated 'feature grid'; use tints on large, uneven blocks with real screenshots.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Pastel cards are a tell when uniform and iconed; uneven blocks with one tint each and no icons read designed.

nodes.name: Dated changelog line as pill
nodes.what: Instead of a 'New ✨' badge, the pill under the hero quotes the latest changelog line with a date: Amie 'Sep 3: much better CPU, new recorder pill, new recording settings'; Cal.com 'Cal.com launches v6.9.5'; Mux 'Mux Robots · Now GA!' as a top strip; Inngest shows an 'Open Source 7.1K' star badge in the nav.
nodes.why: A specific dated line proves the product is alive in a way a generic badge cannot.
nodes.implementation: Sep 3 much better CPU, new recorder pill .pill{border:1px solid var(--hair);border-radius:999px;font-size:13px} time{font-family:ui-monospace}
nodes.pitfalls: The 'Introducing X →' gradient-border pill is a strong tell; use a plain hairline pill with a mono date and an unglamorous commit-style message.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Hero announcement pills are generated boilerplate; the date plus a boring real changelog line is what saves it.

nodes.name: Customer proof as text list
nodes.what: Clerk's and Mintlify's homepages render 'Trusted by' as a plain text sentence or list of company names ('Customers include: …') rather than a logo wall; PlanetScale lets 'tech and customer logos do the talking' but in a solid-ruled grid with no marquee; Notion and Together use strictly monochrome logo files.
nodes.why: Typeset names avoid the mismatched-logo-marquee look and read as a sentence a human wrote.
nodes.implementation:
Customers include Vercel, Linear, Raycast, …

or a static CSS grid with 1px solid rules, no animation.
nodes.pitfalls: A text list of unknown startups proves nothing; include at most eight recognisable names.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Generated proof is a greyscale infinite marquee of 12 logos.

nodes.name: Bento grid of feature tiles
nodes.what: A rounded-corner mosaic of unequal feature tiles with icons and short labels (Superhuman Go's section, many 2024-25 SaaS pages). Recorded as the pattern to avoid.
nodes.why: It packages six weak features as one strong image, which is why generators default to it.
nodes.implementation: Avoid. Prefer numbered-section-eyebrows with full-width product figures, or one polarity-flipped card.
nodes.pitfalls: Any grid with 12-16px radius tiles, icon+title+line, and one tile with a gradient is read as generated instantly.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Bento grids are the most recognisable 2023-25 generated layout.

nodes.name: Serif-italic accent word (tell)
nodes.what: One italicised word in Instrument Serif inside a geometric sans headline, or underscored emphasis like Midday's 'The business stack for _modern_ founders'; Warp's extraction lists Instrument Serif for 'rare editorial italics'. Recorded as a pattern to avoid.
nodes.why: It gives a cheap editorial flourish, hence its spread.
nodes.implementation: Avoid. Use a full serif display or none.
nodes.pitfalls: Now a recognised tell; if a serif is wanted set the whole headline in it at weight 400 (editorial-serif-display-for-devtool).
nodes.ai_tell_note: Instrument Serif italic accent words are a 2025 generated signature.

nodes.name: Story numbers as list markers
nodes.what: The archive is a single vertical list where every story carries a running number in the gutter (The Pudding counts down from #226; Soft Labor labels posts 'No. 56'; Increment numbers its 18 topic categories 1-18). The number sits as the list marker or as a small label above the title, in tabular figures, and never resets.
nodes.why: A running count turns an archive into a serial publication with history, something a generic blog grid never communicates.
nodes.implementation: ol { counter-reset: story 227 } li { counter-increment: story -1 } li::before { content: '#' counter(story); font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums }
nodes.pitfalls: Numbers that restart per page or per year lose the serial effect; use a global counter.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Generated layouts default to undated cards; a global issue counter implies a real backlog.

nodes.name: Volume, number, date as page title
nodes.what: The issue identifier is the largest text on the contents page: 'Vol. 48 No. 20 · 5 November 2026' set as a display heading with a rule under it, middle dot separators, previous/next issue arrows beside it (LRB). Asterisk does the same with '16: Flourishing' and an explicit 'No next issue' label on the disabled arrow.
nodes.why: Treats the issue, not the brand, as the object the reader arrived at, which is how print periodicals present themselves.
nodes.implementation: h1.issue { font-size: clamp(2rem, 5vw, 4rem); font-variant-numeric: lining-nums tabular-nums } separator via content: ' · ' ; disabled arrow gets aria-disabled and a literal 'No next issue' label.
nodes.pitfalls: Only works if content is genuinely grouped into issues; a fake issue number reads as costume.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Requires an editorial model (issues, volumes) that generated sites almost never have.

nodes.name: Contributor name above title
nodes.what: Contents entries lead with the author's name as the heading and put the piece title beneath it in a secondary size (LRB contents; n+1 issue pages put the author link above the underlined title). Multiple contributors are joined with 'and' or an ampersand; Asterisk runs several names together with no punctuation at all.
nodes.why: Signals that the publication sells writers, not SEO headlines, and it reads like a printed table of contents.
nodes.implementation:
• Name

    Title

    • with .who at 1.25rem/600 and .what at 1rem serif italic.
nodes.pitfalls: Fails when authors are unknown to the audience; then the title must stay visually dominant.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Inverts the default title-then-byline order that every template ships with.
avoid_words: news feeds where the headline is the hook

nodes.name: Italic citation block under reviews
nodes.what: Review entries carry a full citation line in italics beneath the reviewer's name: book title, author, publisher, page count, price, publication month, ISBN (LRB contents). On the article page the block repeats under the headline with a 'Show More' disclosure when there are several works; a film review swaps in 'directed by'.
nodes.why: Dense bibliographic metadata, set as typography rather than a card, is an instant marker of a serious review organ.
nodes.implementation:
Title by Author.
Publisher, 320 pp., £25, October, 978 0 00 000000 0

with hanging-punctuation: first; details/summary for 'Show More'.
nodes.pitfalls: Needs real data for every field; a half-filled citation looks broken rather than scholarly.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Generated drafts never invent ISBNs and page counts; the density itself reads as human.

nodes.name: Genre prefix in the title
nodes.what: Recurring formats are named inside the title with a colon: 'Short Cuts: ...', 'Poem: "9 October"', 'At the Movies: "Digger"', 'Diary' (LRB). The Paris Review does it with 'In the Current Issue, Issue 257' plus a tiny section icon; Monocle and Every use the column name as a label line such as 'Oct 28, 2026 IN Context Window'.
nodes.why: Formats become brands readers return to, and the prefix does the job a coloured tag chip normally does without any chip.
nodes.implementation:
Short Cuts: Title

.kicker { font-variant: small-caps; letter-spacing: .04em; font-weight: 500 }
nodes.pitfalls: More than five or six recurring formats and the prefixes stop being memorable.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Generated UIs reach for coloured pills; typographic prefixes are an editorial habit.

nodes.name: Word count in the byline
nodes.what: The byline row states length as words, not minutes: '4,053 words' under the LRB headline; Klim's essays put word count, author and date on one line beneath the standfirst. Monocle instead shows 'Issue #198 · 4 min read' and Werktitel '62 minuten' for audio.
nodes.why: A word count is honest and specific, and it tells the reader this is a long read before they commit.
nodes.implementation:
4,053 words · Eyal Weizman · 5 Nov 2026

with font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums.
nodes.pitfalls: Rounded 'approximately 4,000 words' undoes the precision; print the exact tabular number.
nodes.ai_tell_note: '5 min read' with a clock icon is the generated default; exact word counts are not.

nodes.name: 'Words by' above the headline
nodes.what: The byline is phrased 'Words by Alex Chalmers' and placed between the hero image and the title, before the headline, in small type (Works in Progress). The headline then follows, with date, share icons, a translate control and reading time on one row beneath it.
nodes.why: Crediting 'words' (and by implication 'images') frames the page as a made object with several crafts, not a post.
nodes.implementation:
Words by Name

Title

...
nodes.pitfalls: Looks affected when there is only one craft on the page; pair it with 'Photographs by' or 'Illustration by'.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Byline-before-title is an editorial inversion that templates do not produce.

nodes.name: One-line question as dek
nodes.what: Instead of a summary paragraph, the standfirst is a single provocative line: 'How many Sagrada Famílias is too many?' (Asterisk), 'Alex Chalmers reviews Armies of Sand by Kenneth Pollack' (WIP). Quanta sets its dek under the byline and opens with the subject's name.
nodes.why: A single short line under a big headline preserves the typographic hierarchy that a three-sentence summary flattens.
nodes.implementation: h1 + p.dek { font-size: 1.25rem; font-style: italic; max-width: 40ch; text-wrap: balance }
nodes.pitfalls: Clickbait phrasing ruins it; the line should be witty or declarative, not a tease.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Generated copy produces a two-sentence summary; a single wry line is an editor's move.

nodes.name: Asterisms instead of subheads
nodes.what: Long essays have no internal headings; sections are separated by centred '* * *' (Asterisk articles use four such breaks; Walker Reader separates standfirst from body with one; Craig Mod uses them between homepage sections). The break is set in the text face with generous space above and below.
nodes.why: Keeps the reading rhythm of a book and refuses the skimmable, SEO-shaped H2 ladder.
nodes.implementation: hr.asterism { border: 0; text-align: center; margin: 3rem 0 } hr.asterism::before { content: '*  *  *'; letter-spacing: .5em; font-family: inherit }
nodes.pitfalls: On a page that genuinely needs navigation (long reference text) the lack of headings becomes hostile.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Generated articles are heading-heavy; asterisms are a literary convention.

nodes.name: Footnotes shown three ways
nodes.what: Klim marks a note with a superscript numeral, repeats the note inline immediately after the paragraph with a back-arrow link, and lists it again under 'Notes & references' at the end. Asterisk uses bracketed [1] after punctuation with a numbered end list and a return arrow icon per note.
nodes.why: The reader never has to leave the paragraph, yet the scholarly apparatus still exists for citation.
nodes.implementation:
1 ...
1. text ↩
; sup { font-variant-position: super } with a fallback font-size: .75em.
nodes.pitfalls: Superscripts in many browsers render as faux-shrunk glyphs; use font-variant-position: super and real sup figures.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Generated prose never carries footnotes at all.

nodes.name: Sidenotes in the right margin
nodes.what: Notes float into the outer margin beside their anchor rather than at the foot. Tufte-CSS values: float: right; margin-right: -60%; width: 50%; font-size: 1.1rem; line-height: 1.3, collapsing to inline toggles below 760px. Nystrom uses padding-right: 300px on the page and 240px-wide asides from 800px up; Gwern.net repositions with JS to avoid overlaps and switches to floating footnotes on narrow screens.
nodes.why: Keeps commentary in the reader's peripheral vision without breaking the main measure.
nodes.implementation: article { display: grid; grid-template-columns: 1fr min(65ch, 100%) 18rem 1fr } .sidenote { grid-column: 3; font-size: .85rem } @media (max-width: 760px) { .sidenote { grid-column: 2; display: none } .toggle:checked + .sidenote { display: block } }
nodes.pitfalls: Adjacent notes overlap; either accept author-managed spacing, use calc() nudges, or add a small reflow script.
nodes.ai_tell_note: A real margin apparatus is rare and clearly deliberate.

nodes.name: Left/Right paired figures
nodes.what: Two images sit side by side with one caption that begins 'Left:' and 'Right:' and ends with a shared credit such as 'Both images courtesy Wikimedia Commons' (Asterisk). Captions give work, architect, date, location and source in that order.
nodes.why: One caption for two images is a print convention that signals an editor arranged the spread rather than a CMS dumping images.
nodes.implementation: .pair { display: grid; grid-template-columns: 1fr 1fr; gap: 1rem }
nodes.pitfalls: On mobile the pair stacks and 'Left/Right' becomes wrong; switch to 'Above/Below' via a container query or number the figures.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Generated layouts caption each image independently.

nodes.name: Sentence captions with courtesy line
nodes.what: Captions are full sentences naming director, work (italic), year, then a separate credit 'Image courtesy Janus Films.' (Walker Reader). Quanta sets the credit as 'Name for Quanta Magazine'; LRB uses '© and TM Aardman Animations LTD'. Credits are smaller, often in a second colour, and end with a period.
nodes.why: Proper provenance is how institutions write, and the two-tier caption gives the figure its own micro-hierarchy.
nodes.implementation: figcaption { font-size: .875rem } figcaption .credit { display: block; color: var(--ink-2); font-variant-caps: all-small-caps; letter-spacing: .03em }
nodes.pitfalls: Fake credits are worse than none; only use when provenance is real.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Generated pages omit credits entirely, which is itself a tell.

nodes.name: Quoted line instead of summary
nodes.what: List entries show a short quotation from the piece in quotation marks under the title instead of a synopsis: McSweeney's puts 'The full moon is not an excuse for absenteeism.' beneath a title, then 'by Name'. n+1 has a 'pullquote' card template that replaces the image with a large quote. Quanta transcripts repeat key sentences as standalone pull lines.
nodes.why: The piece introduces itself in its own voice, which no auto-generated summary can do.
nodes.implementation: p.quote { hanging-punctuation: first; quotes: '“' '”' } p.quote::before { content: open-quote }
nodes.pitfalls: Needs curly quotes and hanging punctuation or the opening quote mark dents the left edge.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Generated cards use description text; a quoted line is an editorial selection.

nodes.name: Date or status before the title
nodes.what: Museum cards put timing above the title as a short kicker: 'Until 31 January' (Serpentine), 'Through Feb 27, 2027' and a 'Last chance' label (MoMA), 'Opens 6 November 2026', 'Free Display', 'Members go free' (Design Museum), 'Now on View' (SFMOMA, Cooper Hewitt). The status word is the scannable element, not the image.
nodes.why: Visitors scan for whether they can still go; the date line answers that before the name.
nodes.implementation:
Until 31 January

Title

.when { font-size: .8rem; text-transform: uppercase; letter-spacing: .08em }
nodes.pitfalls: Mixed capitalisation ('Now on view' vs 'Now On View') undermines it; fix the vocabulary.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Generated event cards put the date under the title in grey; leading with it is a curatorial habit.

nodes.name: Collapsed date ranges
nodes.what: Ranges drop whatever the two ends share: 'Fri 13 —Sun 15 Nov 2026', 'Fri 9 Oct 2026 —Sun 28 Feb 2027', single events 'Mon 9 Nov 2026, 20:00' (Barbican). Hours use an en dash and weekday grouping: 'Mon–Tue 10 a.m.–5 p.m.' with 'Wed Closed' on its own line (SFMOMA); '10:00 – 17:00' (Design Museum). Walker uses 'Oct 17, 2026–Feb 14, 2027'.
nodes.why: Typographically correct dates are one of the clearest signs a human set the page.
