Framer's ASCII Hero Image keeps the headline as a real DOM text layer above the canvas.
nodes.why: Edge-aware glyph choice keeps silhouettes crisp so the object reads at a glance instead of as a noise field.
nodes.implementation: Three.js: offscreen scene pass at 12px per cell row, cell pass computing glyph index into an 8-bit target, post pass sampling the atlas with textureGrad; static fallback: <pre aria-hidden> with the first frame.
nodes.pitfalls: If WebGL fails the element stays empty; always ship a pre-rendered <pre> frame as the fallback and the first paint.
nodes.ai_tell_note: ASCII heroes spread fast through Framer and 21st.dev components in 2025; the shape-aware renderer with a real monospace system still reads bespoke, a luminance-ramp donut does not.

nodes.name: Static ASCII art in a pre block
nodes.what: ASCII or box-drawing art set in a <pre> with the site's monospace font, coloured through CSS (spans per tone, or background-clip: text over a gradient), optionally animated frame by frame with a CSS steps() animation swapping a few hand-made frames; 21st.dev's ASCII editor exports such loops in Pixel Art, Dither and Hex Dump styles. The real headline sits beside it as HTML text.
nodes.why: It gives a technical brand a hero image that costs no bytes, scales with the type system and prints well.
nodes.implementation: pre{font:400 clamp(.4rem,1vw,.8rem)/1.1 var(--mono);white-space:pre;aria-hidden:true} .f{display:none} .f:nth-child(1){display:block} with @keyframes cycling frames via steps(1).
nodes.pitfalls: A <pre> wider than the viewport breaks mobile; set font-size with clamp() in vw units or hide it below 640px.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Generated pages use SVG illustrations; typeset ASCII is a culture-specific signal.

nodes.name: Square lens follows cursor
nodes.what: A square window (squareSize 0.3, about 60% of the shorter viewport side) follows the pointer with a lerp factor of 0.1 and shows the colour, undistorted image inside while the outside stays grayscale with gentle wave (frequency 10, strength 0.01) and noise (strength 0.02) distortion; inside the square a lens bulge (lensDistortion 1.5) and RGB shift of ±0.01 grow linearly toward the edges; the mask uses hard step edges, no feathering. All in one full-screen fragment shader, no render targets.
nodes.why: Keeping the rest desaturated makes the lens the only colour on screen, which pulls the eye wherever the user points.
nodes.implementation: WebGL fragment with uMouse lerped on CPU; CSS approximation: grayscale page plus a fixed square div with backdrop-filter: grayscale(0) is impossible, so layer a colour copy clipped with clip-path: inset() around the cursor.
nodes.pitfalls: Lerp per frame is frame-rate dependent; scale the factor by delta time or it feels different on 120Hz.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Bespoke shader with hard-edged square mask, not a template effect.

nodes.name: Fluid simulation under cursor
nodes.what: A GPU fluid sim (density dissipation, velocity, pressure, curl parameters) driven by pointer movement, used either as visible smoke colour or, as in Atelier UI, with blend and intensity at 0 so it only distorts the WebGL copies of text and images beneath the cursor; elements opt out with postProcessing false. Framer variants add bloom, sunrays and idle autoplay splats so touch devices still see motion.
nodes.why: Distortion without colour keeps the page's typography intact while making every pointer move feel wet and responsive.
nodes.implementation: Three.js or WebGPU fluid sim ping-pong textures; sample the velocity texture as UV offset in the material of mirrored DOM planes; no static equivalent.
nodes.pitfalls: Rainbow smoke trails were a 2019 cliché; keep it colourless and subtle, and never on the whole page on mobile.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Coloured fluid cursors are a known Framer-component look; distortion-only versions on real content read handmade.

nodes.name: Liquid chrome logotype
nodes.what: A wordmark or headline rendered as molten chrome: Paper Shaders' 'liquid metal' logo animation, 21st.dev 'Weld Pool' which embeds the headline in the same height field as the metal so letters dent under the pointer, and SmoothUI's WebGL2 liquid metal with chrome, gold, mercury and oil palettes plus a text-clipped mode. Y2K guidance: use one chrome cue per composition. The static approximation is background-clip: text over a hard-stop metallic linear gradient rotated via an @property-registered angle.
nodes.why: Chrome gives type specular highlights that move, so a flat wordmark reads as an object.
nodes.implementation: @property --a{syntax:'<angle>';inherits:false;initial-value:0deg} h1{background:linear-gradient(var(--a),#fff 0 8%,#8a8a8a 9% 28%,#fff 30% 34%,#2b2b2b 36% 60%,#e8e8e8 62% 70%,#555 72%);-webkit-background-clip:text;color:transparent;animation:a 6s linear infinite} @keyframes a{to{--a:360deg}}.
nodes.pitfalls: Chrome plus bubble type plus holographic gradient is the full Y2K kit and reads as costume; pick the chrome and keep the rest flat.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Liquid metal exploded in 2025 shader libraries; a chrome blob background is becoming a tell, chrome applied to a custom logotype is not yet.
avoid_words: holographic gradients and lens flares at the same time

nodes.name: Datamosh shot transition
nodes.what: Cutting between 3D shots while a feedback decoder keeps smearing the old frame: each frame is the previous output warped by screen-space motion vectors (clamped ±0.25, scaled 0.5, quantised to 8px blocks) plus only 12% of the fresh render and a luminance-only residual; packet-loss rectangles freeze after 300ms, up to 4 lost-sector layers starting at a 7 × 5 grid, and a 370ms recovery ramp returns the clean image on release. Triggered by pointer press, Space or touch.
nodes.why: The glitch has physical cause (motion vectors) so it reads as broken video rather than a random noise filter.
nodes.implementation: Three.js: velocity pass with previous MVP, ping-pong feedback targets, decode pass with Catmull-Rom sampling, FXAA; no static equivalent.
nodes.pitfalls: Hold-to-mosh with no cap can flash; limit duration, honour reduced motion with a hard cut, and avoid full-screen luminance flicker.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Far too specific to be generated; generic 'glitch' CSS text shadows are the tell, not this.

nodes.name: CRT scanlines on one surface
nodes.what: A terminal window, video embed or hero panel (not the whole page) gets 2px repeating-linear-gradient scanlines at low alpha, a soft radial vignette, slight barrel distortion via a border-radius on the inner frame and a 1px chromatic text-shadow (red left, cyan right) on monospace text; optionally a slow 'roll' bar moving down every few seconds. Retro-nostalgia requests stayed around 1% of generated sites in 2026, so it remains a niche rather than a trend.
nodes.why: Scoped to a single device-like surface it reads as a prop in the layout instead of a filter on the design.
nodes.implementation: .crt::before{content:'';position:absolute;inset:0;pointer-events:none;background:repeating-linear-gradient(0deg,rgba(0,0,0,.18) 0 1px,transparent 1px 3px)} .crt{box-shadow:inset 0 0 80px rgba(0,0,0,.6)} .crt code{text-shadow:-1px 0 rgba(255,0,0,.4),1px 0 rgba(0,255,255,.4)}.
nodes.pitfalls: Full-page scanlines plus glitch text plus neon green is the 'hacker template'; limit it to one framed element.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Full-page CRT and glitch effects are a generated-aesthetic cluster; a single scoped CRT panel inside an otherwise calm layout is acceptable.

nodes.name: Scroll drives a 3D camera path
nodes.what: A 500vh or 900vh container (no pin) whose scroll progress scrubs a GSAP timeline of camera keyframes: scrub 1 for the main timeline, 0.8 for typographic overlays and 0.5 for chapter cues; custom eases 'cinematicSilk' (0.45, 0.05, 0.55, 0.95), 'cinematicSmooth' (0.25, 0.1, 0.25, 1) and 'cinematicFlow' (0.33, 0, 0.2, 1); FOV 45, DPR capped at 2, ScrollSmoother smooth 4; text chapters slide ±100px over 0.2 to 0.6s with 0.02 SplitText stagger and 0.5 to 1s holds. A cylinder of images rotates +=28.27 linearly while the camera eases. Reactive Depth's image tube adds inertia: velocity += deltaY × 0.004 clamped ±2, eased at 0.12, decaying 0.92 per frame, hover slowing time to 0.35.
nodes.why: Linear object motion against eased camera moves is what makes the sequence feel filmed rather than scrubbed.
nodes.implementation: Three.js + GSAP ScrollTrigger scrub; static stand-in: .ring{transform-style:preserve-3d;animation:spin linear both;animation-timeline:scroll()} .ring img{transform:rotateY(calc(var(--i)*30deg)) translateZ(40vw)}.
nodes.pitfalls: 900vh of scroll with a model that barely moves is a hostage situation; each 100vh should produce a visible shot change.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Generated pages cannot author camera paths; a CSS-only ring of images rotated by a scroll timeline is the honest static stand-in.

nodes.name: One canvas mirrors DOM text
nodes.what: A single fixed full-screen WebGL canvas sits behind the page; real text and images stay in the DOM at opacity 0 (so they remain selectable, indexable and readable by screen readers) and are painted onto planes using their computed styles. Each plane measures getBoundingClientRect once on mount and resize and only subtracts scroll each frame; Lenis updates in the frame loop's update step and the render happens in postRender so there is no lag. Effects (ripple, pixelation, lens with dispersion, fluid distortion) are material swaps. Decorative text at 45vw and 18vw with −0.1em and −0.08em tracking; TextRoll stagger 0.05; footer parallax y −50%→0.
nodes.why: One context, one measurement pass and DOM-first content give WebGL typography without the SEO, a11y or memory cost of per-element canvases.
nodes.implementation: R3F or vanilla Three.js: FOV = 2·atan((innerHeight/2)/cameraZ) so world units equal CSS px; PlaneGeometry scaled to rect width/height; uniforms uQuadSize, uBorderRadius from computed style.
nodes.pitfalls: Measuring every frame (autoReflow) for all elements kills performance; only opt in elements moved by transforms.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Architecture-level craft; nothing like it ships from a generator.

nodes.name: Dotted WebGL globe, 5KB
nodes.what: A rotating dotted globe via COBE (about 5KB, zero dependencies): createGlobe(canvas, {devicePixelRatio: 2, phi, theta: 0.2, dark: 0 or 1, diffuse: 1.2, mapSamples: 16000, mapBrightness: 6, baseColor, markerColor, glowColor, markers}) with phi incremented per frame for rotation and optional drag; Globestudio and R3F variants add arcs and anchored DOM labels.
nodes.why: A sampled dot map matches a typographic or monochrome system better than a photoreal earth.
nodes.implementation: import createGlobe from 'https://esm.sh/cobe'; let phi=0; createGlobe(canvas,{devicePixelRatio:2,width:600,height:600,phi:0,theta:.2,dark:1,diffuse:1.2,mapSamples:16000,mapBrightness:6,baseColor:[.3,.3,.3],markerColor:[1,.5,.1],glowColor:[1,1,1],markers:[],onRender:s=>{s.phi=phi+=.005}}).
nodes.pitfalls: The globe with glowing arcs is the single most generated infra hero of 2023 to 2025; use it only when the markers are real locations and consider a flat dotted map instead.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Globe heroes are a strong AI and template tell; COBE's sampled-dot look is the least offensive version but still recognisable.

nodes.name: Shader text bulges near pointer
nodes.what: Text rendered as a black PNG texture on a PlaneGeometry(15, 15, 100, 100); the vertex shader lifts vertices toward the camera up to 1.0 units when within min_distance 3.0 of the raycast hit point, eased with easeInOutCubic over a remapped 0 to 1 distance; a second blurred, semi-transparent copy acts as a shadow whose alpha fades with the same distance. Motion.dev's examples list similar 'TSL particle morph' and 'shader lens' text pieces.
nodes.why: The shadow plane sells the lift as physical, so a flat headline becomes embossed paper under the finger.
nodes.implementation: ShaderMaterial with uDisplacement vec3 set from raycaster.intersectObject(hitPlane); vertex: float d=distance(worldPos.xyz,uDisplacement); pos.z += ease(map(d,0.,3.,1.,0.)) * 1.0.
nodes.pitfalls: Texture text is not real text; keep an accessible heading in the DOM and treat the plane as decoration.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Bespoke shader work, not template output.

nodes.name: Custom-shaped cursor trail field
nodes.what: Instead of a round smear, the cursor paints into a 200 × 200 float data texture (R,G store flow direction, B speed) with brushes defined as envelope × pattern: a hatch brush with 6 repeats and 0.44 thickness, a dot grid, or any PNG alpha; cells decay by decay^(dt × 60) each frame, warp strength 1.5 displaces the text or image behind, and speed maps to a red-yellow-orange ramp with a white core on fast strokes. Reduced motion shows a still frame of the source text.
nodes.why: A brush with structure (hatching, dots) turns a generic trail into a mark-making tool that can carry brand texture.
nodes.implementation: Three.js WebGPU + TSL: DataTexture FloatType NearestFilter, deposit loop limited to brush radius, 3×3 Gaussian in shader, uv += flow × 1.5 × strength.
nodes.pitfalls: Re-uploading the grid every frame is fine at 200² but not at 1000²; keep the field small and let the shader blur it.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Bespoke WebGPU work.

nodes.name: Gestures commit on release
nodes.what: Drag and swipe rules from Rauno Freiberg's essay: lightweight actions (open search) may trigger mid-swipe once a distance is reached, but destructive ones (dismiss, delete) wait until the finger lifts even past the threshold so the user can reverse; a peek may snap into view but commits only on release; a pinch applies scale immediately and animates only past a threshold; back-swipes must be able to interrupt an in-flight slide-in. Dismissals keep the gesture's momentum and angle instead of snapping to a fixed path.
nodes.why: Reversibility until release removes fear from gestures, which is why users trust native sheets and distrust most web ones.
nodes.implementation: pointermove sets transform directly (no transition); pointerup decides commit from distance OR velocity (px/ms) and then applies transition .5s cubic-bezier(.32,.72,0,1); pointercancel reverts.
nodes.pitfalls: Using CSS keyframes for the enter animation makes it uninterruptible; drive gesture-linked motion with transitions or WAAPI you can cancel.
nodes.ai_tell_note: A behavioural quality, invisible in screenshots, and absent from generated code which usually animates with keyframes.

nodes.name: No motion for frequent actions
nodes.what: Actions a user performs dozens of times a day (command menu, tab switch via keyboard, right-click menu) open instantly with no entrance animation; feedback moves to a micro cue such as macOS's menu item flashing the accent colour on selection before the menu fades. Raycast is the cited product with no animations; Vercel's dashboard tab animation was moved from JS to CSS because it dropped frames during loads.
nodes.why: Removing animation from repeated actions makes the whole product feel faster without changing a single network call.
nodes.implementation: [data-frequent] .popover{transition:none} .item:active{animation:flash .12s steps(2)} @keyframes flash{50%{background:transparent}}.
nodes.pitfalls: Removing all motion also removes the confirmation cue; keep a 100 to 160ms press feedback or a flash.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Generated UIs animate every popover identically; selective stillness is a product-design decision.

nodes.name: Reduced motion swaps, not removes
nodes.what: Under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce, each motion gets a calmer equivalent rather than nothing: a 0.2s bounce becomes a 0.2s fade, a pixel page transition becomes a plain fade, a looping 3D portrait swap is turned off while the one-time intro fade still plays, a WebGL cursor trail shows a still frame of the text, scroll-driven reveals keep the finished state in base styles and put the hidden start state inside @media (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference) so nothing is ever invisible.
nodes.why: Users who opt out of motion still get state changes communicated, and nothing depends on an animation that never runs.
nodes.implementation: @media (prefers-reduced-motion:no-preference){.r{opacity:0;animation:…}} @media (prefers-reduced-motion:reduce){.bounce{animation:fade .2s ease-out}} and matchMedia checks before initialising Lenis or WebGL loops.
nodes.pitfalls: The common failure is opacity:0 in base styles with the reveal animation disabled, leaving blank sections.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Invisible to most viewers but a reliable marker of handmade work when inspected.

nodes.name: Line minimap for long pages
nodes.what: A vertical strip of thin horizontal lines fixed to the page edge, one per section or heading, where the current line is longer or brighter and the strip scrolls with you; hovering a line reveals its label and clicking jumps there. Rauno's 'Minimap' craft piece and the 'Line Minimap' prototype in Devouring Details are the references; the essay also proposes scroll landmarks (double-tap the scrollbar to drop a return point).
nodes.why: It gives spatial memory to a long narrative page without a sticky table of contents stealing width.
nodes.implementation: <nav class=mm> with one <a> per section; IntersectionObserver toggles aria-current; .mm a{display:block;height:1px;width:12px;background:currentColor;margin:6px 0;transition:width .2s cubic-bezier(.23,1,.32,1)} .mm a[aria-current]{width:28px}.
nodes.pitfalls: Dozens of lines with no labels is decoration; cap at the section count and show labels on hover or focus.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Generated pages use dots-on-the-right carousels or nothing; a labelled line minimap is a product-craft device.
avoid_words: pages with a progress bar already

nodes.name: Blur-to-sharp text entrance
nodes.what: Text enters by animating filter: blur(8px) to 0 together with opacity and a small translate, per word or per line with a short stagger; Rauno's 'Blur Reveal' (2024) popularised it and it now ships in many Framer templates. Because filter is expensive, it should be limited to a few words at a time and skipped on low-end devices.
nodes.why: Focus pulling is a camera metaphor people read instantly, so it feels cinematic even at 300ms.
nodes.implementation: .w{animation:bl .5s cubic-bezier(.23,1,.32,1) both;animation-delay:calc(var(--i)*.04s)} @keyframes bl{from{filter:blur(8px);opacity:0;translate:0 4px}}.
nodes.pitfalls: Blurring a whole paragraph in and out on scroll is now the signature of AI-tool landing pages; if used at all, one hero line, once.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Blur-in word reveals (often with a gradient 'shimmer') are a top 2025 to 2026 generated-landing tell.

nodes.name: Split-flap board numerals
nodes.what: A countdown or stat shown as split-flap tiles: each digit is a top and bottom half; on change the top half tips forward (rotateX) carrying the old digit on its front and the new one on its back, casts a shadow on the half below, a catch-light fades as it lands, and it overshoots slightly before settling; tiles have separate colours for halves, seam and hinge, tabular numerals prevent jitter, role=timer with muted live updates, and the animation runs only while in view. Pure CSS 3D transforms, no canvas.
nodes.why: The mechanical flap is a trusted real-world display for departures and scores, which gives numbers authority.
nodes.implementation: .flap{perspective:400px} .top{transform-origin:bottom;animation:tip .6s cubic-bezier(.34,1.3,.64,1)} @keyframes tip{to{transform:rotateX(-180deg)}} with ::after gradient shadow fading via opacity keyframes; font-variant-numeric:tabular-nums.
nodes.pitfalls: Announcing every second to screen readers is hostile; aria-live=off with a periodic polite summary.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Generated countdowns are plain numbers in boxes; a physically modelled flap is an uncommon build.

nodes.name: Enter screen with sound choice
nodes.what: An opening gate with two choices, 'Enter' and 'Enter without audio', the wordmark set letter-spaced, a loading state and a persistent 'Toggle Sound' control afterwards; interaction hints such as 'Click & Hold' and 'Drag to explore' appear as small labels near the cursor. Unseen's site is the reference.
nodes.why: Asking for consent to sound makes audio part of the experience instead of an ambush, and the gate doubles as the preloader.
nodes.implementation: <dialog open> with two buttons; audio.muted = choice; store in sessionStorage; dialog closes with clip-path inset wipe .8s cubic-bezier(.77,0,.175,1).
nodes.pitfalls: A gate in front of content that people need (pricing, docs) is a bounce machine; use only for experiential sites.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Generated sites never gate; this is an experiential-studio convention.

nodes.name: Rotating conic gradient border
nodes.what: A card border made from a conic-gradient whose angle is a registered custom property (@property --a with syntax '<angle>') animated 0 to 360deg, masked to a 1px ring with padding-box/border-box backgrounds; often combined with a glow. Baseline since July 2024.
nodes.why: Registered properties let the browser interpolate the angle, so the border rotates smoothly without JS.
nodes.implementation: @property --a{syntax:'<angle>';inherits:false;initial-value:0deg} .c{border:1px solid transparent;background:linear-gradient(var(--bg),var(--bg)) padding-box,conic-gradient(from var(--a),transparent 70%,var(--accent)) border-box;animation:r 3s linear infinite} @keyframes r{to{--a:360deg}}.
nodes.pitfalls: The spinning glowing border on a dark card is one of the most recognisable AI-generated UI elements of 2024 to 2026; use @property for other interpolations (gradient stops, hue) instead.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Included as a warning: the 'shimmer border' card is a strong generated-UI tell even though the underlying CSS feature is useful.

nodes.name: Pick one motion personality
nodes.what: Before animating, choose a motion personality with concrete ranges and apply it everywhere: 'press' (entrances 0.3 to 0.5s, sharp ease-out, no overshoot, tight staggers, exits faster than entrances), 'gallery' (0.8 to 1.2s, smooth ease-in-out, long staggers, mostly fades and masks) or 'kinetic poster' (bold, slight overshoot, springy settles). Every element gets an intro, a resting state and an outro; the masthead animates on first load only; animate the existing design rather than restyling it; remove exhibits that do not earn their place.
nodes.why: A single named personality is what makes a site's motion feel authored instead of a pile of effects from different tutorials.
nodes.implementation: Define tokens once: --ease-press: cubic-bezier(.16,1,.3,1); --t-press: .4s; --ease-gallery: cubic-bezier(.65,0,.35,1); --t-gallery: 1s; use only those tokens site-wide.
nodes.pitfalls: Choosing 'kinetic' for a saas product or 'gallery' for a dev tool mismatches audience expectations; match personality to product type first.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Generated motion is uniform fade-up; a consistent personality with distinct intro/outro is a design decision.
avoid_words: mixing spring overshoot with slow gallery fades on one page

nodes.name: Fragment-stacked hero statement
nodes.what: The studio descriptor is broken into one word or fragment per line and revealed in stages (Locomotive: Digital / Digital-First / Digital-First Design; Immersive Garden: Innovative / digital / experiences / studio; Significa: Think. Design. Develop. Launch. Scale.). No image, no buttons, text fills roughly 60 to 80 percent of the viewport width, left aligned.
nodes.why: The line breaks become the composition, so the hero reads as typeset rather than templated.
nodes.implementation: h1 with display:grid; each line a span; text-wrap:balance off, max-inline-size in ch per line; staged reveal with animation-delay per span or a scroll-driven animation-timeline.
nodes.pitfalls: Breaking lines with br tags instead of an explicit max-inline-size makes the composition collapse on other viewports.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Generated heroes centre a sentence and add two CTAs; a left-set stack of single words with no CTA is a designer move.

nodes.name: Imperative manifesto list
nodes.what: A short vertical list of imperative lines that act as the hero and the values page at once. rauno.me runs seven: Make it fast / beautiful / consistent / carefully / timeless / soulful / Make it. Each line is a plain paragraph at body size, generous line height, nothing else on screen.
nodes.why: Repetition with one changing word gives rhythm without any visual device.
nodes.implementation: ol with list-style:none; each li in text-wrap:pretty; optional ::before counter in a mono font; no animation needed.
nodes.pitfalls: More than about eight lines or any adjective-heavy line turns it into a slogan wall.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Generated copy avoids repetition and pads with adjectives; terse repeated imperatives read as authored.

nodes.name: Name, role, two-line bio hero
nodes.what: Portfolio opens with the person's name at roughly 20 to 28px (not display size), role on the next line, then a two-sentence bio naming current and past employers (emilkowal.ski: Design Engineer, formerly Linear and Vercel; paco.me: webmaster at Linear; benji.org adds a last-updated date). One column around 60ch, nothing else above the fold.
nodes.why: The restraint signals confidence and lets the project list do the talking.
nodes.implementation: main{max-inline-size:60ch;padding-block:20vh} h1{font-size:1.25rem;font-weight:500} p{text-wrap:pretty}; subset fonts via unicode-range.
nodes.pitfalls: Looks unfinished if type pairing and measure are not immaculate; it depends on a good body face (paco.me ships Söhne, Newsreader and Inter subsets).
nodes.ai_tell_note: Generated portfolios make the name huge and add an avatar and social buttons; small name plus prose bio is the opposite.

nodes.name: Split-letter staggered headline
nodes.what: Headline letters or words are wrapped individually and revealed with a stagger from a masked line (Dogstudio: We Make Good Shit arrives letter by letter; Lando Norris uses split-type on ON / TRACK with dash underlines; OkayDev ships SplitText). Typical stagger 20 to 40ms per character, 600 to 900ms total, ease-out expo.
nodes.why: Motion is confined to typography so the page feels crafted without needing imagery.
nodes.implementation: Wrap chars in span with overflow:hidden parent line; translateY(110%) to 0 with animation-delay:calc(var(--i)*30ms); CSS-only with @property counters or GSAP SplitText.
nodes.pitfalls: Splitting breaks screen readers and hyphenation unless the original text stays in an aria-label or a visually hidden copy.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Common in agency work since 2019 and now in libraries; still rarely produced by generators, which fade whole blocks.

nodes.name: Live next-event card in hero
nodes.what: A small card anchored in the hero shows the next dated event (Lando Norris: Next Race, Mexico GP, linking to the calendar). It sits at a corner of the hero, mono or small-caps label, one line of content, arrow link.
nodes.why: Gives a static hero a reason to be revisited and proves the site is maintained.
nodes.implementation: aside positioned with anchor positioning relative to the hero heading (position-anchor) or inset in a grid cell; time element with datetime attribute; mono label via font-variant-caps.
nodes.pitfalls: Dead if the date passes without an update; render from data with a fallback state.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Generators do not invent time-bound components; they produce evergreen marketing blocks.

nodes.name: Bracketed or numbered eyebrow labels
nodes.what: Section eyebrows are set inside square brackets or with two-digit indices: Lama Lama uses [ Featured work ] and [ Who we are ]; Unseen numbers its nav 01 Index, 02 Projects, 03 Contact, 04 World; Akaru and Huge number service blocks 01 to 05 or 01 to 06. Small size (11 to 13px), tracking +0.05em, often mono.
nodes.why: Reads like a technical document or film slate and gives hierarchy without colour.
nodes.implementation: span.eyebrow::before{content:'[ '} ::after{content:' ]'} or counter-reset on the section list with counter(section, decimal-leading-zero).
nodes.pitfalls: Numbering everything turns the page into a table of contents; number one axis only.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Mono eyebrows alone are now a known generated look; the brackets and the real sequential numbering of content are less common.

nodes.name: Enter gate with audio choice
nodes.what: An intro screen blocks the site with a single decision: Unseen shows a stacked U N S E E N wordmark, the tagline, and two buttons, Enter and Enter without audio; Siena Film Foundation uses an ENTER button on a cinema ticket (ADMIT ONE 004); Bruno Simon loads into a game HUD.
nodes.why: Turning the loading wait into a consent moment makes sound and motion feel intentional rather than imposed.
nodes.implementation: dialog element open on load with two buttons; store the choice in sessionStorage; prefers-reduced-motion skips the gate; the stacked wordmark via writing-mode:vertical-lr or one letter per grid row.
nodes.pitfalls: A gate on a site people visit to read is hostile; only use when the experience really has audio.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Generated sites never block entry; this is a deliberate experiential choice.

nodes.name: Preloader with a copy joke
nodes.what: The percentage loader carries brand voice: Don't Board Me reads bounce a ball to get to the site, loading 0%; Lando Norris shows Load Norris; Son Daven writes Loading the website / Please wait / 0%. Big mono counter, one line of copy, solid brand colour background, exits with a wipe.
nodes.why: The first 1.5 seconds set tone, and a line of voice does more than a spinner.
nodes.implementation: Fixed overlay; counter via @property --n integer animated to 100 with counter-reset: n var(--n) and content:counter(n); exit with clip-path:inset(0 0 100% 0) transition 600ms.
nodes.pitfalls: A fake counter that runs on a timer rather than real asset progress is noticed; keep it under 1.5s or skip when cached.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Generators do not write preloaders at all, and when asked they produce a spinner.

nodes.name: Multilingual greeting intro
nodes.what: Intro overlay cycles greetings in several scripts before revealing the page (dennissnellenberg.com: Hello, Bonjour, Ciao, Hallå and more, each around 150 to 200ms, then the panel slides up with a curved SVG bottom edge).
nodes.why: Signals an international practice in under two seconds and gives the preloader content.
nodes.implementation: Array of strings swapped on a 180ms interval, then translateY(-100%) on the overlay with an SVG path at its base; respect prefers-reduced-motion.
nodes.pitfalls: This exact device has been cloned in hundreds of tutorial portfolios since 2022, so it now reads as borrowed.
nodes.ai_tell_note: It is the most copied portfolio intro of the decade and appears in template kits; generators reproduce it from tutorials.

nodes.name: Rotate-device prompt as a stance
nodes.what: Instead of a responsive layout, some experiential sites show a full-screen instruction: Lando Norris says Please rotate your device, this is a vertical drive (locking portrait); Siena Film Foundation and Niccolò Miranda ask to rotate to landscape; Son Daven says Rotate your phone for better experience.
nodes.why: Owning one orientation lets the main layout be a single composed canvas.
nodes.implementation: @media (orientation: landscape) and (max-height: 500px) show a fixed overlay with the instruction; everything else aria-hidden while it shows.
nodes.pitfalls: It is a refusal to do responsive work; only acceptable when the experience truly needs the aspect ratio.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Generated output is always dutifully responsive; a prompt like this only appears when a human made a call.

nodes.name: Menu word toggle to full overlay
nodes.what: Header shows a wordmark, one CTA (Let's talk) and the word Menu, which swaps to Close and opens a full-screen panel listing four or five links in display type plus newsletter, socials and office addresses (Lusion, Dogstudio Toggle menu, 14islands Menu/close, Era Residence, Koto). No hamburger icon, no desktop link row.
nodes.why: Keeps the hero clean and turns navigation into a designed moment with large type and metadata.
nodes.implementation: button[aria-expanded] toggling a popover or dialog; overlay links at clamp(2.5rem,8vw,7rem); open with clip-path:inset(0 0 100% 0) to inset(0) over 700ms; links stagger 60ms each.
nodes.pitfalls: Hiding five links behind a word on desktop costs a click; justify it with what the overlay adds (addresses, time, featured image).
nodes.ai_tell_note: Generated navs are a horizontal link row with a primary button; a text toggle and an overlay with office metadata is studio behaviour.

nodes.name: Nav items with descriptors
nodes.what: Each overlay menu link carries a short secondary line: Koto pairs Work with Explore case studies and Contact with Reach out; Mouthwash and Pentagram use descriptive sublabels in filters. Display link at 40 to 80px, descriptor at 12 to 14px in a muted colour, right aligned or on the next line.
nodes.why: Turns a list of nouns into an index page and fills the overlay without decoration.
nodes.implementation: li display:grid; grid-template-columns:1fr auto; a span.desc{font-size:.8rem;color:color-mix(in oklch,currentColor 55%,transparent)}.
nodes.pitfalls: Descriptors that just restate the label (About: learn about us) are noise.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Generators output bare link labels.

nodes.name: Local time in nav or footer
nodes.what: A live clock pinned to the studio's timezone: Obys shows CET 00:00 AM in header and footer; dennissnellenberg.com shows 09:41 PM CET next to Located in the Netherlands; Koto's studio tabs each carry a --:-- time; benji.org signs off 12:00am in Los Angeles, California.
nodes.why: Implies a real place and real people without a photo.
nodes.implementation: time element updated every 1000ms with Intl.DateTimeFormat timeZone; font-variant-numeric:tabular-nums so digits do not jitter.
nodes.pitfalls: Shows --:-- or wrong time if JS fails; render a server time first.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Appeared in enough portfolio tutorials that it is semi-generic; still rare in generated drafts.
avoid_words: global SaaS with no place identity

nodes.name: Sound toggle as a nav primitive
nodes.what: A persistent Sound On / Off control sits in the header next to Menu: Dogstudio and Unseen label it Toggle sound; Immersive Garden renders 0 / Off / On and themes it with --sound-color flipping between #000 and #e8e8e8; Lusion exposes PLAY and MUTE; Josh Comeau offers Disable sounds for UI clicks.
nodes.why: Makes audio a first-class, reversible choice rather than a surprise.
nodes.implementation: button[aria-pressed] with a 3-bar equaliser drawn in CSS (animation paused when off); state persisted in localStorage; Web Audio only after user gesture.
nodes.pitfalls: Autoplaying audio before the toggle is touched is blocked by browsers and hated by users.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Generators never add audio controls.

nodes.name: Click-to-copy email with Copied state
nodes.what: The contact link copies the address instead of opening a mail client and swaps its label to Copied for about 1.5s (rauno.me, mouthwash.studio on both hello@ and careers@, Koto's Say Hello with a Copy option).
nodes.why: Most people paste addresses into webmail; the micro state is a tiny proof of care.
nodes.implementation: a[href^=mailto] click -> navigator.clipboard.writeText; toggle data-copied and swap text via ::after content; revert after 1500ms.
nodes.pitfalls: Removing the mailto entirely strands users without clipboard permission; keep the href and intercept on click.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Generators produce a mailto link or a contact form.

nodes.name: Vertical / Horizontal / Grid view switch
nodes.what: The work index offers the same data in different layouts: Obys exposes Vertical, Horizontal, Grid; Uncut.wtf toggles Grid and List with per-category counts (Sans 66, Serif 27, Mono 23, Display 47); OkayDev lets profiles switch Classic and Bento layouts.
nodes.why: Gives the visitor agency and shows the system underneath the design.
nodes.implementation: Radio group writing data-view on the list; CSS switches grid-template via :has(#view-grid:checked); view-transition-name on items so reflow animates.
nodes.pitfalls: Three views of nine projects is overkill; needs 15 plus items to feel earned.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Generators pick one grid.

nodes.name: Work filter by industry and discipline
nodes.what: Two independent filter axes over the project list: Pentagram splits Discipline (Books, Brand Identity, Typefaces) and Sector (Arts and Culture, Technology, Health); Mouthwash filters by Industry (Art, Architecture, Technology, Health, Sport, Fashion, Beauty, Sustainability); Unseen offers All, Branding, Digital, Motion, Experiment; Instrument all / brand / marketing / product.
nodes.why: Turns a portfolio into a searchable archive and signals volume of work.
nodes.implementation: Plain text buttons with counts in parentheses; filtering via data attributes and :has or a tiny script; counts rendered server-side.
nodes.pitfalls: Filters that leave empty states on most combinations expose a thin archive.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Generated work sections show six cards and no filters.

nodes.name: AI agent guidance link in footer
nodes.what: A 2026 footer item that links to machine-readable guidance: darkroom.engineering lists Agent guidance alongside Site map and Privacy; Build in Amsterdam links Guidance for AI agents (llms.txt). Set in the same small utility row as legal links.
nodes.why: Acknowledges non-human readers and marks the studio as current without a banner.
nodes.implementation: a[href='/llms.txt'] in the footer utility list; serve a plain text file with site structure and contact.
nodes.pitfalls: Linking to an llms.txt that is empty or stale is worse than none.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Ironically a human decision; generators do not add it.

nodes.name: Year-grouped archive index
nodes.what: All work listed under year headings in reverse order instead of a curated six: Phantom groups 93 projects from 2026 back to 2016, each row with title, client, lowercase tags and one line; Maxime Heckel groups posts by year 2026 to 2018 with short dates; Order groups news under full dates like 13 May, 2026.
nodes.why: Volume and longevity become the argument, and the structure costs nothing visually.
nodes.implementation: section per year with a sticky h2 (position:sticky;top:0) in a two-column grid: year left, rows right; rows are a dl or table with tabular-nums dates.
nodes.pitfalls: A year heading with one entry under it looks worse than no grouping.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Generated portfolios show a fixed small grid of featured items.

nodes.name: Index rows with number, tags, and status
nodes.what: Projects as table-like rows rather than cards: Obys gives each a two-digit index 01 to 19, a category (Architecture, Fashion) and service tags (Creative Direction, Web Design/Dev); Blond tiles show discipline plus a year or a status word like Confidential or Coming Soon; Dennis Snellenberg lists discipline and year and a More work count of 11.
nodes.why: Metadata becomes texture, and the eye scans like a catalogue.
nodes.implementation: ul with grid-template-columns: 3ch 1fr auto auto; border-block-end 1px color-mix(in oklch, currentColor 15%, transparent); counter for the index.
nodes.pitfalls: Rows without a hover image or thumbnail can feel like a spreadsheet; pair with a preview.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Generated work sections are three or six cards with rounded images and a button each.

nodes.name: Plain-text client roster instead of logo wall
nodes.what: Clients as a comma-separated run of linked names in body type rather than a logo strip: basement.studio lists about 40 names (SpaceX AI, Vercel, Linear, Cursor, MrBeast) inline; Instrument prints a plain-text roster; Area 17 names five clients next to We partner with.
nodes.why: Reads as a sentence, avoids logo-size negotiations, and the names carry more than grey marks.
nodes.implementation: p with inline links separated by commas via li::after{content:', '}; text-wrap:pretty; hyphens:none.
nodes.pitfalls: Alphabetical order looks like a legal disclosure; order by recency or weight.
nodes.ai_tell_note: The logo wall (often a marquee) is the generated default.

nodes.name: Hover swaps the still
nodes.what: Grid tiles carry two images and swap on hover without zoom or overlay: Lando Norris helmet cards swap base to hover image with season, theme and year labels; Oliver Dupuy toggles single landscape frames (via hoverstat.es listing). Swap is instant or under 150ms.
nodes.why: A second frame says more than a scale transform and feels like a contact sheet.
nodes.implementation: figure with two img stacked in grid-area:1/1; img:nth-child(2){opacity:0} figure:hover img:nth-child(2){opacity:1} transition 120ms; preload the second via loading=eager within viewport.
nodes.pitfalls: No touch equivalent; show the second image on tap or in the detail page.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Generated cards use scale and shadow on hover.

nodes.name: Mixed-aspect tile grid
nodes.what: Thumbnails alternate landscape and portrait in one grid rather than being cropped square: Lama Lama alternates 1200x800 and 960x1200; Blond mixes portrait and landscape tiles; Félix Péault shows 11 frames of differing ratios; Kai Blamey Nguyen runs from 16:9 to wider and squarer.
nodes.why: Respects the work's native frame and breaks the card rhythm.
nodes.implementation: grid-template-columns:repeat(12,1fr); tiles span 4 or 5 columns with aspect-ratio 3/2 or 4/5; grid-auto-flow:dense.
nodes.pitfalls: Pure masonry (random heights) reads as Pinterest; keep two or three fixed ratios and a strict column grid.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Generated grids force aspect-ratio 16/9 or 1/1 on everything.

nodes.name: Projects titled as sentences
nodes.what: Each project is introduced by a short claim rather than a client name: Koto pairs Instagram with A new mark with old memories (2026, Social Media); Antinomy lists i-D, Vast, Gemini and Waabi as sentence-style headlines; Phantom opens case studies with a provocation like Earth is so 2020.
nodes.why: Reads as editorial and tells the visitor what the studio thinks, not just who paid.
nodes.implementation: article h3 sentence at 1.5 to 2.5rem; client, year and sector in a small dl beneath; text-wrap:balance on the h3.
nodes.pitfalls: Every sentence needs a real idea; generic ones (Elevating the brand) are worse than a client name.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Generated titles are Client Name + Website Redesign.

nodes.name: Custom or renamed studio typeface
nodes.what: The studio ships a face under its own name: Locomotive loads PPLocomotiveNew-Light (a Pangram Pangram collaboration) with HelveticaNowDisplay as the secondary; Obys loads ObysSans4.woff2; Dennis Snellenberg declares the family Dennis Sans (files are Neue Montreal); Order serves its own foundry faces (Haltung, Plebeian, Sita Serif, Sita Sans, Stringer, Spades, Pastiche Grotesque, Etude, Vanity).
nodes.why: Owning the typeface, or at least naming it, is the clearest signal of an authored identity.
nodes.implementation: @font-face{font-family:'Studio Sans';src:url(studio.woff2) format('woff2');font-display:swap;size-adjust:...} and expose as --font-display; subset with unicode-range.
nodes.pitfalls: Renaming a licensed font does not change its licence; and a weak custom face is worse than a good licensed one.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Generated CSS reaches for Inter, Space Grotesk or Instrument Serif; a named studio family is the opposite tell.

nodes.name: Grotesk plus real text serif
nodes.what: A neutral grotesk for UI and a true text serif (not an italic accent word) for long copy or pull quotes: Mouthwash pairs Suisse BP Intl Antique with Suisse Works; Build in Amsterdam pairs NHaas Grotesk TX Pro with Reckless Neue Book; Collins uses Graphik with Portrait Text; Immersive Garden uses Helvetica Neue with PS Times; Unseen uses Neue Montreal with Saol Display Light Italic; dia.studio sets JJannon Book.
nodes.why: The serif carries reading and quotation, the grotesk carries wayfinding, and neither is decorative.
nodes.implementation: --font-ui: 'Suisse Intl', system-ui; --font-text: 'Suisse Works', Georgia; blockquote, .lede, article p use --font-text at 1.125 to 1.25rem with line-height 1.45.
nodes.pitfalls: Using the serif only for one italic word per headline is the 2024 generated look; use it for whole paragraphs, quotes or the case-study body.
nodes.ai_tell_note: The generated version is sans headline with one italic serif word; whole-text serif usage with a quality grotesk reads as designed.

nodes.name: Condensed or slab display headline
nodes.what: A characterful display face for headlines only, with a plain grotesk for everything else: Don't Board Me sets Bayon (tall condensed) over Neue Montreal; Lando Norris sets Brier Bold over Mona Sans Variable; Dogstudio sets GT Sectra Display over Gilroy and Heebo; Siena sets Neue Brucke over NB International with P22 Parrish Roman for accents.
nodes.why: One loud face at display sizes gives a brand a voice while the body stays legible.
nodes.implementation: h1{font-family:var(--font-display);font-size:clamp(3rem,12vw,11rem);line-height:.9;letter-spacing:-.01em;text-transform:uppercase}.
nodes.pitfalls: Condensed faces need tight line-height (0.85 to 0.95) and letter-spacing tweaks or they look like a default install.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Generators pick Space Grotesk or Syne when asked for character; a licensed condensed or slab face with tuned leading is not in their repertoire.

nodes.name: Light display weight at huge size
nodes.what: Headlines set in a 300 weight at 80 to 160px rather than bold: Exo Ape runs Lausanne 300 as its primary face on #0D0E13 and sand #E0CCBB; Locomotive loads PP Locomotive New Light; Unseen uses Saol Display Light and Light Italic; Immersive Garden uses Helvetica Neue Light for the stacked hero.
nodes.why: Light strokes at scale feel expensive and leave room for imagery behind.
nodes.implementation: h1{font-weight:300;font-size:clamp(3.5rem,10vw,10rem);letter-spacing:-.02em;line-height:1} ensure the variable font axis wght 300 is loaded.
nodes.pitfalls: Below 40px the hairline disappears; use a heavier weight for body and never for buttons.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Generated headlines default to 700 or 800 weight with tight tracking.

nodes.name: Mono reserved for real metadata
nodes.what: A monospace face used only for data that is actually data: Lama Lama sets Sometype Mono for labels beside Suisse BP Intl; OkayDev sets Aeonik Mono; Anime.js uses Berkeley Mono for code and Digital-7 for a counter readout; makingsoftware.com uses the system ui-monospace stack; jhey.dev prints Rev 567a34c.
nodes.why: Mono signals measurement; reserving it for counts, times, hashes and tags keeps that signal honest.
nodes.implementation: --font-mono: 'Berkeley Mono', ui-monospace; .meta{font-family:var(--font-mono);font-size:.75rem;font-variant-numeric:tabular-nums;letter-spacing:.02em}.
nodes.pitfalls: Mono eyebrows on every section with no real data behind them is now a recognised generated look.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Mono labels are a 2024 to 2025 AI tell when decorative; they read as designed when the content is genuinely numeric or system-generated.

nodes.name: Build metadata in the footer
nodes.what: Footer prints information about the site itself: jhey.dev shows © 2026 Jhey and Rev 567a34c; Maxime Heckel renders a debug panel with commit hash, browser, time and dimensions; benji.org leads with last updated Aug 22, 2026; lynnandtonic.com labels the design v. XIX; Brittany Chiang states the site is set in Inter and built with Next.js.
nodes.why: Treats the site as a maintained artefact and gives a nerdy, specific texture.
nodes.implementation: Build step writes GIT_SHA and date into a data attribute; footer small element in --font-mono with tabular-nums.
nodes.pitfalls: Fake hashes or a hard-coded date defeat the point; inject at build.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Generated footers are copyright plus social icons.

nodes.name: Giant closing statement footer
nodes.what: The footer opens with one display-size sentence before the link columns: Lando Norris ends with Always bringing the fight. beside a 360-degree helmet; Huge closes with Bye.; Lama Lama with Say no more. it's a match plus a phone number; Niccolò Miranda repeats Let's create something together three times with Email Me buttons; Dennis Snellenberg uses Let's work together with Get in touch.
nodes.why: Gives the page an ending instead of a sitemap and leaves the last impression in the brand voice.
nodes.implementation: footer>p.statement{font-size:clamp(2.5rem,9vw,9rem);line-height:.95;text-wrap:balance} followed by a grid of link columns at .8rem.
nodes.pitfalls: Let's work together is now itself a cliché; the sentence has to be in the brand's own voice.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Generators do produce a CTA band, but centred with two buttons; a left-set, full-width sentence with an email and a time is still a studio signature.

nodes.name: Full stops on labels and names
nodes.what: Every label, client name and nav word ends in a period: Huge writes Work. Contact. Bye. and NBCU. CoinTracker. Google.; Significa's hero is Think. Design. Develop. Launch. Scale.; Collins closes headlines with periods (Learning to see.).
nodes.why: The period turns labels into statements and slows the reading pace.
nodes.implementation: Author it in content; optionally a::after{content:'.'} on nav links so the period inherits hover colour.
nodes.pitfalls: Inconsistent application (some labels with, some without) looks like a typo.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Generated labels are Title Case with no punctuation.

nodes.name: Lowercase navigation and CTAs
nodes.what: All nav labels, buttons and tags set in lowercase: Don't Board Me uses pricing, about us, services, blog, contacts and book now; Josh Comeau's nav reads categories, courses, goodies; Lando Norris runs lowercase label strips like mclaren f1 since 2019; Phantom lowercases project tags (3d, ai, motion).
nodes.why: Lowercase reads as casual and designed, and it distinguishes labels from headlines.
nodes.implementation: nav, .btn, .tag{text-transform:lowercase} with font-feature-settings for case-sensitive forms off.
nodes.pitfalls: Lowercasing proper nouns in body copy looks like an error; restrict to UI strings.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Generators use Title Case buttons and uppercase tracked eyebrows.

nodes.name: Emoji as punctuation in headings
nodes.what: Emoji inserted into section headings as a wink, not as icons: Locomotive labels sections with 🛑🚹🚺 and 🍺🔞; Josh Comeau titles The Future of CSS ✨; Don't Board Me names an element Our Services, Woof 🐶 and its 404 poooooooo 🐶💩. Used sparingly, one or two per page, in otherwise strict typography.
nodes.why: Breaks the seriousness of a disciplined layout and reads as human.
nodes.implementation: Plain text; wrap in span[role=img][aria-label] and set font-size:.8em so it does not inflate the line box.
nodes.pitfalls: Emoji as list bullets or one per feature card is the generated look; emoji inside a serious heading once is the opposite.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Generators overuse emoji as bullet icons; a single emoji embedded in disciplined typography reads as authored.

nodes.name: One neon on near-black plus bone
nodes.what: A single acid accent carried by a dark and a bone neutral rather than white: Lando Norris uses lime #D2FF00 on #111112 with cream #EFEFE5, dark green #282C20 and a secondary orange #FF6B00; darkroom.engineering sets --primary-color as oklch(0.5882 0.2334 27.96) red on oklch(0 0 0) black; Locomotive pairs #DA382E red and #312DFB blue with black and white.
nodes.why: One saturated colour against neutrals of different temperatures reads as a brand system, not a theme.
nodes.implementation: :root{--ink:#111112;--bone:#EFEFE5;--acid:#D2FF00;--deep:#282C20} use oklch() for derived tints: color-mix(in oklch, var(--acid) 20%, var(--ink)).
nodes.pitfalls: Neon on pure white vibrates; the bone or cream neutral is what makes it work.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Generated palettes pick a teal or violet brand colour with a gradient; a lime on near-black with a cream secondary neutral is a specific art direction.

nodes.name: Warm paper instead of white
nodes.what: Page background is a warm off-white measured in hex: Huge #F7F4EE, Collins #F8F8F7 with ink #140700, Build in Amsterdam #F2EFE6 with terracotta #C38133, Siena #FAF7EF, Exo Ape #E4E0DB and sand #E0CCBB, Anime.js #F6F4F2, Oryzo AI #FFEDD6, Don't Board Me #F3F3E9.
nodes.why: Warm neutrals read as print and photography stock, and they make black type feel softer without grey.
nodes.implementation: :root{--paper:#F7F4EE;--ink:#140700} body{background:var(--paper)} surfaces via color-mix(in oklch, var(--paper) 92%, var(--ink)).
nodes.pitfalls: Cards or inputs left pure white on a warm ground look like holes; tint every surface.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Generated backgrounds are #FFFFFF or a cool slate; a measured warm paper is a designer choice.
avoid_words: pure white cards on tinted background

nodes.name: Muddy retro five-colour palette
nodes.what: Five desaturated, slightly dirty brand colours used as full-bleed section fills: Don't Board Me runs red #E33529, olive #A7A238, yellow #FFF500, brown #854720, blue #2B6786 and pinks #F3C3CB and #F0B5BE on cream #F3F3E9; Dogstudio's accent set includes #FF4940, #D79A21, #00978C and #C80AFB on its project tiles.
nodes.why: Reads as 1970s print rather than a UI kit, and section colour changes do the pacing.
nodes.implementation: Section-scoped tokens: section[data-tone=olive]{--bg:#A7A238;--fg:#F3F3E9} with background:var(--bg) and color:var(--fg); buttons invert the pair.
nodes.pitfalls: Five colours need a strict rule for which carries text; test contrast per pairing, not per colour.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Generators pick one brand colour and a neutral scale; a muddy multi-colour set with section fills is a hand-built identity.

nodes.name: Named near-black and off-white pair
nodes.what: Dark sites avoid #000 and #FFF: Exo Ape #0D0E13 with #F8F8F8; Dennis Snellenberg #1C1D20 with #FFFFFF and a warm #E0D9D1; paco.me #1C1C1C; OkayDev #0C0C0C with #121212 surfaces; Immersive Garden #030303 with #E8E8E8 text; Koto #141414; Blond #1D1717 with #F9F9F9 in light mode.
nodes.why: A tinted near-black reads as material rather than void and keeps white text from glaring.
nodes.implementation: :root{--ink:#0D0E13;--text:#E8E8E8} prefer oklch(0.14 0.005 260) so tints derive consistently; meta theme-color per prefers-color-scheme.
nodes.pitfalls: Too blue a tint (#0F172A slate) is the Tailwind default and reads as generated.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Generated dark modes use slate-900 or pure black; a warm or neutral #0D0E13 style near-black with an #E8E8E8 text colour is tuned by hand.

nodes.name: Perceptual colour tokens in CSS
nodes.what: Colour systems declared in hsl, oklch or color-mix rather than hex ramps: Josh Comeau defines --color-action: hsl(240deg 95% 62%) and alpha variants like hsl(52deg 100% 50% / 0.25); darkroom.engineering sets --primary-color in oklch and theme-color as oklch(0 0 0); OkayDev derives --app-chrome-bg with color-mix(in srgb, ...).
nodes.why: Derived tints stay consistent across light and dark and the code reads as a system.
nodes.implementation: :root{--accent:oklch(0.59 0.23 28)} .tint{background:color-mix(in oklch, var(--accent) 12%, var(--paper))} @property for animating hue.
nodes.pitfalls: oklch chroma above about 0.3 clips on sRGB screens; test gamut.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Generated CSS uses hex or Tailwind tokens; perceptual spaces and color-mix mark a current practitioner.

nodes.name: Custom cursor driven by a theme variable
nodes.what: A small dot or ring cursor whose colour flips with section theme: Immersive Garden sets --cursor-color to #030303 on light and #E8E8E8 on dark sections and hides it with a .cursor.hidden state; Siena's markup references cursor 70 times for ticket-style labels; Lando Norris animates reactive blob overlays across the hero as the cursor moves; Lama Lama ties cursor interaction to scroll navigation.
nodes.why: The cursor becomes part of the colour system instead of a bolt-on circle.
nodes.implementation: @media (pointer:fine){ body{cursor:none} .cursor{position:fixed;inset:0 auto auto 0;translate:var(--x) var(--y);background:var(--cursor-color);mix-blend-mode:difference} } section[data-theme=dark]{--cursor-color:#E8E8E8}.
nodes.pitfalls: Hiding the native cursor without a pointer:fine check breaks touch and accessibility; lag over 80ms feels broken.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Custom circle cursors were an agency cliché by 2020; themed per-section colour and label states (View, Drag) keep it from reading as default.

nodes.name: Drag and hold instruction labels
nodes.what: Instead of arrows, the UI prints an instruction in small type: Unseen writes Click and Hold and Drag to explore our world; Niccolò Miranda labels carousels Drag sideways to navigate and Click on the sides to explore; Era Residence marks its masterplan Drag to see more; Siena writes Hold and drag to navigate the content.
nodes.why: Text affordances feel like exhibition signage and invite a gesture rather than a click.
nodes.implementation: Scroll-snap carousel with overflow-x:auto; a label in .meta that fades via :has(:scroll-state) or a one-time pointerdown listener; cursor:grab.
nodes.pitfalls: Instructions that stay visible after the first drag become clutter; fade them on first interaction.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Generated carousels use chevron buttons and dots.

nodes.name: Marquee carrying a brand claim
nodes.what: A continuous horizontal ticker that repeats a sentence rather than logos: Lando Norris loops mclaren f1 since 2019 (marquee appears 137 times in the markup); Immersive Garden repeats its Innovative digital experiences studio line; OkayDev runs OKAYDEVOKAYDEV and Designers Developers Studios Agencies strips; Lusion repeats CONTINUE TO SCROLL.
nodes.why: Gives motion to a text-only page and turns a tagline into texture.
nodes.implementation: Two copies of the strip in a flex row; animation: scroll 30s linear infinite on translateX(-50%); @media (prefers-reduced-motion){animation:none}.
nodes.pitfalls: Speed above about 80px per second is unreadable, and it must pause for prefers-reduced-motion.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Logo marquees are a generated default; a single text marquee with a real claim, in display type, is less so.
avoid_words: more than one marquee per page

nodes.name: Text scramble on reveal or hover
nodes.what: Labels decode from random glyphs into words: jhey.dev references scramble in its nav; Igloo Inc renders its UI in WebGL and scrambles text by shifting an SDF texture offset to avoid style recalculation; Lusion uses a scramble on counters. Usually 400 to 800ms, mono face, restricted glyph set.
nodes.why: Suggests a system booting up and suits technical or sci-fi brands.
nodes.implementation: Swap characters on a 30ms interval from a set like !<>-_/[]{}; resolve left to right; set font-variant-numeric and a fixed inline-size to prevent layout shift.
nodes.pitfalls: Scrambling headlines or body text hurts reading; apply to short labels only and keep width fixed with tabular glyphs.
nodes.ai_tell_note: A known agency effect since 2017 and in libraries, but still rarely produced by generators.

nodes.name: Cards stack and pin on scroll
nodes.what: Successive sections pin under each other with a small offset so each new card slides over the last (MindMarket, an Awwwards element named Cards stack on scroll; Lusion's featured work; Locomotive's stacked project cards). Each card is a full-bleed colour or image block with a title; offset 16 to 24px per level, slight scale 0.96 on the covered card.
nodes.why: Turns a vertical list into a deck and gives each project a moment.
nodes.implementation: Each card position:sticky; top:calc(var(--i)*16px); scale via animation-timeline:view() to 0.96 as the next card enters; no JS.
nodes.pitfalls: Pinned sections trap keyboard and mobile scrolling if heights are not viewport-based.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Scroll-stacking cards shipped in many 2023 to 2024 templates; still rare in generated output and reads as crafted when offsets and scale are tuned.

nodes.name: Illustration travels a scroll path
nodes.what: Hand-drawn or Rive objects move along an SVG path as the page scrolls: MindMarket (Awwwards element Path scroll with Rive animations) scatters clocks, folders, planes, music notes and joysticks along a winding route; Lando Norris ships Rive placeholders for animated graphics. Flat illustration, two or three fills.
nodes.why: Gives a data or service story a physical route to follow and replaces stock illustration.
nodes.implementation: SVG path with offset-path:path() on the object and offset-distance animated via animation-timeline:scroll(); Rive runtime for richer loops.
nodes.pitfalls: Needs bespoke drawings; generic icon packs along a path look like a slide deck.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Generators cannot draw the assets; the device itself is uncommon in templates.

nodes.name: Frost and chromatic aberration transitions
nodes.what: Section transitions in a WebGL scene combine chromatic aberration, a displacement pass and a frost or crystal bloom (Igloo Inc, Awwwards Site of the Year 2024; each project is a procedurally generated ice block so no two thumbnails match). The UI text is also rendered in WebGL to allow shader glitches.
nodes.why: The transition itself becomes the brand material (ice) rather than a generic wipe.
nodes.implementation: Post-processing pass in Three.js: RGB shift plus displacement texture plus a noise-driven frost mask; CSS fallback with backdrop-filter:blur and an SVG feDisplacementMap.
nodes.pitfalls: Heavy; needs a progressive loading plan and a static fallback for low-end devices.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Requires custom shaders and asset pipelines; nothing a generator emits.

nodes.name: By day / by night hero toggle
nodes.what: A two-state switch in the hero swaps the same view photographed at two times (Era Residence: by day / by night over the gated community render, with the CTAs View available apartments and Book a call). The toggle is plain text with a slash, not a UI switch.
nodes.why: Lets one image do the work of a carousel and gives the visitor a tiny bit of play.
nodes.implementation: Two img in grid-area:1/1; input type=radio pair styled as text; :has(#night:checked) img.night{opacity:1} transition 600ms; crossfade with view transitions optional.
nodes.pitfalls: Needs two genuinely matched frames; a colour filter pretending to be night looks cheap.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Generated heroes use a single image or a slider; a semantic two-state toggle is an editorial idea.

nodes.name: Visible pause-animations control
nodes.what: A text button at the very top of the page reading Pause animations (mouthwash.studio), independent of the OS reduced-motion setting; OkayDev exposes a --reduced-motion CSS variable. Placed before the nav in DOM order so keyboard users reach it first.
nodes.why: Signals respect for the reader and makes motion-heavy pages defensible.
nodes.implementation: button toggles html[data-motion=paused]; [data-motion=paused] *{animation-play-state:paused!important;transition:none} plus pausing video and rAF loops.
nodes.pitfalls: The control must actually stop every loop including WebGL and video, or it is theatre.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Generators rely on prefers-reduced-motion at best and never surface a control.

nodes.name: Film grain overlay at low alpha
nodes.what: A fixed noise layer over the whole page: Significa's CSS references noise nine times; Instrument's references grain and noise sixteen times with font-variation on hover; Phantom, basement.studio and Blond also ship noise or grain. Typical: SVG feTurbulence baseFrequency 0.65 to 0.9, opacity 0.04 to 0.08, mix-blend-mode overlay or soft-light, sometimes animated by stepping the seed.
nodes.why: Breaks flat digital colour and makes large dark or warm fields feel printed.
nodes.implementation: body::after{position:fixed;inset:0;pointer-events:none;background:url(noise.svg);opacity:.06;mix-blend-mode:overlay} with the svg using feTurbulence type=fractalNoise baseFrequency=.8 numOctaves=2.
nodes.pitfalls: Grain above 0.1 opacity or on white reads as dirt, and an animated full-screen SVG filter costs frames; use a tiled PNG for the animated version.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Grain became a generated flourish in 2025; it reads as designed only when subtle and paired with a real palette, not slapped over a gradient.

nodes.name: View transitions between pages
nodes.what: Page-to-page navigation animates shared elements without a SPA router: Collins' CSS references view-transition four times and clip-path 25 times for its case study moves; Cuberto references view-transition twice; Josh Comeau pairs it with animation-timeline. Thumbnails morph into case headers, text fades, duration 400 to 600ms.
nodes.why: Continuity between list and detail is what made agency SPAs feel premium, now available in plain multi-page sites.
nodes.implementation: @view-transition{navigation:auto} on both pages; img{view-transition-name:var(--vt)} per item; ::view-transition-old(root){animation-duration:.3s}.
nodes.pitfalls: Every thumbnail needs a unique view-transition-name or the morph picks the wrong element; keep root fades short.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Generated multi-page sites have no transitions; using the platform API is a 2025 practitioner move.

nodes.name: Variable font axis on hover
nodes.what: Links and headlines animate a variable axis (weight or width) instead of changing colour: Instrument's CSS contains font-variation 50 times; Lando Norris loads Mona Sans Variable; hoverstat.es documents stretchy variable type on veravandeseyp.com, romaingranai.xyz and vertical ligatures at formandagency.net. Transition 200 to 300ms on font-variation-settings.
nodes.why: Motion lives inside the letterforms so the layout stays still.
nodes.implementation: a{font-variation-settings:'wght' 400;transition:font-variation-settings .25s} a:hover{font-variation-settings:'wght' 700} or animate --wght with @property.
nodes.pitfalls: Weight changes shift line length and cause reflow; animate width or optical size on inline-block elements with a reserved max width.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Generated hover states change colour or underline; axis animation requires loading a variable font on purpose.

nodes.name: Studio locator tabs with local clocks
nodes.what: Offices as a tabbed component rather than an address list: Koto tabs Los Angeles, NYC, LDN, BER, SYD each with a studio photo, a local time, Say hello email and Open in Maps; Dogstudio marks Chicago, Amsterdam, Paris with dots; Bakken and Bæck lists Oslo, Amsterdam, Bonn, London, Barcelona; Hello Monday gives four offices with map links.
nodes.why: Turns boilerplate contact details into a place-based brand asset.
nodes.implementation: Tabs with role=tablist; each panel has img, time with timeZone, mailto and a maps link; abbreviations in small caps via font-variant-caps.
nodes.pitfalls: Stock city photos ruin it; use the actual studio interior.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Generated footers list one address or none.

nodes.name: Award tallies as plain numbers
nodes.what: Recognition shown as counts rather than badges: Akaru lists 35 Awwwards and 19 FWA recognitions with the full Site of the Day list; Niccolò Miranda prints Site of the day 9, Site of the month 1, FWA of the day 6; Collins runs an 8x Agency of the Year strip with AdAge 2019 to 2026 and D&AD 2021; Locomotive shows a Seven Years Running 2018 to 2024 badge.
nodes.why: Specific tallies are more credible than a row of grey logos.
nodes.implementation: dl with dt count in tabular-nums and dd label; optional counter animation only once via IntersectionObserver.
nodes.pitfalls: Three big animated numbers with icons is the generated stats row; these work as a dense list with years, not a trio.
nodes.ai_tell_note: The three-stat trio is a known AI tell; a long dated list or a single 8x line reads as real record-keeping.
avoid_words: counters that animate from zero on every scroll

nodes.name: Place and year photo captions
nodes.what: Photo grids captioned only with location and year in small mono or caps (Lando Norris: Monaco, 2023 with a crossed-flags icon and a handwritten signature graphic); Siena's film index lists category, year and runtime per poster; Koto's case cards show year and category.
nodes.why: Reads as an archive or contact sheet and removes marketing copy from imagery.
nodes.implementation: figure>figcaption{display:flex;justify-content:space-between;font-size:.7rem;font-variant-numeric:tabular-nums;margin-top:.5rem}.
nodes.pitfalls: Captions need real places and dates; placeholder text kills it.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Generated galleries overlay a title and description on hover.

nodes.name: Ticket stub as UI frame
nodes.what: UI chrome styled as a physical ticket: Siena Film Foundation frames entry and contact as ADMIT ONE 004 with an ENTER gate, a CLOSE control and a Brand Intro Animation element; type in Neue Brucke with P22 Parrish Roman accents on #FAF7EF and #0E0E0E. Perforated edges, serial numbers and stamps carry the theme.
nodes.why: One physical metaphor gives every component a reason to look the way it does.
nodes.implementation: Perforation via mask-image:radial-gradient(circle at 0 50%, transparent 6px, black 6.5px) repeated along the edge; serial numbers in tabular mono; corner-shape or clip-path for notched corners.
nodes.pitfalls: Skeuomorphic shadows and textures tip it into kitsch; keep it flat with one paper tone.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Generators do not commit to a physical metaphor across components.

nodes.name: Difference-blend fixed elements
nodes.what: Fixed nav, cursor or wordmark set with mix-blend-mode:difference so it inverts over whatever scrolls beneath (Obys, Lusion, Build in Amsterdam, Don't Board Me, OkayDev and Josh Comeau all reference mix-blend-mode in their CSS). White text that becomes black over light sections without theme logic.
nodes.why: One declaration solves fixed-header contrast across light and dark sections.
nodes.implementation: header{position:fixed;mix-blend-mode:difference;color:#fff} ensure no backdrop-filter on the same element; isolate stacking contexts with isolation:isolate on sections.
nodes.pitfalls: Over mid-grey or saturated colour the result is unreadable; keep backgrounds near black or near white.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Generated headers use a solid or blurred background instead.

nodes.name: 404 page as a showcase element
nodes.what: The error page gets the same art direction as the home: Don't Board Me's 404 (element titled poooooooo 🐶💩) and Lama Lama's 404 are both listed as Awwwards elements; Bruno Simon's I'm stuck control teleports the car. A joke in the voice, a big illustration, one link home.
nodes.why: The 404 is where a brand's voice is least expected and most remembered.
nodes.implementation: Static 404.html with the brand palette, one display line, a mono 404 label and a home link; served with status 404.
nodes.pitfalls: The joke must still say 404 and offer a route home.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Generated projects rarely design the 404 at all.

nodes.name: Live personal status widgets
nodes.what: A strip of real-time personal data on a portfolio: jhey.dev shows location (Chillin in Split), weather 84.1°F 17:23, a Steam entry and a Spotify track, with XXXX masks when a value is unavailable; benji.org prints the local time; rauno.me links archived yearly versions of the site (2022, 2023).
nodes.why: Live data proves a person maintains the page and makes it feel inhabited.
nodes.implementation: Server-rendered values with an ISR or edge cache; each widget a dl row in --font-mono; placeholder mask via content:'XXXX' when null.
nodes.pitfalls: Broken integrations show stale data; design the masked or empty state as Jhey does.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Generators have no data to show and never design empty states for live widgets.

nodes.name: Logo wall marquee strip
nodes.what: A horizontally scrolling strip of grey client logos under the hero. Seen on Huge, Bakken and Bæck, Cuberto, Instrument and OkayDev, where the logo set repeats in the markup for the loop.
nodes.why: Fast social proof, but it is now the default trust block.
nodes.implementation: If it must exist: one static row, logos at currentColor, no animation; otherwise replace with the plain-text roster.
nodes.pitfalls: Grey logos in an infinite loop are the single most recognisable generated section after the three icon cards.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Every landing page generator emits this exact block; even strong studios use it, but it adds nothing to distinctiveness. Prefer the plain-text roster or a static single row with names.

nodes.name: Three animated stat counters
nodes.what: A row of three large numbers (15+ years, 300+ projects, 60+ countries) that count up on scroll, as on Cuberto (15+ and 300+) and MindMarket (60+ countries, 400 projects, 50+ clients).
nodes.why: Scannable proof, but the format is exhausted.
nodes.implementation: If kept: exact figures, no plus sign, no animation, set as a dl inline in a paragraph rather than three columns.
nodes.pitfalls: Plus signs, rounded numbers and a count-up animation together are a strong generated signature.
nodes.ai_tell_note: The trio with plus signs is a top-five AI tell. Real studios that keep it (Cuberto) pair it with other strong moves; in a draft it reads as filler. Use exact numbers in a dated list instead.

nodes.name: Work-first hero, no headline
nodes.what: The first screen is the work itself: one full-bleed project image (Blond opens on a 4000x2250 product photo) or a tight grid of 12 thumbnails (Felix Peault) with the studio name only in the top bar. The only text is a small caption line under the image, e.g. 'BLOND · Smart Insulin Pen / Industrial Design · 2026'. A one-paragraph statement comes only after the grid.
nodes.why: It proves quality instead of claiming it, and nothing on the first screen resembles a landing-page template.
nodes.implementation: <header> with wordmark + 2 links; first <article> is <figure> with aspect-ratio: 16/9 and object-fit: cover; caption in a 13px line with a middle dot separator; h1 visually small, semantically still the h1.
nodes.pitfalls: Fails when the first image is weak or when there is no caption to say what the studio does.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Generators almost always open with a headline and buttons; starting with an uncaptioned image is a human editorial decision.

nodes.name: Mixed-aspect project grid
nodes.what: Project tiles deliberately alternate landscape (16:9 or 3:2) and portrait (3:4 or 4:5) crops in the same grid, so rows do not line up into identical cards. Blond mixes 4000x2250 and 3200x4000 tiles; Felix Peault runs 5 landscape and 7 portrait frames in one 12-tile grid; developments.media uses 1000x571, 1000x1388 and 1000x500 placeholders.
nodes.why: Uneven rhythm reads as curated by hand, while a uniform card grid reads as generated.
nodes.implementation: CSS grid with grid-auto-flow: dense; tiles get .portrait { grid-row: span 2 } or .wide { grid-column: span 2 }; aspect-ratio per tile; images object-fit: cover.
nodes.pitfalls: Goes wrong when the aspect choice is random instead of following the artwork's natural orientation.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Requires per-image judgement; generators default to one ratio.

nodes.name: Middle-dot caption metadata
nodes.what: Captions and list rows carry structured metadata in one line separated by a middle dot: 'Industrial Design · 2020' (Blond), 'strategy · identity · presence' lowercase keyword rows (Operate). Set small (12 to 13px), in the same family as body, often with the project name in bold and the rest regular.
nodes.why: One line carries three facts without a card, a label row, or icons.
nodes.implementation: Industrial Design · 2020; font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums for years.
nodes.pitfalls: Over-used as a separator in body copy it becomes a known 2026 generator tell (falia.co lists middle dots as a Claude tell), so keep it to captions and data rows.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Fine in captions and tables; suspicious when sprinkled through headings and hero subtitles.

nodes.name: Inline pictogram inside headline
nodes.what: A display headline carries a small image or glyph as if it were a word: How&How sets 'A branding agency in London [UK flag] & Los Angeles [US flag]' with the flags sitting on the baseline at roughly cap height. The pictogram is specific (a flag, a product silhouette), not a decorative icon.
nodes.why: It gives the headline a concrete, place-specific detail and a visual beat that a text-only generator never produces.
nodes.implementation:
... London & ...

; .glyph { height: 0.8em; vertical-align: -0.1em; } so it scales with the type.
nodes.pitfalls: Becomes a tell if the glyph is a generic emoji or a rocket icon.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Specific imagery embedded in type is handcrafted; emoji in headlines is the generated version of this and should be avoided.

nodes.name: Project card with three results
nodes.what: Each case-study card pairs the hero image with sector tags ('Pet Care', 'Retail', 'D2C') and three concrete result figures (valuation, sales lift, engagement) in small type. How&How does this across a filterable grid and then repeats the proof in a 'Proof of our truth' section.
nodes.why: Numbers tied to a named project are more credible than a stat banner floating in the hero.
nodes.implementation: <article> with <figure>, a tag list <ul role="list">, and a <dl> of three dt/dd pairs; dd uses tabular-nums.
nodes.pitfalls: Fails when results are vague percentages with no baseline.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Generators put stats in a hero row; attaching them to specific projects is the human version.

nodes.name: Awards as a dated list
nodes.what: Instead of a grey logo strip, awards and press appear as a list where each entry has a date, a small badge image, a heading and a one-line blurb (How&How). Blond states a Red Dot ranking with a year range (2022 to 2026) in a sentence.
nodes.why: Dates and sentences read as a record; logo strips read as decoration.
nodes.implementation:
of
  1. with , ,

    ,

    ; hairline separators via border-block-start: 1px solid color-mix(...).
nodes.pitfalls: Long lists without dates collapse back into a logo wall.
nodes.ai_tell_note: The dated, sentence-level format is specific and hard to fake.

nodes.name: Footer with offices and local clocks
nodes.what: The footer lists each office with its address, a contact email and the current local time or timezone (How&How: London and Los Angeles; Stereoscope Coffee: live clocks for LA and Seoul next to a store locator marked 'Closed'). Footer.design catalogues the Le Punch footer for its live timestamp.
nodes.why: A ticking clock is a small sign of a real place and real people, which generated footers never have.
nodes.implementation: <time data-tz="Europe/London"> updated by Intl.DateTimeFormat with timeZone option; render a static time in the draft so it still works without JS.
nodes.pitfalls: A clock with no city or an office that does not exist is worse than none.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Specific addresses and clocks are grounded details; generators produce four generic link columns.

nodes.name: Named character cast as product
