nodes.what: Town presents its AI assistants as a roster of illustrated characters (a dog in a bowtie, an axolotl, a lobster, a knight), each with a name and a town.com email address, a 'photobooth' set posing them beside real people, and a footer row crediting the characters by name. Feature blocks pair one character with one claim and one testimonial.
nodes.why: A cast with names gives an abstract product a face and a tone without stock illustration.
nodes.implementation: Static WebP characters at 2 sizes via srcset; roster as a <ul> of figure + figcaption with name and address.
nodes.pitfalls: Generic mascots with no names and no roles are just illustration filler.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Requires commissioned character art and a naming system; generators output a rounded-blob illustration.

nodes.name: First-person sample output as copy
nodes.what: Product proof is written as the product speaking in first person: Town shows messages like 'I've drafted a reply offering two open times from your calendar'; Operate shows a Slack-style '#stalled-deals' channel and a meeting card dated 'Wed, 14 Oct, 3:00 PM' with deal values ($1.24M, +$35.0k). The samples are specific, dated, and slightly mundane.
nodes.why: A believable sample output explains the product faster than a benefit headline.
nodes.implementation: Render as semantic <blockquote> or a small chat component in HTML/CSS, not an image, so the text stays crisp and editable.
nodes.pitfalls: Round numbers and lorem-style names ('Acme', 'John Doe') undo the effect.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Specific, imperfect numbers and dates look observed, not generated.

nodes.name: Hero dashboard card with odd numbers
nodes.what: Beside a short headline sits one product card with uncomfortably specific numbers: Polar's hero shows 'Acme Inc' with tokens metered 9.22B, revenue $18,432.17, gross margin 61%, inference cost $7,104.62 and a two-colour legend. Spek uses a full-width screenshot of its real dashboard as the only hero visual.
nodes.why: The Awwwards Razorpay case summarised it as 'keep the product in the hero'; concrete figures carry more trust than a 3D render.
nodes.implementation: HTML table or dl inside a bordered card; font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; one accent colour for the chart line.
nodes.pitfalls: Becomes the 'hero metric' tell if the number is huge and alone; it must sit inside a believable UI.
nodes.ai_tell_note: A single giant number with a small label is flagged by impeccable.style; a dense card with several specific values is not.

nodes.name: Plain-text trust bar
nodes.what: The 'trusted by' row lists company names as plain text in the body face instead of grey SVG logos (Spek). CleanShot keeps logos but flattens them to one grey, #ADADAD, so none competes.
nodes.why: Text names avoid the generated-looking grey logo strip and read as a list someone typed.
nodes.implementation:
Used at Acme, Beta, Gamma and 40 more teams.

or a
    with display: flex; gap: 2ch; no icons.
nodes.pitfalls: Looks unfinished if the names are unknown; then skip the section entirely.
nodes.ai_tell_note: The default is a marquee of logos; a static text list is a deliberate restraint.

nodes.name: Print-object card (magazine cover)
nodes.what: Operate closes with a card styled as a magazine cover carrying print conventions: 'Vol. 1', 'Ref. B001', 'Subject: A PROPER PLACE TO WORK', with a masthead and rules. Elsewhere on recent.design a 'crumpled receipt component' does the same with a receipt.
nodes.why: Borrowing the grammar of a physical object gives a section a texture that no UI-kit card has.
nodes.implementation: A bordered <article> with a 3-column masthead grid, hairline rules, small caps for 'Vol.' and 'Ref.', and a tall aspect-ratio: 3/4.
nodes.pitfalls: If every section becomes a different object the page turns into a scrapbook.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Specific print conventions (volume, reference numbers) are editorial moves, not kit defaults.

nodes.name: Process steps named like chapters
nodes.what: Instead of 'Step 1, 2, 3', the process section names each phase as a proper noun with a bold lead line and a lowercase keyword row: Operate uses 'The Map', 'The Plan', 'The Build', 'The Rollout'. Stereoscope structures its philosophy as 'Five Elements' (Altitude, Soil, Fauna, Climate, Farmer & Roaster).
nodes.why: Named chapters feel authored and brand-specific; numbered steps are the generator's reflex.
nodes.implementation:
per chapter with

The Map

...

discovery · audit · interviews

.
nodes.pitfalls: Over-poetic names that hide what actually happens in each phase.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Numbered 01/02/03 blocks are a flagged tell; named chapters sidestep it.

nodes.name: Parenthetical section kickers
nodes.what: Section labels are set inside spaced parentheses, '( The Studio )', '( The step aside )', with counters like '(08)' and a letterspaced word such as 'w o r k s' as a heading (Nothin'). The brackets replace the all-caps tracked eyebrow label.
nodes.why: It gives the page a typeset, zine-like voice and avoids the eyebrow-label tell.
nodes.implementation:
( The Studio )

with font-feature-settings: 'case'; letter-spacing on the heading via letter-spacing: 0.4em; text-transform none.
nodes.pitfalls: Combined with a numbered counter on every section it drifts back to the numbered-label tell.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Not in any slop catalogue yet; reads as a typographic quirk.

nodes.name: FAQ answers with prices and timelines
nodes.what: Studio FAQ answers state real figures: budgets, durations and what is included (Nothin' gives prices and timelines in a four-question FAQ). Bauhaus Clock answers 'Is it worth paying for?' in its own voice and lists a $19 price up front.
nodes.why: Concrete numbers are the fastest trust signal and the thing generators replace with 'it depends'.
nodes.implementation: Native <details><summary> pairs; no accordion JS; name="faq" attribute for exclusive open.
nodes.pitfalls: Prices without scope ranges create arguments later.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Specific, falsifiable numbers read as human.

nodes.name: Glossy inflated-object photography
nodes.what: Instead of 3D blobs, Nothin' uses product-style photographs of real tactile objects: foil, balloons, bubble wrap, frosting, a shopping bag, inflated or crinkled, shot on transparent, white or dark-gradient backgrounds with strong sheen and creases. Twelve of them frame the hero headline.
nodes.why: Physical objects with real reflections carry texture that rendered gradients cannot.
nodes.implementation: PNG/WebP with alpha, mix-blend-mode: multiply on light paper, drop-shadow filter instead of box-shadow.
nodes.pitfalls: Cheap AI renders of foil look exactly like the thing being avoided.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Requires real photography or art direction.

nodes.name: Image tiles framing the headline
nodes.what: A row or ring of small project images surrounds or sits directly above the headline: Komma Komma puts a strip of tiles over 'Komma Komma is a product design & web-experience creative studio...'; How&How runs a repeating grid of thumbnails behind the text; Nothin' arranges twelve objects around the statement.
nodes.why: Shows breadth of work at a glance while keeping the headline as the anchor.
nodes.implementation: A flex row of 6 to 12 with varied widths above the h1; optional overflow-x: auto with scroll-snap-type: x mandatory and padding-inline matching the page gutter.
nodes.pitfalls: Tiles that auto-scroll turn into the marquee tell; keep them static or draggable.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Needs real work to show; placeholder tiles make it obvious.

nodes.name: Modest studio voice and mailto CTA
nodes.what: Little Website Co. describes itself as 'a little studio' doing 'careful, considered work', lists 19 services alphabetically with only four linked, and ends with a plain mailto link rather than a form or booking widget. Testimonial and work sliders say 'Swipe, or use the arrow keys'.
nodes.why: Understatement and plain mechanics read as a confident human, the opposite of hype copy.
nodes.implementation:
hello@... as the final CTA; services as a
    with columns: 3 and only real links wrapped in .
nodes.pitfalls: Modesty with no evidence of work just looks small.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Generators default to superlatives and a contact form.

nodes.name: Place statement before the work
nodes.what: Counter Forms opens with an Acknowledgement of Country as the first block; Grafik's footer affirms Te Tiriti o Waitangi; both then proceed to the work. The statement is set in body type, not a banner.
nodes.why: A specific, local, political position is something no template or generator supplies.
nodes.implementation: A <section aria-label> of two paragraphs, max-inline-size: 60ch, before <main> content.
nodes.pitfalls: Tokenistic if the organisation has no real connection to the statement.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Grounded in a real place and position.

nodes.name: Single-glyph specimen cards
nodes.what: Cards show one huge character or word set in the thing being sold instead of a thumbnail: Counter Forms previews its typefaces with '2', 'A', 'D', 'Diverse', 'Tongue'. Uncut.wtf lists categories with counts ('Sans Serif 66') in collapsible sections.
nodes.why: Type as image is cheaper and more honest than mockups and gives the grid scale changes.
nodes.implementation: <figure> with a <span aria-hidden> at font-size: clamp(6rem, 20vw, 14rem); line-height: 0.8; overflow: hidden; caption below.
nodes.pitfalls: Only works with a typeface that can carry a 200px glyph.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Not a kit pattern.

nodes.name: Hover swaps to a second image
nodes.what: On hover a card swaps to a second prepared image rather than scaling or lifting: Counter Forms' Crosswords promo swaps files; Jakobsen Copenhagen pairs product tiles so the alternate view appears on hover. No translateY, no shadow growth.
nodes.why: It gives new information on hover instead of decoration, and avoids the 'every card lifts' tell.
nodes.implementation: Two stacked in a grid cell; .alt { opacity: 0 } and :hover .alt { opacity: 1 } with transition 150ms ease-out; @media (hover: none) show the alt as a second slide.
nodes.pitfalls: Needs a touch fallback: show both images or swap on tap.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Content-driven hover rather than a transform preset.

nodes.name: Archive index grouped by year
nodes.what: An archive lists items under year headings in reverse order with only terse labels: The Surfer's Journal Archives groups 188 covers by '2026 - Vol. 35' down to 1992, captioned only by issue number ('35.5'). developments.media numbers interviews 43 down to 1, each with a two-to-four-word poetic title, a location and a date.
nodes.why: Numbering and years give the content a sense of accumulation and history that a card grid cannot.
nodes.implementation:
per year with

2026 · Vol. 35

and a grid of
nodes.pitfalls: Only legitimate when the numbers are a real sequence.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Real sequences are the one place numbering is not a tell.

nodes.name: Named multi-theme switcher
nodes.what: Max Böck's site offers ten named colour themes (Classic, Dark, eight Mario Kart 64 tracks, Hacker News) from a theme panel; the whole page recolours via custom properties. Themes have personality names rather than 'light/dark'.
nodes.why: It treats colour as play and proves the system is built on tokens.
nodes.implementation: [data-theme="rainbow-road"] { --paper: ...; --ink: ...; } on <html>; persist in localStorage; use color-mix for derived tints so each theme needs only 3 to 4 base values.
nodes.pitfalls: Themes that only change the accent are not themes.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Generators ship exactly light and dark.

nodes.name: Version number in the masthead
nodes.what: Robin Rendle's header reads 'Robin Rendle / v19.1.1' and the navigation is a nested, numbered list grouped by year (2026 back to 2022) then by stories; the body is a grid of ~400px square photo thumbnails labelled with filenames. Max Böck numbers his nav '01 Home 02 Writing 03 Notes 04 About'.
nodes.why: A semver masthead and year-grouped nav say 'this site is maintained by a person' more than any About page.
nodes.implementation:
Robin Rendle / v19.1.1
; nav as nested
    with list-style: decimal-leading-zero.
nodes.pitfalls: Numbered nav items are fine for four items; numbered section eyebrows on marketing pages are a tell.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Specific to a maintained personal site.

nodes.name: Draggable preview strip hero
nodes.what: Osmo's hero stacks a large 'Dev Toolkit / Built to Flex' heading over a horizontal strip of resource previews labelled 'Drag', plus a circular rotating-text SVG badge. Navigation is a single 'Menu' button opening a panel with two link groups.
nodes.why: A hand-controlled strip is tactile and pauses by default, unlike an auto marquee.
nodes.implementation: overflow-x: auto; scroll-snap-type: x proximity; cursor: grab; pointer-drag to scrollLeft in 20 lines of JS; padding-inline matches the page gutter at both ends.
nodes.pitfalls: Circular rotating badges are now a Framer component default; use at most one.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Drag strips are human-feeling; the rotating circular badge alone is now a template signal.

nodes.name: Single Menu button and panel
nodes.what: Top bar holds the wordmark, one 'Menu' word and at most one action (Osmo: Login, Join; Thursday's Child and Little Website Co. show 'Menu / Close'). The panel lists grouped links in large type. No icon hamburger, no mega-menu.
nodes.why: A word instead of three lines reads as considered, and the panel can carry the brand type at scale.
nodes.implementation: <button popovertarget="menu">Menu</button> with a [popover] panel; toggle label text to 'Close'; use @starting-style for the fade.
nodes.pitfalls: Hiding primary conversions behind the panel on a marketing site.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Generators output a five-link bar plus two buttons.

nodes.name: One custom or rare typeface
nodes.what: The new Obys site runs a single custom neo-grotesque, 'OTF Obys NG', for both functional and expressive text, with hierarchy from size, spacing and rhythm only. Speakeasy's 2025 redesign uses Tobias for headlines and ABC Diatype plus Diatype Mono for everything else. Typewolf's December 2025 picks are all paid or rare faces (Grenette, Styrene, Swear, Kabel, Editorial Old, Signifier, Arizona Flare, Agipo).
nodes.why: A face nobody else on the marketplace uses is the single strongest anti-template signal.
nodes.implementation: @font-face with font-display: swap and a size-adjust fallback; variable font with wght axis; use font-feature-settings for alternates ('ss01') to make even a known face look unfamiliar.
nodes.pitfalls: Free lookalikes of famous faces (Inter for Helvetica) do not count; pick a genuinely different design.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Generators pick from a short list of Google Fonts; see notes for fresh free alternatives.

nodes.name: Serif + grotesk + mono triad
nodes.what: A three-role system: an opinionated display serif for headlines, a quiet grotesk for UI and body, and a mono for data, captions and code. Typewolf's late-2025 sites: Tobias / Diatype / Diatype Mono (Speakeasy), Swear / DM Mono (Dirty Vine), Cardinal / Sweet Sans / Baskerville (Heart & Soil).
nodes.why: Three distinct voices let hierarchy come from family changes instead of size jumps and labels.
nodes.implementation: --font-display, --font-text, --font-data custom properties; mono only on <code>, <time>, tables and captions; serif only on h1/h2 and pull quotes.
nodes.pitfalls: Instrument Serif + Geist + Geist Mono is this exact triad in its generated form; choose faces outside the Google/Vercel default set.
nodes.ai_tell_note: The structure is sound; the risk is entirely in which three families you pick.

nodes.name: System font stack, on purpose
nodes.what: Bauhaus Clock labels its page 'System Font Enabled' and sets everything in the OS font (San Francisco on Mac), letting the product screenshots carry character. Paco Coursey's site is a single column of short sections with links as the only interactive elements.
nodes.why: Zero webfont weight and native rendering read as confident restraint, and no generator ever chooses it.
nodes.implementation: font-family: system-ui, -apple-system, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, sans-serif; font-optical-sizing: auto; use modern-font-stacks.com for serif/mono equivalents.
nodes.pitfalls: On Windows the stack falls to Segoe UI, so check hierarchy at both weights.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Defaults picked on purpose; label it so it reads as intent.

nodes.name: Palette derived from a real artifact
nodes.what: Lando Norris's site (OFF+BRAND, Awwwards Site of the Year 2025) takes its colours from his helmet: acid #CBF902 on a warm green-black #2D3126 with off-white #F4F3F1 and grey-green #7F8177. Causal names its swatches after real paint names (Pearl Bush #E8E0D5, Mojo #C04737, Viridian Green #678975, Bistre #3D2B1F). CleanShot uses one saturated blue #0d44e8 and greys the rest.
nodes.why: A palette with a source story has internal logic; a generic purple-to-cyan pair has none.
nodes.implementation: Define --ink, --paper, --accent, --muted in oklch; derive hovers with color-mix(in oklch, var(--accent), black 15%); never pure #000.
nodes.pitfalls: Near-black plus one acid accent is itself a 2026 generator default; the warm tinted neutrals and the source object are what make it specific.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Safe when the palette has 4 to 6 related values and a visible origin; risky when it collapses to black plus neon.

nodes.name: Full colour system, not one accent
nodes.what: Webflow's 2026 trends list names 'full color systems': palettes of several working colours rather than one accent on grey. Town uses a different colour per character; Causal's product shows nine named swatches; Lando Norris pairs acid with warm greys.
nodes.why: Multiple hues with roles give sections identity without changing layout.
nodes.implementation: Tokens --hue-1..--hue-5 in oklch with matched lightness (e.g. L 0.72 C 0.14); sections use data-tone attributes to switch --accent.
nodes.pitfalls: Without a neutral base and assigned roles it becomes rainbow noise.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Generators default to one accent; a five-hue system with roles is a designed artefact.

nodes.name: Mono-chroma page field
nodes.what: The whole page is one saturated colour field; header and footer dissolve into it; chapters are marked with thin rules and square media instead of background changes; type grows toward the end as a 'late crescendo' (Pixelgrade pattern language, drawn from reviewed sites).
nodes.why: One chromatic room makes the page feel like a single object instead of stacked sections.
nodes.implementation: html { background: var(--field) } and all surfaces transparent; chapters via border-block-start: 1px solid color-mix(in oklch, var(--ink) 30%, transparent); final h2 at clamp(3rem, 10vw, 9rem).
nodes.pitfalls: A nested component falling back to white, or identical intensity everywhere, kills the rhythm; verify contrast for every text role.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Generators alternate section backgrounds; a single field with rule-based chapters is a designed system.

nodes.name: Hairline rules instead of cards
nodes.what: Sections and list rows are separated by 1px rules spanning the content width, with no card backgrounds, radii or shadows: Little Website Co. uses rules between single-column sections; Counter Forms and Polar use row lists. Spacing above a heading is larger than below so it binds to its own content (impeccable.style rule).
nodes.why: Rules give structure with zero visual weight and avoid every card-related tell.
nodes.implementation: section + section { border-block-start: 1px solid var(--rule) } ; h2 { margin-block: 3rem 1rem } ; no border-radius anywhere.
nodes.pitfalls: Falia lists 'newspaper layout with hairline rules and square corners' as a Claude 2026 tell when paired with a serif headline, terracotta accent and all-caps labels; keep the rules, drop the rest of that kit.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Rules alone are neutral; the full newspaper kit is now recognisable.

nodes.name: User-switchable collection layouts
nodes.what: The portfolio or catalogue can be viewed in more than one arrangement: Obys offers vertical, horizontal and grid; Caspia (Framer) toggles grid and fullscreen; Uncut.wtf toggles grid and list. The switch is a small text control, not an icon pair.
nodes.why: It respects how different visitors scan and shows the content is structured data, not a fixed page.
nodes.implementation: Radio inputs + :has(#list:checked) .collection { display: block } switching grid-template-columns; persist via localStorage; view-transition-name on items for the morph.
nodes.pitfalls: Three layouts that all look like cards is not a choice.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Requires real structured content.

nodes.name: Transform and opacity only, under 300ms
nodes.what: Emil Kowalski's rules: animate only transform and opacity, keep UI transitions under 300ms with ease-out, use springs for gestures, never animate keyboard-initiated actions, and respect prefers-reduced-motion by swapping movement for a 200ms fade. Josh Comeau shows CSS linear() for spring curves without JS.
nodes.why: Fast, composited motion feels like a tool; slow eased motion feels like a template demo.
nodes.implementation: transition: transform 180ms ease-out, opacity 180ms ease-out; @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) { * { transition-duration: 0.01ms } }; springs via animation-timing-function: linear(0, 0.3 10%, 1.05 40%, 0.98 70%, 1).
nodes.pitfalls: Height/padding animations trigger layout; pair opacity with a transform or use grid-template-rows: 0fr to 1fr.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Restraint and speed are the opposite of the generated 'everything fades up' look.

nodes.name: No animation for frequent actions
nodes.what: Command menus, context menus, tab switches and anything triggered from the keyboard open instantly (Raycast is the reference; macOS skips the Cmd+Tab overlay if pressed quickly). Animation is reserved for state changes the user needs to follow, such as a drawer or a deletion.
nodes.why: Repeated motion becomes friction; its absence reads as a professional tool.
nodes.implementation: Menus: no transition on open; close with a 120ms opacity fade at most; popover + anchor positioning for placement.
nodes.pitfalls: Applying 'no animation' to a modal that appears from nowhere loses spatial context.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Generators add a fade to everything.

nodes.name: Immediate, interruptible gesture response
nodes.what: Rauno Freiberg's details: apply the drag delta immediately rather than after a threshold; let destructive gestures fire only on release; keep a drag alive when the finger leaves a small control; carry the throw's velocity; make every animation interruptible mid-flight; put frequent targets in screen corners.
nodes.why: Interfaces that respond during the gesture feel physical; ones that animate after a threshold feel scripted.
nodes.implementation: setPointerCapture on pointerdown; translate3d on pointermove; on pointerup use Web Animations API with the measured velocity; CSS transitions (not keyframes) so they can be interrupted.
nodes.pitfalls: Needs pointer capture and velocity tracking; a naive implementation snaps instead of following.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Depth of interaction craft is not something a static generator produces.

nodes.name: Scroll as reversible state
nodes.what: Scroll-driven sequences where every position maps to a deterministic state and scrolling up restores it exactly (Exat microsite with GSAP ScrollTrigger and Lenis). Josh Comeau's scroll-driven animations article shows the same with the CSS animation-timeline API and no JS.
nodes.why: Deterministic, reversible scroll feels like a physical object; one-shot fade-ins feel like a slideshow.
nodes.implementation: animation-timeline: view(); animation-range: entry 0% cover 40%; animations on transform/opacity only; works without JS and reverses naturally.
nodes.pitfalls: Scroll-jacking the native scroll speed is what makes Lenis-based sites feel templated; keep native scroll.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Reversible CSS scroll timelines are rare in generated output, which uses one-shot IntersectionObserver fades.

nodes.name: Playable 404 or waiting state
nodes.what: Design Spells catalogues a fully functional iPod on Apple Music's 404 page, a hidden Snake game while ChatGPT images generate, and Deel's Pretzel Pong during Oktoberfest. The game is small, themed to the brand, and only appears where waiting is unavoidable.
nodes.why: It turns dead time into a brand moment and is self-evidently handmade.
nodes.implementation: A <canvas> under 5KB of JS on /404 only; keyboard controls; a static illustrated fallback in the draft.
nodes.pitfalls: A game on the homepage is a gimmick; it belongs on 404s and long waits.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Bespoke by nature.

nodes.name: Text-only menus, no icon per item
nodes.what: Menus and footers list words only, with no leading icon on every item (Jim Nielsen's 'No More Icons In Every Menu By Default'; Blond, Felix Peault and developments.media navs are bare words). Icons appear only where they carry meaning (an eraser for a drawing tool, a flag for a place).
nodes.why: Icon-per-row lists are a kit reflex; words alone look typeset.
nodes.implementation: Plain <ul> of <a>; no svg; use font-weight or a leading em-dash on hover for state.
nodes.pitfalls: Very long menus may need grouping headings instead.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Generators attach a Lucide icon to every nav and feature item.

nodes.name: Measure, balance and pretty wrapping
nodes.what: Body lines held to 65 to 75 characters, headings wrapped with text-wrap: balance, paragraphs with text-wrap: pretty so no single word is left on the last line, line-height around 1.5 for body, and horizontal scrollers padded at both ends to match the page gutter (impeccable.style's source-level checks).
nodes.why: These are the invisible fixes that separate typeset pages from generated ones.
nodes.implementation: p { max-inline-size: 65ch; text-wrap: pretty; line-height: 1.5 } h1,h2 { text-wrap: balance } .scroller { padding-inline: var(--gutter); scroll-padding-inline: var(--gutter) }.
nodes.pitfalls: text-wrap: balance on long paragraphs is slow and wrong; use it only on headings up to about 6 lines.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Generated pages routinely show orphans and 90-character lines.

nodes.name: TELL: badge, centred H1, two buttons
nodes.what: A pill badge directly above a centred headline, a one-line subhead, a primary plus secondary button, then a row of grey client logos. Flagged in every 2025-2026 tells list (falia.co, impeccable.style, adriankrebs' Show HN scorer, 925 Studios). CleanShot's 'Introducing Studio Mode' eyebrow is the mild human version.
nodes.why: It does not; it is the statistical centre of landing-page training data.
nodes.implementation: Replace with work-first-hero-no-headline, dashboard-card-with-real-numbers or text-led-hero-lowercase-labels; left-align by default.
nodes.pitfalls: Even one of these elements (the badge) is enough for scorers to flag the page.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Store as an avoid rule: no pill above H1, no centred two-button stack by default, no grey logo marquee.

nodes.name: TELL: three identical icon cards
nodes.what: A row of three (or a grid of six) equal cards, each with a rounded icon tile above a heading and two lines of text, identical padding, radius and height. Impeccable flags 'icon tile stacked above heading' and 'identical card grids'; falia and 925 Studios list it as the 2025 signature; Relume-built Webflow sites are criticised for the same three-column feature grid.
nodes.why: It gives every point equal weight so nothing is said.
nodes.implementation: Replace with hairline-rules-as-chapters rows, project-card-with-results, or a two-column text + image alternation with unequal weights.
nodes.pitfalls: Also covers 'nested cards' and 'coloured left border accent' variants.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Avoid rule: never three equal cards with icons; group ideas and vary the layout; put icons beside headings or drop them.

nodes.name: TELL: purple/indigo gradient and gradient text
nodes.what: Indigo-to-purple or purple-to-cyan gradients on buttons, headlines (gradient text), backgrounds and blobs; adriankrebs calls it 'VibeCode Purple'; 925 Studios traces it to Tailwind defaults; impeccable adds 'bright cyan on dark', 'radial-gradient halo' and 'soft spotlight behind content'.
nodes.why: It carries no information about the business.
nodes.implementation: Use palette-from-a-real-artifact or full-colour-system; one solid accent; emphasis through size and weight.
nodes.pitfalls: Includes mesh gradients and 'aurora' backgrounds.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Avoid rule: no gradient text, no purple/indigo/cyan defaults, no radial glow behind content.

nodes.name: TELL: Inter/Geist/Space Grotesk defaults
nodes.what: Inter everywhere (2025), then Geist, Space Grotesk, Manrope, Plus Jakarta Sans, DM Sans, Satoshi, Outfit, Poppins; impeccable's 'overused font' check names Inter and Geist; adriankrebs scores Inter on centred heroes and the Space Grotesk / Instrument Serif / Geist pairing; saaslandingpage.com's own popular-font list is Inter, Geist Sans, Graphik, Geist Mono, Suisse Int'l, Roobert, Tiempos Headline.
nodes.why: They are good faces that now signal 'nobody chose this'.
nodes.implementation: See notes-templates.md for free alternatives (Google Fonts 2025 additions, Fontshare, Uncut) by role.
nodes.pitfalls: Geist Mono and JetBrains Mono as the 'technical' accent are part of the same reflex.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Avoid rule: these families are only acceptable as the invisible body face under a distinctive display face, never as the headline.

nodes.name: TELL: Instrument Serif italic accent word
nodes.what: A sans-serif hero headline with one word swapped to an italic serif (usually Instrument Serif, sometimes Playfair or Fraunces), or an oversized italic serif display headline on its own. adriankrebs scores it explicitly; impeccable calls Instrument Serif 'the newest reflex' and flags 'italic serif display headline'; falia lists 'one highlighted word in italics or colour' as a 2026 Claude default.
nodes.why: It was tasteful in 2023 and is now the most recognisable generated flourish.
nodes.implementation: Use serif-grotesk-mono-triad with a different serif (see notes), or a grotesk-only headline with inline-pictogram-in-headline.
nodes.pitfalls: Highlighting one word in the accent colour is the same tell in a different coat.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Avoid rule: no single-word italic or colour accent in headlines; if a serif is used, set the whole headline in it and choose a face other than Instrument Serif.

nodes.name: TELL: all-caps eyebrow above headings
nodes.what: A small, letterspaced, uppercase label (often mono, often with a dot or dash) above every section heading, repeating the heading's words. Impeccable: 'label above a heading'; falia: the defining 2026 Claude tell alongside serif headlines and monospace small labels; adriankrebs: 'all-caps headings and section labels'.
nodes.why: It adds a line without adding information.
nodes.implementation: Delete the label or fold its words into the heading; if a kicker is required use parenthetical-section-kickers in sentence case.
nodes.pitfalls: Also covers 'mono labels everywhere' and 'wide letter spacing on body text'.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Avoid rule: at most one eyebrow per page, never mono, never tracked uppercase; prefer parenthetical kickers or none.

nodes.name: TELL: 01/02/03 on non-sequences
nodes.what: Two-digit numbers ('01', '02', '03') prefixed to features, values or testimonials that have no order. Impeccable: 'tiny numbered section labels'; falia: a 2026 Claude default; adriankrebs: 'numbered 1, 2, 3 step sequences'. Polar's 01 to 05 feature eyebrows sit on the edge of this.
nodes.why: Numbers imply a sequence the content does not have.
nodes.implementation: Use <ol> only when order matters; style with list-style: decimal-leading-zero so the numbers are semantic.
nodes.pitfalls: Real sequences (archives, issues, true processes) are exempt.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Avoid rule: numbers only for ordered content; otherwise use named-process-chapters.

nodes.name: TELL: giant number and stat rows
nodes.what: A huge number with a tiny label as the first thing on the page, or a row of three or four stat cards ('10k+ users', '99.9% uptime', '24/7'), often counting up on scroll. Impeccable: 'hero metric layout'; adriankrebs: 'rows of stat banners'; falia: Codex 'grids of statistic cards even where they add nothing'.
nodes.why: Round numbers without context read as invented.
nodes.implementation: Use project-card-with-results or dashboard-card-with-real-numbers.
nodes.pitfalls: Count-up animations make it worse.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Avoid rule: numbers live inside project cards or product UI with specific, non-round values.

nodes.name: TELL: glassmorphism, glow, neon dark
nodes.what: Frosted-glass panels with backdrop blur, hairline white borders, large coloured box-shadows, neon accent borders on near-black, pulsing dots, 'floating' panels with heavy shadows. Impeccable: 'glassmorphism everywhere', 'dark mode with glowing accents', 'hairline border with wide shadow'; adriankrebs: glassmorphism and 'large coloured glows'; falia: Codex signature.
nodes.why: Blur and glow are decoration standing in for hierarchy.
nodes.implementation: Opaque surfaces, border: 1px solid color-mix(in oklch, var(--ink) 15%, transparent), no shadow or one short neutral shadow.
nodes.pitfalls: Dark mode itself is fine; mid-grey body text on it fails contrast and is its own tell.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Avoid rule: no backdrop-filter panels, no coloured box-shadows, no glow; dark themes use tinted near-black with opaque surfaces.

nodes.name: TELL: grid lines, dot grids, blobs
nodes.what: Faint grid-line or dot-grid backgrounds, repeating gradient stripes, floating gradient blobs, abstract 3D spheres and rough 'hand-drawn' SVG squiggles. Impeccable flags 'decorative grid-line background', 'repeating-gradient stripes', 'rough SVG illustrations' and 'placeholder-style illustrations'; 925 Studios flags gradient blobs.
nodes.why: They imply measurement or art without delivering either.
nodes.implementation: Use glossy-object-photography, specimen-glyph-cards or mono-chroma-field.
nodes.pitfalls: Grids are fine for maps, canvases and actual measurement.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Avoid rule: no background grids or blobs; use real photography, specimen type or a flat field.

nodes.name: TELL: fade-up and lift on everything
nodes.what: Every section fades and slides up on scroll, every card translates -4px and grows a shadow on hover, buttons bounce, dialogs overshoot. Falia lists 'sections that fade in on scroll and hover effects on every card' as a 2026 Claude default; impeccable flags 'bounce or elastic easing' and 'content stuck waiting to appear'.
nodes.why: Uniform motion carries no information and hides content when JS fails.
nodes.implementation: Use transform-opacity-only-motion rules; no IntersectionObserver fade wrappers; native scroll.
nodes.pitfalls: Includes Lenis smooth-scroll and preloaders on every route, which Framer templates (Nakula, Fabrica) ship by default.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Avoid rule: content visible by default; animate at most one hero element; hover changes content (image swap, underline) not elevation.

nodes.name: TELL: marquee and pulsing status dot
nodes.what: A logo or testimonial strip scrolling by itself, a green dot pulsing next to 'All systems operational' or 'Available for work', a blinking cursor on static text. Impeccable flags all three; falia flags Codex's 'coloured status dots with no real status behind them'.
nodes.why: Fake liveness is the easiest thing to spot.
nodes.implementation: Use plain-text-trust-bar, draggable-preview-strip-hero or dual-office-local-time-footer.
nodes.pitfalls: A live clock or real status feed is the honest alternative.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Avoid rule: no marquees, no pulsing dots, no decorative carets.

nodes.name: TELL: serif, terracotta, cream kit
nodes.what: The 2026 successor to purple-and-Inter: high-contrast serif headline, terracotta or rust accent, cream or beige background, hairline rules, square corners, dense columns, mono small labels, all-caps eyebrows, 01/02/03 markers, middle dots and an arrow appended to every link. Falia attributes the kit to Claude Code's late-2025 to 2026 defaults; impeccable flags 'cream / beige palette' and 'italic serif display headline'. Its dark twin is tinted near-black with a single acid green or vermilion accent and grey body text (also a 2026 default per falia.co).
nodes.why: Any one piece is fine; the full kit is now as recognisable as the purple gradient.
nodes.implementation: If editorial, keep hairline-rules-as-chapters but pick a warm grey or a saturated field, a serif outside Instrument/Playfair/Fraunces, and no eyebrow labels.
nodes.pitfalls: Counter-rule: use at most two of these elements, and never terracotta-on-cream as the base pair.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Avoid rule: cap the editorial kit; swap the palette source (palette-from-a-real-artifact) and the serif (see notes).

nodes.name: TELL: not-X-but-Y slogans
nodes.what: Headlines built as 'It's not a tool, it's a teammate', 'Build faster. Ship smarter.', rule-of-three adjective lists, em dashes in every sentence, 'delve', 'seamless', 'effortless', and an arrow after every link. Impeccable flags 'forced contrast', 'generic marketing claims' and 'em-dash overuse'; falia flags negative parallelism and the rule of three; 925 Studios flags weightless headlines. Nothin's 'Not a style, a perspective' is a human instance, which shows how close the line is.
nodes.why: A competitor could paste the same copy onto their site unchanged.
nodes.implementation: Use first-person-sample-output, faq-with-real-prices, modest-studio-voice.
nodes.pitfalls: Question-form section titles and a closing 'Conclusion' section are the long-form variants.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Avoid rule: no 'not X, Y' constructions, no triads by default, no em dashes, no trailing arrows; headlines must contain a noun only this product could use.

nodes.name: TELL: emoji and icon tiles
nodes.what: Emoji in place of icons in feature lists, nav or sidebars; or a rounded tile containing a thin-line Lucide icon above each heading. Falia: 'emojis used in place of icons' (2025); adriankrebs: 'sidebars or navs with emoji icons'; 925 Studios: 'thin-line and slightly generic' icons.
nodes.why: Emoji render differently per OS and read as placeholder.
nodes.implementation: Use text-only-menus-no-icons and inline-pictogram-in-headline for the rare meaningful glyph.
nodes.pitfalls: Also in documentation, commit messages and buttons.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Avoid rule: no emoji in UI; icons only when they carry meaning and never one per list item.

nodes.name: TELL: bento grid of feature tiles
nodes.what: A 'bento' arrangement of rounded tiles in 1x1, 2x1 and 2x2 sizes, each with a tiny illustration and a heading, usually on a grey or dark field. Not in the older slop lists but named in the brief as a default; it is the 2024 Apple-keynote pattern that every Framer SaaS template (Suprema, Strativ, CloudCraft in the oma-kase roundup) now ships.
nodes.why: It looks organised while saying nothing specific about any tile.
nodes.implementation: If a tile layout is needed, use square corners, no backgrounds and one image per tile (see mixed-aspect-project-grid).
nodes.pitfalls: Extreme corner radii that squeeze content (impeccable) usually come with it.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Avoid rule: no bento by default; use mixed-aspect-project-grid for images or hairline rows for features.

nodes.name: TELL: Lenis, preloader, wordmark footer
nodes.what: The Framer/Webflow template signature: Lenis smooth scroll (Fabrica changelog), a preloader on every page plus page transitions (Nakula), a rotating circular text badge, a particle-text or animated ASCII hero (Soren), 'glitter' animated hero backgrounds (Jet), a retainer pricing toggle with a 'most popular' badge (Mugen), and a footer with the brand name set at viewport width cropped by the bottom edge (Framer 'Futer' component; Pixelgrade pattern).
nodes.why: These are purchasable components, so they are now the template tell rather than the AI tell.
nodes.implementation: Use dual-office-local-time-footer or colophon-footer; dark-to-light-opening once per session at most.
nodes.pitfalls: ASCII and particle text are spreading fast through 2026 templates and will date within a year.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Avoid rule: native scroll, no preloader after first visit, no oversized wordmark footer, no ASCII/particle hero unless type is the product.

nodes.name: TELL: Relume/Flowbase section kit
nodes.what: The Webflow component-library pattern: hero, three-column feature grid, logo bar, alternating image-text rows, testimonial cards, accordion FAQ, CTA band, four-column footer, all with the same 5rem section padding and 1.5rem gaps. Reviews of Relume in 2026 say 'every generated site tends to share the same 3-column feature grid, the same hero section, the same accordion FAQ'.
nodes.why: It is a page assembled from a catalogue, and visitors have seen the catalogue.
nodes.implementation: Spacing scale with at least three section gaps (e.g. 3rem, 6rem, 12rem) chosen per section; tldr-overview-block instead of FAQ where possible.
nodes.pitfalls: Impeccable's 'monotonous spacing' check catches the uniform padding even when components are restyled.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Avoid rule: no fixed section-padding token applied everywhere; vary rhythm by content; no accordion FAQ by default.

nodes.name: Lookbook opening
nodes.what: The store opens on one full-bleed image with a single line of type along the bottom edge: brand and season in mono, one short headline, one text link. No grid above the fold.
nodes.implementation: A section at 88svh with the image absolutely positioned; a bottom strip with a translucent bg tint; headline at clamp(2rem, 5vw, 4.5rem) weight 400.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Only one image and one line, which depends on the photograph being good.

nodes.name: Category tiles opening
nodes.what: The first screen is a flat grid of six square category tiles separated by hairlines, each with the category name in the corner; no hero copy at all.
nodes.implementation: A 3-column grid with 1px gaps on the hairline colour; tiles aspect-ratio 1; names at lg size bottom left.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Structure instead of a welcome message; common on utilitarian commerce sites.

nodes.name: Editorial product grid
nodes.what: Products laid out on a four-column grid with uneven spans (one wide, one tall), a mono index on each tile and the price on the same line as the name.
nodes.implementation: CSS grid with grid-auto-rows and span classes; the index at 11px mono top right; name and price in a flex row.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Uneven spans and indices look edited; equal cards look generated.

nodes.name: Sticky buy column
nodes.what: The product page stacks all photos in a left column while the buy box (name, price, option, add to cart, a short specification sheet) stays sticky on the right.
nodes.implementation: A two-column grid with align-items start; the info column position sticky top 88px; a dl spec sheet with hairline rows.
nodes.ai_tell_note: The commerce standard for considered purchases.

nodes.name: Broadsheet masthead
nodes.what: A newspaper masthead: a date line and issue number in mono between hairlines, the title at poster size centred, a second rule with the section names, then the nav.
nodes.implementation: A grid header with two mono lines and a display name at clamp(3rem, 9vw, 7rem); 2px rule under the whole block.
nodes.ai_tell_note: A masthead with a real date and issue number reads as a publication, not a blog template.

nodes.name: Side notes column
nodes.what: Reading layout with a narrow column of numbered side notes beside the prose; the lead image carries a figure caption.
nodes.implementation: A grid of measure plus 220px; notes at sm size with an index and a hairline above each.
nodes.ai_tell_note: A print device no template ships.

nodes.name: Archive index list
nodes.what: Further reading as an archive index: a mono date column, the title in the heading face, a reading time at the right, hairlines between rows and an entry count above.
nodes.implementation: Grid rows 8ch 1fr auto; hover underlines the title; count in mono.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Lists with dates and counts look maintained; three cards look generated.

nodes.name: Icon rail shell
nodes.what: The application shell is a 56px rail with the wordmark initial, one glyph per section and the avatar at the bottom; the work area takes the rest.
nodes.implementation: A 56px first grid column; 36px square links; aria-current highlighted with a primary tint.
nodes.ai_tell_note: A rail says the product is used all day; a labelled sidebar is the template.

nodes.name: Ledger table
nodes.what: Data tables without a box: mono column headers, hairline rows only, lowercase status words instead of coloured pills, tabular numerals right-aligned.
nodes.implementation: Transparent table; th in mono 11px; borders only between rows; font-variant-numeric tabular-nums.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Status pills in five colours are the dashboard tell; a ledger reads as serious.

nodes.name: Inspector panel
nodes.what: The detail view is an inspector: a tabbed column separated from the table by one hairline, no card, no shadow.
nodes.implementation: A column with border-left and padding; tabs on top from the component system.
nodes.ai_tell_note: A panel inside a card inside a page is the template.

nodes.name: Command palette first
nodes.what: A command palette sits at the top of the work area as the primary way in: a search line with a K key cap and the first four commands listed.
nodes.implementation: A 560px panel, sticky top, with an input row and a list; the real palette opens on Cmd or Ctrl K.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Everywhere on developer tools since 2022; still the right call for keyboard products.

nodes.name: Acid lab
nodes.notes: Near-black, off-white and one acid green on under five percent of the page; the 2025 developer-tool signal colour.

nodes.name: Paper & signal red
nodes.notes: Warm paper, near-black ink and a signal red used for one rule, one word, one button.

nodes.name: Archive ink
nodes.notes: Off-white and ink with the browser's own link blue as the only colour; reads as an index, not a brand.

nodes.name: Raw document
nodes.notes: White, black, default link blue and visited purple: the honest document look of text-first sites.

nodes.name: Night grain
nodes.notes: Warm near-black with grain, bone text and an amber accent; the warm dark of Warp and Resend rather than blue-black.

nodes.name: Phosphor
nodes.notes: Black glass and phosphor green with a yellow warning tone; terminals, hardware, play.

nodes.name: Cobalt & cream
nodes.notes: Cream canvas with International Klein Blue blocks and a coral counterpoint; colour as structure.

nodes.name: Stone & serif
nodes.notes: Stone white, warm black and a deep teal for links; built for very large serif type and long reading.

nodes.name: Signal orange
nodes.notes: Mistral's cream and sunset orange with a yellow stripe colour; loud, warm and flat.

nodes.name: Clay canvas
nodes.notes: Anthropic's canvas, ink and clay with an olive second colour; soft without being pastel.

nodes.name: Graphite & coral
nodes.notes: Raycast's near-black with a coral accent and an amber second tone; glass only where there is depth.

nodes.name: Bone & teal
nodes.notes: Perplexity's bone white, warm text and a single teal; quiet, trustworthy, no second colour.

nodes.name: Bricolage Grotesque / Instrument Sans
nodes.notes: A grotesque with ink traps and optical sizes over a quiet grotesque; the pair reads as one voice with two volumes.

nodes.name: Big Shoulders / Work Sans
nodes.notes: A condensed display face at poster size with a plain grotesque body; the condensation does the work, no weight games.

nodes.name: Newsreader / Hanken Grotesk
nodes.notes: A newspaper serif with optical sizes over a neutral grotesque; set the serif at 300 for display and 400 for text.

nodes.name: Libre Caslon Display / Libre Franklin
nodes.notes: Caslon at display size only, Franklin for everything else; the American magazine pair.

nodes.name: Gloock / Instrument Sans
nodes.notes: A high-contrast didone for the H1 alone over a low-contrast grotesque body.

nodes.name: Familjen Grotesk / Martian Mono
nodes.notes: One grotesque superfamily with a wide mono for labels, dates and counts; the archive and index voice.

nodes.name: Martian Mono / Familjen Grotesk
nodes.notes: A wide mono for headings at modest sizes with a grotesque body; headings stay under 48px.

nodes.name: Doto / Geist
nodes.notes: A dot-matrix display face for the H1 and labels, a neutral grotesque for text; the pixel register without a pixel body.

nodes.name: Pixelify Sans / IBM Plex Sans
nodes.notes: A pixel display face at large sizes only, Plex for reading; both come from engineering lineages.

nodes.name: Funnel Display / Funnel Sans
nodes.notes: A 2024 superfamily with a display cut whose tight apertures read as drawn, not defaulted.

nodes.name: Geologica / JetBrains Mono
nodes.notes: A variable geometric with a slant and sharpness axis; one family, two weights, no second voice.

nodes.name: Mona Sans / Kode Mono
nodes.notes: GitHub's variable sans with a width axis for headlines, and a mono with a visible personality for labels.

nodes.name: Kode Mono / Mona Sans
nodes.notes: A mono with character for headings under 48px, a variable sans body.

nodes.name: Parkinsans / Hanken Grotesk
nodes.notes: A geometric with soft terminals for headlines over a plain grotesque.

nodes.name: Bodoni Moda / Hanken Grotesk
nodes.notes: A variable didone with optical sizes over a plain grotesk; the fashion pair at any size.

nodes.name: Italiana / Hanken Grotesk
nodes.notes: A calligraphic display face for one line per page, a plain grotesque body.

nodes.name: Cormorant Garamond / Geist
nodes.notes: Cormorant at 10rem and above, where its small x-height becomes elegance; Geist keeps the page quiet beneath.

nodes.name: Acid lab
nodes.summary: Black, off-white and one acid green on a visible grid; mono labels, bordered cells with corner crosses, a marquee of real nouns, dithered artwork.
tells_to_avoid: neon on dark for a non-technical product

nodes.name: Paper & signal
nodes.summary: Warm paper, a transitional serif at broadsheet scale, hairline rules, signal red on one rule and one word; dates, issue numbers and archive lists everywhere.

nodes.name: Archive index
nodes.summary: An index rather than a brochure: one grotesque, a wide mono for dates and counts, hover rows that reveal images, ledger lists, a colophon with the local time.

nodes.name: Raw document
nodes.summary: A web page that admits it is a document: system serif, default link blue, visible borders, tables, no cards, no shadows, square buttons with brackets; honest to the point of style.

nodes.name: Night grain
nodes.summary: Warm near-black with film grain, a serif display at scale, one amber accent, strands of generated line art, a single giant quote and a colophon; dark without the blue glow.

nodes.name: Phosphor terminal
nodes.summary: Black glass, phosphor green, a dot-matrix display face for the one big line, mono everywhere else, scanlines, ASCII artwork and bracket buttons; hardware and terminal brands.

nodes.name: Cobalt block
nodes.summary: Cream and International Klein Blue in full-bleed blocks, a display face stacked one word per line, the nav inverting over each block, fill-up buttons and a coral counter-colour used once.

nodes.name: Giant serif
nodes.summary: A serif at ten rem and above as the whole image, a letter or manifesto as the first screen, side notes, hanging punctuation, warm stone white and one deep link colour; built for words.
tells_to_avoid: italic serif as the only idea

nodes.name: Signal orange
nodes.summary: Cream, warm black and a sunset orange used hard: a condensed display face, stickers with true words, a stat wall of sourced figures, a ticket call to action, flat everywhere.

nodes.name: Clay canvas
nodes.summary: Anthropic's canvas: warm off-white, ink, one clay accent and an olive second; a serif body at reading size, cream and ink bands, captioned figures, hairline accordions, a colophon. Soft without pastel or gradient.
tells_to_avoid: cream plus terracotta as the whole idea

nodes.name: Figma

traits: seven decorative colour blocks incl. navy

nodes.notes: 86px display at weight 340; eyebrow 18px +0.54px tracking; seven decorative colour blocks incl. navy; magenta #ff3d8b promo only; mono eyebrows and captions

nodes.name: Lovable

traits: DM Mono terminals, Instrument Serif rare italics

nodes.notes: warm brown-black dark #2b2622; seven colours total, 3 to 4px radii; ink at .83 .82 .40 .04 alpha ramps; DM Mono terminals, Instrument Serif rare italics

nodes.name: GitHub
nodes.notes: Mona Sans at weights 425 460 480; dark #0d1117 with #000 hero bands; link blue #8dd6ff lifted for dark; Copilot gradient as one scene; green #5fed83 glow only

nodes.name: Medium

traits: one green illustration as the only colour

nodes.notes: cream #f7f4ed canvas; 120px GT Super at line-height 0.83; all weights 400; zero radius except pill CTA; one green illustration as the only colour

nodes.name: Zed

traits: IBM Plex Serif display 72px at weight 340

nodes.notes: warm paper #f5f5f3 with #eeede9 #e7e6e1 steps; IBM Plex Serif display 72px at weight 340; iA Writer body and mono; cobalt #004edb single accent; 4px CTA radius, warm hairline #e2e2de

nodes.name: UNCUT.wtf

traits: Uncut Sans for everything, unicase ink-trap logo

nodes.notes: grey canvas; Uncut Sans for everything, unicase ink-trap logo; strong size contrast; grid or list toggle; red animated hearts on credits

nodes.name: Narrow old-style serif, display only
nodes.what: A condensed old-style display serif (Instrument Serif is the free one; Gloock or Libre Caslon Display are alternatives) set only at 72 to 120px, weight 400, line-height 0.95 to 1.0, letter-spacing -0.01em to -0.02em, never below 40px and never as body. Body stays in a plain grotesk at 16 to 18px so the serif is a headline voice, not a theme.
nodes.why: The narrow proportions give large headlines the density of a magazine masthead while the plain body keeps the page quiet.
nodes.implementation: h1{font-family:'Instrument Serif',serif;font-size:clamp(3rem,9vw,7.5rem);line-height:.95;letter-spacing:-.015em;text-wrap:balance;text-box-trim:trim-both;text-box-edge:cap alphabetic}
nodes.pitfalls: Dropping it into an otherwise Inter page as a single italic word is now the most recognised generated-site cliche.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Instrument Serif itself is on the 2026 list of fonts that flag vibe-coded sites; it only reads handmade when it carries the whole headline system at true display sizes with a non-default body face.

nodes.name: Bricolage Grotesque optical-size headlines
nodes.what: Bricolage Grotesque (Google Fonts, 2023) carries three axes: opsz 12 to 96, wdth 75 to 100, wght 200 to 800. Headlines use opsz 96, wdth 75 to 85 and wght 700 to 800 so the exaggerated ink traps and nervous Grotesque No. 9 character show; body uses opsz 12 at wght 400 where the same family turns neutral. One family, two personalities, zero extra font files.
nodes.why: The optical-size axis gives you an expressive display cut and a calm text cut from one variable file, which no default stack does.
nodes.implementation: h1{font-family:'Bricolage Grotesque';font-variation-settings:'opsz' 96,'wdth' 80;font-weight:800} body{font-optical-sizing:auto}
nodes.pitfalls: Leaving font-optical-sizing on auto at 18px body gives the neutral cut, but setting opsz 96 at body sizes makes text look clumsy.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Appears mostly on independent culture and exhibition sites; generators rarely touch the width or opsz axes.

nodes.name: Fraunces SOFT and WONK axes
nodes.what: Fraunces (Google Fonts) exposes SOFT 0 to 100 (ink-spread, Cooper-like) and WONK 0 or 1 (leaning n, m, h and flagged terminals) alongside opsz 9 to 144 and wght 100 to 900. Display at opsz 144, SOFT 80 to 100, WONK 1, wght 500 to 700; body at opsz 9 to 14, SOFT 0, WONK 0. The wonky alternates are what make a headline look drawn rather than typeset.
nodes.why: Turning on alternates only at display size produces a handmade signature without a second typeface.
nodes.implementation: h1{font-family:Fraunces;font-variation-settings:'opsz' 144,'SOFT' 90,'WONK' 1;font-weight:600;line-height:1}
nodes.pitfalls: Fraunces is on the 2026 vibe-coded font list; using it at default settings (SOFT 0, WONK 0) in a centred hero is exactly the generated look.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Default Fraunces is a tell; axis-driven Fraunces with WONK on and large opsz is not, because generators do not set font-variation-settings.

nodes.name: Mono as the label voice
nodes.what: All eyebrows, captions, nav items, table headers and metadata set in a monospace at 11 to 13px, uppercase, letter-spacing 0.06 to 0.1em, in the muted text colour; headlines and body stay proportional. Seen as Diatype Mono (Speakeasy), DM Mono (Dirty Vine), Geist Mono at 12 to 13px (Vercel), Anthropic Mono eyebrows, LatteraMonoLL at 11px (Nothing). Free equivalents: DM Mono, Geist Mono, JetBrains Mono, Fragment Mono, Commit Mono.
nodes.why: A second voice for system text makes hierarchy legible without extra sizes or colours.
nodes.implementation: .eyebrow{font:500 12px/1.3 'DM Mono',ui-monospace,monospace;text-transform:uppercase;letter-spacing:.08em;color:var(--ink-muted)}
nodes.pitfalls: Krebs counts all-caps section labels on 10.5% of Show HN sites; it only works when mono labels are small, few, and the headline is clearly a different face.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Uppercase mono eyebrows are now common on generated dark pages; the handmade version keeps them to one per section at 11 to 12px with real tabular data nearby.

nodes.name: Ultralight display weights 100 to 340
nodes.what: Headlines set at weights well below 400: Figma 86px at weight 340, ElevenLabs Waldenburg 300, Stripe Sohne 300, Teenage Engineering 100 to 300, Nothing NType82 at 100, Mercury 480 display over 360 body. Free faces that hold up thin: Hanken Grotesk (100), Geist (100), Mona Sans (200), Sofia Sans (1 to 1000), Archivo (100), Epilogue (100). Pair with slightly positive tracking (+0.2 to +0.5px) because thin strokes read tighter.
nodes.why: Thin large type reads as considered and expensive because it demands a quiet layout and a high-resolution screen.
nodes.implementation: h1{font-family:'Hanken Grotesk';font-weight:200;font-size:clamp(2.5rem,7vw,5.5rem);letter-spacing:.005em;line-height:1.05}
nodes.pitfalls: Below 300 on a 16px body fails contrast and shimmers on low-DPI screens; keep ultralight to 40px and above.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Generated pages default to 600 to 700 semibold headlines; weight 300 and below is a deliberate choice.

nodes.name: Tracking scaled to size
nodes.what: Letter-spacing tightens as a percentage of size rather than a fixed value: Linear 80px/-3px (-3.75%), 56px/-1.8px, 28px/-0.6px, 16px/-0.05px; Framer 110px/-5.5px (-5%); Vercel 48px/-2.4px to 20px/-0.6px; Supabase 64px/-1.92px (-3%); Cursor 72px/-2.16px. Rule of thumb: -0.05em at 96px, -0.03em at 48px, -0.01em at 24px, 0 at 16px, +0.02 to +0.06em below 13px.
nodes.why: Optical spacing changes with size, and a single tracking value makes either the hero loose or the captions cramped.
nodes.implementation: Define per step: --t-96:-.05em;--t-48:-.03em;--t-24:-.01em;--t-16:0;--t-12:.06em and apply with the size token
nodes.pitfalls: Applying -0.05em to a geometric sans with already tight sidebearings makes r-n pairs collide; test with 'rn' and 'cl'.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Generators apply tracking-tight uniformly; a proportional ladder is invisible but reads as polished.

nodes.name: Display leading at or below 1.0
nodes.what: Headline line-height between 0.83 and 1.05 while body stays at 1.5 to 1.6: Medium 120px at 0.83, Figma 86px at 1.0, Resend 96px at 1.0, Granola 68px/68px, Linear 1.05, Mercury 96px at 1.0. Combine with text-box-trim so the cap height sits flush to the container edge and the gap above the first line disappears.
nodes.why: Tight stacks turn a two-line headline into one solid shape that anchors the hero without a background box.
nodes.implementation: h1{line-height:.92;text-box-trim:trim-both;text-box-edge:cap alphabetic;margin-block-end:.5em}
nodes.pitfalls: Below 0.9 descenders of line one touch ascenders of line two; only works with mostly-lowercase or all-caps headlines.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Default framework headings sit at 1.1 to 1.2; 0.9 is a visible authorial decision.

nodes.name: Serif display, sans UI, mono code
nodes.what: Three roles, three faces: a text serif at display size (IBM Plex Serif 72px weight 340 at Zed; IBM Plex Serif 54px at Railway; Quadrant at Granola; Waldenburg 300 at ElevenLabs; Anthropic Serif at 88 to 90px), a humanist sans for UI and body (Inter, iA Writer, Melange), and a mono for code or labels. Free trio: Newsreader or Literata or Source Serif 4 at opsz 72 for display, Hanken Grotesk or Switzer or General Sans for UI, JetBrains Mono or Geist Mono for code.
nodes.why: Each role gets a voice built for it, so hierarchy survives even when sizes are close.
nodes.implementation: --font-display:'Newsreader',serif;--font-ui:'Hanken Grotesk',sans-serif;--font-code:'JetBrains Mono',monospace; h1{font-family:var(--font-display);font-weight:400;font-optical-sizing:auto}
nodes.pitfalls: Picking a display-only serif (Playfair, Instrument Serif) for the serif role makes 24px subheads spindly; use a text serif with an opsz axis.
nodes.ai_tell_note: The generated version is 'Inter plus one serif italic word'; the handmade version uses a text serif as a full headline system at weights 300 to 400.

nodes.name: Variable weights off the hundreds
nodes.what: Weights chosen between the standard stops using a variable font: GitHub Mona Sans at 425 (hero), 460 and 480 (h2, cards); Mercury 480 display, 360 body, 420 UI; Figma 340, 330, 320, 540; Zed 340 serif display; Shopify 330 display, 420 and 550 body. A 20 to 60 unit offset from 400 or 500 changes texture without reading as bold.
nodes.why: Odd weights give a custom-cut feel because nobody ships a static 425 file.
nodes.implementation: @font-face{font-family:'Mona Sans';src:url(MonaSans[wdth,wght].woff2) format('woff2-variations');font-weight:200 900} h1{font-weight:425}
nodes.pitfalls: Requires the variable file; a static fallback snaps to 400 and the body suddenly looks heavier on the fallback.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Generated CSS uses font-semibold and font-bold; a weight of 460 is a hand-set value.

nodes.name: Optical size axis, body vs display
nodes.what: Choose faces with an opsz axis and let it work: Newsreader 6 to 72, Literata 7 to 72, Source Serif 4 8 to 60, Fraunces 9 to 144, Bodoni Moda 6 to 96, Imbue 10 to 100, Merriweather (2024 variable rebuild) 18 to 144, Big Shoulders (2025 rebuild) 10 to 72, DM Sans 9 to 40, Roboto Flex 8 to 144, Google Sans Flex 1 to 144. At 14px the strokes thicken and spacing opens; at 96px contrast sharpens. Set font-optical-sizing:auto and size in px or rem so the browser maps correctly.
nodes.why: Text sizes get the sturdiness they need and headlines get the finesse, exactly as metal type did.
nodes.implementation: @import url('https://fonts.googleapis.com/css2?family=Newsreader:opsz,wght@6..72,200..800&display=swap'); html{font-optical-sizing:auto}
nodes.pitfalls: Loading only a static 'Display' cut and using it at 16px is the common failure; the Google Fonts CSS API needs the opsz range requested.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Invisible as a feature but it is why handmade editorial sites look crisp at every size.

nodes.name: Width axis for compressed headlines
nodes.what: Use the wdth axis instead of a separate condensed family: Mona Sans and Hubot Sans 75 to 125, Archivo 62 to 125, Anybody 50 to 150, Mozilla Headline (2025) 75 to 125, League Gothic 75 to 100, Instrument Sans 75 to 100, Martian Mono 75 to 112.5, Roboto Flex 25 to 151. Headlines at wdth 75 to 85 and wght 700 to 800; body at wdth 100. Hubot Sans at wdth 75 reads as a tech poster face.
nodes.why: Compressed headlines fit more words per line at larger sizes, so heroes can be set in two lines at 9vw.
nodes.implementation: h1{font-family:'Hubot Sans';font-stretch:78%;font-weight:750;line-height:.9;text-transform:uppercase}
nodes.pitfalls: Animating wdth on hover reflows the whole line; only animate on elements with a fixed width.
nodes.ai_tell_note: font-stretch is almost never emitted by generators.

nodes.name: Stylistic sets to de-default a sans
nodes.what: Turn on OpenType alternates so a familiar family stops looking stock: Vercel sets Inter ss01 and ss02; Raycast sets calt, kern, liga, ss03 site-wide and ss02 plus ss08 at display with liga off; Framer uses cv01, cv05, cv09, cv11, ss03, ss07; Stripe sets ss01 on body; Mercury ss03 on every family. Instrument Sans ships 12 stylistic sets; Kode Mono ss01 swaps D, Q, 8. On Geist or Hanken Grotesk the single-storey a and open 6/9 change the whole texture.
nodes.why: Alternates alter the most frequent letters, so the same font reads as a custom cut.
nodes.implementation: body{font-feature-settings:'ss01','ss03','cv11'} h1{font-feature-settings:'ss02','ss08','liga' 0}
nodes.pitfalls: Inter with ss01 is still Inter; the trick only breaks the tell when applied to a less-seen family.
nodes.ai_tell_note: font-feature-settings is rarely in generated CSS, and the alternate glyph shapes are what people subconsciously notice.

nodes.name: Tabular numerals and slashed zero
nodes.what: Numbers in pricing, tables, timers and stats set with font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums (Stripe applies tnum to money and numeric cells; Clerk ships a 'geistNumbers' cut; Linear uses Linear Mono for figures). Pair with slashed-zero and a mono or a sans with true tabular figures (Geist, Martian Mono, JetBrains Mono, IBM Plex Mono, Source Serif 4 has tnum too). Prices at 48 to 64px in tnum with the currency symbol at 60% size, superscript-aligned.
nodes.why: Columns of figures align and animate without jitter, which is what makes a dashboard or pricing table feel engineered.
nodes.implementation: .num{font-variant-numeric:tabular-nums slashed-zero;font-feature-settings:'tnum','zero'} .price sup{font-size:.6em;vertical-align:.5em}
nodes.pitfalls: Not every free font has tabular figures (Instrument Serif does not); check the tnum feature before relying on it.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Stat banners are a Krebs tell (12.2%), but aligned tabular figures in a real table are the opposite signal.

nodes.name: Pixel and dot-matrix type as product voice
nodes.what: A dot or pixel face used for one role only, usually product names or counters: Nothing sets product names in Ndot at 20 to 40px uppercase while body is a proportional sans; Apagao (2025) uses Doto with a mono. Free variable options: Doto (ROND 0 to 100, wght 100 to 900), Tiny5 (BLED, JITT, ROND, wdth 50 to 200), Workbench and Sixtyfour (BLED and SCAN axes), Handjet (23 element shapes), Bitcount (2025, CRSV, ELSH, ELXP, slnt), Silkscreen, Jersey 10, Micro 5, Departure Mono.
nodes.why: One dotted word on an otherwise clean page gives a hardware or terminal personality without a theme.
nodes.implementation: .product-name{font-family:Doto;font-variation-settings:'ROND' 60;font-weight:700;text-transform:uppercase;letter-spacing:.04em}
nodes.pitfalls: Pixel type for body or more than one role turns into a retro-game theme.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Rare in generated output; the risk is cliche (hacker terminal), not AI.

nodes.name: Viewport-scaled type, no breakpoints
nodes.what: Every size is a calc against 100vw instead of a breakpoint table: Teenage Engineering sets display 40px, nav 23px, body 19px and labels 13px as calc(100vw * k) with weights 100 to 300 in a mono-ish grotesk. The whole page scales like a printed sheet; nothing reflows into a 'mobile layout'.
nodes.why: Proportions stay identical on every screen, which gives the page the feel of a fixed-format object.
nodes.implementation: :root{--u:calc(100vw/1440)} h1{font-size:max(28px,calc(40*var(--u)))} body{font-size:max(14px,calc(19*var(--u)))}
nodes.pitfalls: Pure vw sizes ignore user zoom and get tiny on phones; mix with rem (clamp) and set a floor of 14px for body.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Generators emit Tailwind breakpoint classes; a vw-based scale is a different mental model.

nodes.name: Ink-trap grotesque headline
nodes.what: A grotesk whose notched joins show at 48px and above: Familjen Grotesk (free, notches described as ink traps, tall x-height), Bricolage Grotesque compressed cuts, Uncut Sans (unicase logo with ink traps on uncut.wtf), Fivo Sans Modern (free display with large traps), Schibsted Grotesk. Set at 56 to 96px weight 600 to 700 with -0.02em so the traps read as deliberate cuts.
nodes.why: The traps add a drawn, slightly industrial detail that a neo-grotesque like Inter or Helvetica lacks.
nodes.implementation: h1{font-family:'Familjen Grotesk';font-weight:700;font-size:clamp(2.5rem,7vw,6rem);letter-spacing:-.02em}
nodes.pitfalls: At body size the traps fill in and the face just looks like any grotesk, so choose it for the headline role only.
nodes.ai_tell_note: None of these families appear on the vibe-coded list; Familjen Grotesk is on Google Fonts yet rarely chosen.

nodes.name: Quirky 19th-century grotesque
nodes.what: Replace the neutral neo-grotesque with a crude, irregular one: paid references are Apercu, Mabry, Founders Grotesk, Dia (Typewolf's quirky list); free versions with the same irregularity are Uncut Sans (12 weights), Overused Grotesk, Nacelle, Apfel Grotezk (Collletttivo), Karrik (deliberately uneven weights), Terminal Grotesque (Velvetyne), Authentic Sans, Archivo. Use it for everything including body so the quirk becomes the brand, with a quiet mono for labels.
nodes.why: Irregular letterforms read as human-made at every size, so even a plain layout feels authored.
nodes.implementation: @font-face{font-family:'Uncut Sans';src:url(UncutSans-Variable.woff2);font-weight:300 700} body{font-family:'Uncut Sans',system-ui}
nodes.pitfalls: Space Grotesk is the quirky grotesk everyone reaches for and is now a flagged font; the others above are not.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Uncut Sans, Karrik and Apfel appear on fontsinuse in independent studio work through 2026, not in generated output.

nodes.name: Fontshare serif display pairs
nodes.what: Indian Type Foundry's free serifs used as display with a free sans for text: Boska (14 styles, high-contrast) with Inter at Tromso Kunstforening 2024; Zodiak (14 styles) with Cabinet Grotesk at SisInBiz 2026 and with JetBrains Mono at AL BIES; Sentient (12 styles) with Aether Mono; Erode, Gambetta, Recia, Rowan, Bespoke Serif, Melodrama are the others. Display at 64 to 96px weight 300 to 400 italic; text in Switzer, General Sans or Author at 16 to 17px.
nodes.why: These serifs have real italics and multiple weights, so one family covers hero, pull quotes and captions with no licence.
nodes.implementation: @font-face{font-family:Zodiak;src:url(Zodiak-Variable.woff2) format('woff2');font-weight:100 900} h1{font-family:Zodiak;font-weight:300;font-style:italic}
nodes.pitfalls: Fontshare's own CSS API serves fixed weights; self-host the variable files to use intermediate weights and italics properly.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Satoshi and Clash Display are overexposed through Webflow templates; the serif side of Fontshare is still rarely seen.

nodes.name: Satoshi plus Clash Display template duo
nodes.what: The Fontshare pairing that ships with hundreds of Framer and Webflow templates: Clash Display 600 to 700 headlines over Satoshi 400 body, usually with -0.03em tracking and a dark canvas. Cabinet Grotesk heavy headlines are the sibling version (Matt Imling portfolio, Wieniawski Society 2025, Popina 2024).
nodes.why: It works because Clash Display is genuinely a strong geometric display face, which is also why everyone picked it.
nodes.implementation: If you must: use Clash Display only at 80px plus with tight leading and pair it with a serif or mono body, never Satoshi.
nodes.pitfalls: Included only as a warning: in 2025 to 2026 this pair signals 'template' as strongly as Inter signals 'default'.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Satoshi is now the second most common free sans after Inter in AI-built landing pages; Clash Display headlines mark Framer templates.

nodes.name: Serif italic accent word in sans hero
nodes.what: A sans headline (usually Inter, Geist or Space Grotesk) with one word swapped to Instrument Serif italic, often coloured. Krebs's April 2026 audit of 1,590 Show HN sites names this exact move as a core 'vibe-coded' pattern, together with the Space Grotesk, Instrument Serif and Geist trio.
nodes.why: It once worked because contrast of style inside one line draws the eye; overuse killed the effect.
nodes.implementation: Do not emit <em class='serif'> inside h1. If mixing faces, mix whole lines or use a Velvetyne display for the entire headline.
nodes.pitfalls: Any mixed-face headline now needs a different logic (a whole clause, a different weight, a hand-drawn face) or it reads as generated.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Named explicitly as a tell in the 2026 analysis; avoid in drafts.

nodes.name: Space Grotesk, Instrument Serif, Geist trio
nodes.what: The three faces that the 2026 Show HN audit lists as the font signature of generated sites (with Syne and Fraunces as runners-up): Space Grotesk headlines, Instrument Serif accents, Geist or Inter body, often all three together. Modal Digital (2025) pairs Space Grotesk with Instrument Sans; Sommerfest 25 pairs Instrument Serif with Geist.
nodes.why: Each is a good free font with a distinct voice, which is exactly why models converged on them.
nodes.implementation: Substitutes: Hanken Grotesk or Switzer for Geist; Familjen Grotesk or Uncut Sans for Space Grotesk; Newsreader or Zodiak or Gloock for Instrument Serif.
nodes.pitfalls: Listed so the draft generator can blacklist the combination; any one of them alone is defensible, the trio is not.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Quoted by name in the design-slop audit; 15.8% of audited sites used these combos in the GIGAZINE summary.

nodes.name: Inter for everything
nodes.what: Inter at 400/600 for hero, body, buttons and labels, centred, on white or #0a0a0a. Krebs lists 'Inter used for everything, especially centered hero headlines' as pattern one; Inter logged 414 billion Google Fonts views in the year to May 2025. Even Linear, Raycast and Framer that use Inter do so with Inter Display, stylistic sets or a second display face.
nodes.why: It is the safest UI face ever drawn, which is why it carries no information about the brand.
nodes.implementation: Avoid font-family:Inter in marketing CSS; if used for UI set font-feature-settings:'ss01','cv11' and pair with a different display family.
nodes.pitfalls: If Inter is required (product UI), keep it out of the hero and add a display face; otherwise swap to Hanken Grotesk, Instrument Sans, Mona Sans, Switzer or General Sans.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Pattern one in the 2026 audit.

nodes.name: Condensed poster gothic hero
nodes.what: Heavy condensed sans at 12 to 16vw uppercase, line-height 0.85, tracking 0 to +0.01em: Anton (Fermented Films 2024, Sage Space 2024, Panaille with League Gothic), Big Shoulders (2025 rebuild with opsz 10 to 72 and wght 100 to 900), League Gothic (wdth axis), Oswald, Anton SC (2024 small caps). Body stays small and light so the headline is a poster, not a heading.
nodes.why: Condensed heavy caps let a two-word headline fill the viewport width and feel printed rather than typed.
nodes.implementation: h1{font-family:'Big Shoulders';font-variation-settings:'opsz' 72;font-weight:800;font-size:14vw;line-height:.85;text-transform:uppercase;text-wrap:balance}
nodes.pitfalls: Bebas Neue is the 2015 version of this move and reads as a template; use Anton, Big Shoulders or League Gothic with a wdth tweak.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Generated heroes are centred semibold sans at 48 to 64px; a 14vw condensed cap headline is a poster designer's choice.

nodes.name: Reading-size serif body, 18 to 24px
nodes.what: Body prose in a text serif at 18 to 24px with line-height 1.4 to 1.5 and a 60 to 70ch measure: Anthropic body-lg 24px in its serif, Medium reading serif, Substack post body in a serif (substitutes named: Source Serif 4, Newsreader, Spectral), Daylight's Grenette. Free faces with text-grade italics and opsz: Newsreader, Literata, Source Serif 4, Crimson Pro, Spectral, EB Garamond.
nodes.why: Large serif prose signals that the words are the product, which is why AI labs and publishers converge on it.
nodes.implementation: .prose{font-family:Newsreader,serif;font-size:1.25rem;line-height:1.45;max-inline-size:65ch;font-optical-sizing:auto;hanging-punctuation:first}
nodes.pitfalls: Serif body under 16px on screens looks thin; use opsz-aware fonts and never go below 17px.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Generated pages keep body in a 16px sans; a 20px Newsreader paragraph is an editorial decision.

nodes.name: Humanist sans instead of Inter
nodes.what: A warm, slightly irregular sans for UI and body: Hanken Grotesk (100 to 900), Figtree (Makelog 2023, AELAQ 2024), Onest, Albert Sans, Instrument Sans (12 stylistic sets, wdth axis), Mona Sans (GitHub homepage 2022, Dribbble 2023), Atkinson Hyperlegible Next (2025, with Newsreader at Daylit Studio), Inclusive Sans (Connessioni estetiche 2025), Schibsted Grotesk, Switzer and General Sans from Fontshare. Set body at 16 to 17px weight 400 to 450 with -0.005em.
nodes.why: Humanist proportions carry warmth at text sizes, and none of these is yet a default.
nodes.implementation: body{font-family:'Hanken Grotesk',system-ui;font-weight:430;font-size:17px;line-height:1.55;letter-spacing:-.005em}
nodes.pitfalls: Plus Jakarta Sans, Manrope, DM Sans and Poppins are the previous generation of 'not Inter' and now read as 2021 templates.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Geist is flagged; Hanken, Instrument Sans, Mona Sans and Atkinson Next are not.

nodes.name: Variable axis animated on scroll
nodes.what: Drive a custom font axis from scroll or hover instead of animating transform: Climate Crisis has a YEAR axis 1979 to 2050 built for exactly this; Doto ROND 0 to 100 rounds the dots; Tiny5 JITT and BLED; Fraunces SOFT and WONK; Geologica SHRP and CRSV; Afacad Flux slnt -14 to 14; Roboto Flex GRAD -200 to 150 (weight change without reflow). Register the axis value with @property and bind it to animation-timeline: scroll().
nodes.why: The letterforms themselves change, which is a kind of motion no stock template produces.
nodes.implementation: @property --yr{syntax:'<number>';inherits:true;initial-value:1979} h1{font-family:'Climate Crisis';font-variation-settings:'YEAR' var(--yr);animation:melt linear both;animation-timeline:scroll()} @keyframes melt{to{--yr:2050}}
nodes.pitfalls: Animating wght or wdth reflows text every frame; prefer GRAD, SOFT, ROND, YEAR, which keep advance widths, and respect prefers-reduced-motion.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Requires @property and font-variation-settings knowledge that generated CSS does not show.

nodes.name: Serif italic dek paragraph
nodes.what: The subhead under a sans headline is a 20 to 28px serif, often italic, with slightly negative tracking: Arc deks at 20 to 24px in ABC Oracle, Medium dek-serif 28px -0.5px, Figma subhead 26px at weight 340, Lovable's 'rare editorial italics' in Instrument Serif.
