Free: Newsreader Italic at opsz 24, Literata Italic, Fraunces Italic, Gambetta Italic, Erode Italic, Zodiak Italic. Weight 300 to 400, colour one step muted, measure 40 to 50ch.
nodes.why: The dek carries tone while the headline carries message, and the serif makes the paragraph read as a sentence rather than a tagline.
nodes.implementation: .dek{font-family:Newsreader,serif;font-style:italic;font-size:1.5rem;font-weight:300;line-height:1.3;letter-spacing:-.01em;color:var(--ink-2);max-inline-size:48ch}
nodes.pitfalls: If the italic is Instrument Serif and the headline is Inter you have rebuilt the tell; use a text serif italic at paragraph length.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Italic as a whole paragraph is different from italic as one accent word; keep it to the dek and keep the face a text serif.

nodes.name: Two monos: code vs labels
nodes.what: Code blocks and UI labels use different monospaces: Zed sets code in its writer-mono (iA Writer Mono lineage) while display is Plex Serif; Vercel keeps Geist Mono at 400 only, 12 to 13px; Cursor uses JetBrains Mono for code and an 11px uppercase sans caption for labels; Mintlify Geist Mono for code with Inter labels. Pick a ligature mono for code (JetBrains Mono, Google Sans Code 2024, Kode Mono with ss01, Commit Mono, Monaspace) and a plainer one for labels (DM Mono, Fragment Mono, Sometype Mono).
nodes.why: Code needs ligatures and tall x-height; labels need a quieter, more typographic mono, and using one for both compromises each.
nodes.implementation: pre,code{font-family:'JetBrains Mono',monospace;font-feature-settings:'liga','calt'} .label,kbd{font-family:'Fragment Mono',monospace;font-size:12px}
nodes.pitfalls: Two monos with similar x-heights look like a mistake; choose one with a visibly different voice (Fragment Mono's grotesk feel against JetBrains' tall forms).
nodes.ai_tell_note: Generated docs sites use one mono for everything.

nodes.name: Duospace body text (iA Writer Quattro)
nodes.what: Body copy in iA Writer Quattro or Duo, free SIL faces where most glyphs are monospaced but m, w and i get their own widths: Zed's body 'writer' family falls back to iA Writer Quattro; The Breach website; Saveku redesign 2026 (with Geist Mono); Linear's 2023 'Last Year You Said Next Year' campaign (with Redaction). Set at 16 to 18px, line-height 1.6, weight 400 to 500.
nodes.why: It reads like a draft typed by a person, which suits editors, note tools and anything that wants a writerly voice without a serif.
nodes.implementation: @font-face{font-family:'iA Writer Quattro';src:url(iAWriterQuattroS-Regular.woff2)} body{font-family:'iA Writer Quattro',monospace;font-size:17px;line-height:1.6}
nodes.pitfalls: Long paragraphs in a near-mono get tiring past 60ch; keep measure at 55ch and sizes 17px plus.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Not on Google Fonts, so generated stacks never pick it.

nodes.name: Redaction with pixel-degrade cuts
nodes.what: Redaction (free, by Titus Kaphar and Reginald Dwayne Betts with Forest Young and Jeremy Mickel) comes in a serif and a sans with degrade levels 10, 20, 35, 50, 70, 100 that progressively pixelate. Used by Linear's 2023 campaign (with iA Writer Quattro and Inter), Album Art Galerie website 2021 (with Manrope), Chandan Kolaparthi portfolio 2023 (with Sohne), Connessioni estetiche 2025 (with Inclusive Sans). Step the degrade across a scrolling sequence or use Redaction 35 for the hero and Redaction 10 for body.
nodes.why: The degradation is built into the glyphs, so a crisp page carries a deliberate glitch without filters.
nodes.implementation: @font-face{font-family:'Redaction 35';src:url(Redaction_35-Regular.woff2)} h1{font-family:'Redaction 35',serif;font-size:clamp(3rem,8vw,7rem)}
nodes.pitfalls: Degrade 70 and 100 are illegible below 48px; and the font's origin (a criminal-justice art project) deserves a credit line.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Not in any default library; it reads as a specific choice.

nodes.name: Libre experimental display for one word
nodes.what: A Velvetyne, Collletttivo or similar libre display face carries the hero word while everything else is plain: Avara (XOXO Fest 2024, Footnote c. 2024), Pilowlava (Readymag 'Read me!', Ultramorbidi 2025), Basteleur (Chicano Batman 2024, Blason 2025), Karrik (Le Braquet 2025, Tapered Construction 2024), Le Murmure, Terminal Grotesque, Savate (Velvetyne, on Google Fonts since 2025), Sprat (Collletttivo; Carretta 2025, Multiple Tomorrows 2026), Mazius Display, Ortica (Of Soil and Smoke 2026), Apfel Grotezk (BergamoScienza 2024, En Chantier 2026). Body in a mono or a humanist sans at 16px.
nodes.why: These faces were drawn as experiments, so a single word in one of them gives a studio-grade identity for free.
nodes.implementation: @font-face{font-family:Avara;src:url(Avara-Bold.woff2)} .hero-word{font-family:Avara;font-weight:700;font-size:16vw;line-height:.85}
nodes.pitfalls: Several Velvetyne faces lack a full character set or italics; check coverage and licence per font (OFL vs GPL).
nodes.ai_tell_note: These are absent from generated stacks and from most templates.

nodes.name: Atipo pay-what-you-want luxury serif
nodes.what: Atipo's pay-what-you-want families give a single free weight of a refined face: Argesta (display regular free) for fashion headlines, Salome and Calendas Plus (regular free) for editorial, Geomanist, Basier, Silka and Wotfard regular free for body, Chaney ultra-extended free. The Party by Ostbahnhof used Calendas Plus with Roslindale. Set Argesta at 72px plus with +0.01em tracking and a 300-weight sans body.
nodes.why: One premium-looking weight is enough for a headline system, and nobody expects a free font to look like this.
nodes.implementation: @font-face{font-family:Argesta;src:url(argesta-display-regular.woff2)} h1{font-family:Argesta;font-size:clamp(3rem,8vw,6.5rem);letter-spacing:.01em;font-weight:400}
nodes.pitfalls: Only one weight is free, so the system must be designed around size and case, not bold.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Atipo faces are not in Google Fonts or Fontshare and do not appear in generated output.

nodes.name: Newspaper Didone free serifs, display only
nodes.what: High-contrast headline serifs with thick-thin drama, used at 72px plus and never as body: Gloock (El Uniforme Menstrual 2026), Bodoni Moda (opsz 6 to 96), Libre Caslon Display, Imbue (opsz 10 to 100, condensed), Young Serif (bold old-style), Boska and Melodrama from Fontshare. Tracking -0.01em, leading 0.9, often two words stacked with a hairline rule.
nodes.why: Hairline serifs at display size read as fashion and newsprint, a register no sans reaches.
nodes.implementation: h1{font-family:Gloock,serif;font-size:clamp(3.5rem,10vw,9rem);line-height:.9;letter-spacing:-.01em}
nodes.pitfalls: Playfair Display is the 2014 version of this and marks a template; Gloock, Bodoni Moda and Imbue do not.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Generators reach for Playfair; the others are rarely emitted.

nodes.name: Warm paper canvas, not white
nodes.what: Page background a warm off-white in the #F4F1EA family instead of #fff: Anthropic #faf9f5 with cards #f0eee6; Cursor #f7f7f4 with soft #fafaf7; Zed #f5f5f3 then #eeede9 and #e7e6e1; PostHog #eeefe9; Lovable and Medium #f7f4ed; Perplexity #fdfbfa; Arc #fffcec; Granola #f7f7f2; Stripe's cream band #f5e9d4. White #fff is reserved for raised cards on top of the paper.
nodes.why: A tinted ground makes true white cards and photos lift without shadows and makes the whole page read as printed stock.
nodes.implementation: :root{--canvas:#f7f4ed;--card:#fff;--hairline:#e8e4da;--ink:#1c1917} or oklch: --canvas:oklch(97% .008 85)
nodes.pitfalls: Pairing a warm canvas with cool #e5e7eb (Tailwind gray) borders looks dirty; every neutral must share the hue.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Generated pages default to #ffffff or #0a0a0a; a #f7f4ed canvas with matching warm greys is a system decision.

nodes.name: Ink black that is not #000
nodes.what: Primary text and buttons in a near-black with a hint of warmth or cool: Anthropic #141413, Vercel and Supabase #171717, Mintlify #0a0a0a, Lovable #1c1c1c, Cursor #26251e, Perplexity #27251e, ElevenLabs #0c0a09 (Tailwind stone-950), Medium #242424, Substack #363737, Granola #292929, Zed #16181d (cool). Pure #000 appears only as a full-bleed band (Anthropic, Figma footer).
nodes.why: Off-black softens contrast on bright screens and lets the black carry the canvas temperature.
nodes.pitfalls: #111 on #fff with no hue is still a default; the trick is matching the black's hue to the canvas (warm on cream, blue-black on cool grey).
nodes.ai_tell_note: Tailwind's neutral-900 #171717 is itself common; shift to stone-950 #0c0a09 or a custom #1c1917 for warmth.

nodes.name: Single accent under five percent
nodes.what: One chromatic colour on a monochrome page, used for a handful of pixels: PostHog #f54e00 only on hover and text accents (its handbook forbids it for errors); Framer #0099ff only on links, focus rings and selected states; Zed #004edb on the h1 accent, CTA and links; Substack #ff6719; Figma #ff3d8b promo only; Supabase #3ecf8e as a dot and CTA; Claude's #d97757 only on research sub-pages. Everything else is ink, canvas and greys.
nodes.why: Scarcity makes the accent a wayfinding device and gives the brand a colour without a coloured page.
nodes.implementation: --accent:#f54e00; a:hover,.cta:hover,:focus-visible{color:var(--accent)} /* nothing else */
nodes.pitfalls: The accent on body text, on every button and on card borders at once is the coloured-stripe tell (13% of audited sites).
nodes.ai_tell_note: Generated palettes use the accent as a theme; handmade ones use it as a signal.

nodes.name: Ink is the brand (no accent)
nodes.what: No chromatic accent at all: Vercel's primary is #171717 ('the ink is the brand'); Teenage Engineering's primary button is a black rectangle; Nothing uses #000, #fff, #585a5a, #e5e7eb only; Medium's CTA is a #191919 pill; Resend and Raycast use a white CTA on near-black; Lovable #f7f5f0 CTA on #2b2622. Colour appears only in product photography or one illustration.
nodes.why: A page with zero hue forces attention onto type, spacing and imagery, which is where handmade work shows.
nodes.implementation: .btn-primary{background:var(--ink);color:var(--canvas);border-radius:0} :focus-visible{outline:2px solid var(--ink);outline-offset:2px}
nodes.pitfalls: Without colour, hierarchy must come from a strict grey ladder and at least one strong typographic move; otherwise it is just unfinished.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Generators almost always add an accent; its absence is a choice.

nodes.name: Near-black surface ladder in 3 to 5% steps
nodes.what: Dark mode depth from a ladder of near-blacks instead of grey cards: Linear #010102 canvas, #0f1011, #141516, #18191a, #191a1b surfaces; Raycast #07080a, #0d0d0d, #101111, #121212 with no drop shadows; Resend #000, #06060a, #0a0a0c, #101012; Framer #090909, #141414, #1c1c1c; GitHub #0d1117, #151a22, #24292f. Each step is roughly 2 to 4 OKLCH lightness points above the last.
nodes.why: Tiny lightness steps give elevation without the 'cards on charcoal' look that reads as a default dark theme.
nodes.implementation: --bg-0:oklch(10% .003 270);--bg-1:oklch(13% .003 270);--bg-2:oklch(15.5% .003 270);--bg-3:oklch(18% .003 270); .card{background:var(--bg-1);box-shadow:none}
nodes.pitfalls: Krebs flags 'permanent dark mode with medium-grey body text and all-caps labels' (20.3%); the ladder only looks considered if body text stays at Lc 75 plus and labels are few.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Always-dark is itself a tell; the surface ladder is what separates Linear from a generated dark page, together with restraint in labels and glows.

nodes.name: Translucent white hairlines in dark mode
nodes.what: Borders on dark surfaces as white at 4 to 16% alpha rather than solid grey: Raycast rgba(255,255,255,0.08) soft and 0.16 strong, plus a solid #242728 for cards; Resend 0.04 divider, 0.06 hairline, 0.14 strong; Framer a top-edge highlight rgba(255,255,255,0.10) with rgba(0,0,0,0.25) shadow under floating cards; Linear solid #23252a, #34343a, #3e3e44. The alpha border adapts automatically to whichever surface step it sits on.
nodes.why: Alpha borders stay proportional to their background, so one token works across the whole surface ladder.
nodes.implementation: --hairline:rgb(255 255 255/.08);--hairline-strong:rgb(255 255 255/.16); .card{border:1px solid var(--hairline);box-shadow:inset 0 1px 0 rgb(255 255 255/.06)}
nodes.pitfalls: Above 0.16 alpha the borders glow and the page turns into a wireframe; 1px only, never 2px.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Generated dark themes use solid border-gray-800 (#1f2937, blue-tinted) which clashes with neutral blacks.

nodes.name: Accent as low-alpha glow, never solid
nodes.what: On dark sites chromatic colour appears as an atmospheric wash rather than a fill: Resend defines accent glows rgba(255,89,0,0.22), rgba(0,117,255,0.34), rgba(34,255,153,0.18), rgba(255,32,71,0.34) and uses the accents only as glows; Raycast's four accents exist only in illustrations with 15% alpha soft variants; GitHub's Copilot gradient #9350ff to #0e0aa2 is a single background scene. One glow per page, behind a product shot or the hero, radius 400px plus.
nodes.why: A soft wash gives a dark page warmth and depth without introducing a second UI colour.
nodes.implementation: .hero::before{content:'';position:absolute;inset:-20%;background:radial-gradient(60% 50% at 50% 0%,rgb(255 89 0/.22),transparent 70%);pointer-events:none}
nodes.pitfalls: Krebs pattern 8 is 'large coloured glows and coloured box-shadows' on buttons and cards; a glow on a CTA or on every card is the tell, one scenic glow is not.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Depends entirely on count and placement: one radial-gradient behind the hero reads as photography lighting; glows on components read as generated.

nodes.name: Off-white text ladder on dark
nodes.what: Dark-mode text is never #fff for body: Linear #f7f8f8 headline, #d0d6e0 muted, #8a8f98 subtle, #62666d tertiary; Raycast #f4f4f6, #cdcdcd, #9c9c9d, #6a6b6c, #434345; Resend #fcfdff with body at 86% alpha and secondary at 70%; Mercury #ededf3 and an explicit rule never to use #000 fills or #fff text except on indigo. Body sits at the second step, not the first.
nodes.why: Slightly dimmed body text reduces halation on OLED while keeping headlines bright, so hierarchy survives without size changes.
nodes.implementation: --ink-1:#f4f4f6;--ink-2:#cdcdcd;--ink-3:#9c9c9d;--ink-4:#6a6b6c; body{color:var(--ink-2)} h1,h2{color:var(--ink-1)} small{color:var(--ink-3)}
nodes.pitfalls: Krebs pattern 6 is 'barely passing body-text contrast in dark themes'; keep body at step two (around #cdcdcd on #0d0d0d, APCA Lc 80 plus), not at the muted step.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Grey-on-black body text is a tell when it fails contrast; a five-step ladder with body near the top is the considered version.

nodes.name: Warm dark mode (brown-black)
nodes.what: A dark theme tinted toward brown instead of blue: Lovable canvas #2b2622, soft #383330, hairline #3f3a36, body #c9c0ad, strong #dad2c1, primary #f7f5f0; PostHog's dark surface #23251d; ElevenLabs dark hero #0c0a09 with #1c1917 cards (Tailwind stone 950/900); Zed code blocks #1a1b1e; Medium's suggested dark #1a1a18 with ink #f1ede4. Hue 50 to 80 in OKLCH, chroma 0.004 to 0.012.
nodes.why: Warm darks feel like a lit room instead of a terminal and sit well with serif type and photography.
nodes.implementation: --canvas:oklch(22% .012 60);--surface:oklch(27% .01 60);--hairline:oklch(31% .01 60);--ink:oklch(85% .02 80)
nodes.pitfalls: Warm darks with a cool accent (Tailwind blue-500) look muddy; pick an accent in the same hemisphere (orange, olive, clay) or none.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Generated dark modes are slate or zinc; a brown-black canvas is almost never emitted.

nodes.name: One-hue tinted neutrals
nodes.what: Every grey derived from a single hue token so the whole neutral ramp leans the same way: Open Props defines --gray-0 to --gray-15 as oklch(L var(--gray-chroma) var(--gray-hue)) with L from 99% to 10%; Tailwind v4 ships slate (hue 248 to 265, chroma up to 0.042), zinc (286), stone (49 to 106, chroma 0.001 to 0.006), neutral (0); Radix pairs sand with yellow/amber/orange/brown, olive with grass/lime, sage with teal/green, slate with blue/indigo, mauve with red/pink/purple. Pick the hue of your accent and set chroma 0.005 to 0.02.
nodes.why: Greys that share the accent's hue make the accent look native, and the ramp reads as one material rather than Photoshop grey.
nodes.pitfalls: Chroma above 0.03 on light neutrals turns them into pastels; stay under 0.02 for backgrounds, under 0.01 at the 95% step.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Default Tailwind gray/slate are everywhere; a custom hue token with oklch is visibly different (warm or olive greys).

nodes.name: Three-variable theme (base, accent, contrast)
nodes.what: Linear replaced 98 per-theme variables with three inputs: a base colour in LCH, an accent colour and a contrast number (30 to 100), from which surfaces, text, icons and controls are generated; elevated and translucent surfaces are derived by shifting lightness up a few points and lowering chroma slightly. A third-party reconstruction puts the default dark base near L 12, C 2, H 270. Modern CSS can do this in the browser with relative colour syntax.
nodes.why: A generated palette is internally consistent by construction and lets users retheme without breaking contrast.
nodes.implementation: --base:oklch(14% .006 270);--surface-1:oklch(from var(--base) calc(l + .03) calc(c * .9) h);--surface-2:oklch(from var(--base) calc(l + .06) calc(c * .8) h);--ink:oklch(from var(--base) calc(l + .8) c h)
nodes.pitfalls: The LCH or OKLCH gamut clips at high chroma; clamp chroma per lightness or colours fall out of sRGB.
nodes.ai_tell_note: The technique is invisible in the result but makes a dark theme coherent in a way a hand-picked gray-800/900 palette never is.

nodes.name: Radix 12-step scale semantics
nodes.what: A scale where each step has a job: 1 to 2 app backgrounds, 3 to 5 component backgrounds (normal, hover, pressed), 6 to 8 borders (subtle, interactive, strong/focus), 9 to 10 solid fills (9 is peak chroma; sky, mint, lime, yellow and amber take dark text, the rest white), 11 to 12 text (Lc 60 and Lc 90 APCA guaranteed on step 2). Vercel's Geist uses the same logic in ten steps (100 default bg, 200 hover, 300 active, 400 to 600 borders, 700 to 800 high-contrast bg, 900 to 1000 text). Dark mode swaps in the dark scale with identical semantics.
nodes.why: Assigning roles to steps removes guesswork and keeps hover, border and text contrast consistent across every hue.
nodes.implementation: .btn{background:var(--blue-4);border:1px solid var(--blue-7);color:var(--blue-11)} .btn:hover{background:var(--blue-5);border-color:var(--blue-8)}
nodes.pitfalls: Using step 9 for body text or step 3 for borders is the common misuse; stick to the map.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Tailwind's 50 to 950 steps have no semantic roles, which is why generated UIs pick 500 for everything.

nodes.name: OKLCH accents with even perceived brightness
nodes.what: Accents specified in OKLCH so that different hues at the same lightness feel equally loud: Tailwind v4 rebuilt its palette this way (red-500 oklch(63.7% 0.237 25.331), orange-500 oklch(70.5% 0.213 47.604), lime-400 oklch(84.1% 0.238 128.85), blue-600 oklch(54.6% 0.245 262.881)); Evil Martians' Harmony builds shades with OKLCH plus APCA contrast targets and ships P3 variants; Substack's orange is oklch(0.70 0.20 42). Use chroma up to 0.3 inside @supports (color: oklch(0 0 0)) with a hex fallback.
nodes.why: Equal-lightness accents let two or three colours coexist without one shouting, and P3 chroma reaches colours hex cannot.
nodes.implementation: --accent:#f54e00; @supports (color:oklch(0 0 0)){:root{--accent:oklch(66% .22 40)}}
nodes.pitfalls: Copying hex from a v3 palette into a v4 project shifts colours; and oklch() in older Safari needs the fallback line first.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Tailwind defaults are still recognisable by hue; the win is custom hues at matched lightness, not the syntax itself.

nodes.name: International Orange or signal red accent
nodes.what: A warm safety colour as the only accent on paper or black: PostHog #f54e00 (its handbook bans it for warnings), Substack #ff6719, Mintlify testimonial cards #f55a3c, Raycast's hero stripe #ff5757 to #a1131a, Arc's red #fb3a4d, Teenage Engineering's --te-orange #f05a24, Vercel's error #ee0000, Anthropic clay #d97757. International Orange proper is #ff4f00; Golden Gate is #c0362c. Use it on one element per viewport.
nodes.why: Orange-red reads as a physical label or warning tape, so it feels industrial and human against black or cream.
nodes.implementation: --accent:#f54e00;--accent-ink:#fff; .marker{background:var(--accent);color:var(--accent-ink);padding:.1em .3em}
nodes.pitfalls: Orange on a blue-tinted dark (#0f172a) looks like a Bootstrap alert; keep the dark neutral or warm.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Generated palettes pick blue, violet or teal; orange-red is a studio signal.

nodes.name: Cobalt or IKB blue as the only colour
nodes.what: A deep, saturated blue as the single accent on paper, close to International Klein Blue (#002fa7) or cobalt: Zed #004edb with hover #003fb5 and pressed #003299 on #f5f5f3; Arc's press band #3139fb with navy text #000354 on #fffcec; Framer #0099ff on #090909; Vercel's link #0070f3; Mercury's #5266eb on indigo-dark #171721. Keep it away from violet (hue under 270 in OKLCH).
nodes.why: Cobalt on warm paper is a classic print pairing that reads as serious and crafted rather than corporate.
nodes.implementation: --accent:oklch(45% .24 262); /* approx #004edb */ --accent-hover:oklch(40% .22 262)
nodes.pitfalls: Drifting the hue toward 280 turns cobalt into the indigo that marks generated CTAs; stay at hue 255 to 265 with chroma 0.2 plus.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Tailwind blue-600 is common, but deep IKB-range blue on cream paper is not.

nodes.name: Acid or lime accent on dark or cream
nodes.what: A yellow-green accent used sparingly: Granola olive #5b6f00 CTA with #788c15 hover, #b2c248 soft and #d1e043 gradient stop on cream #f7f7f2; Resend #11ff99; Supabase #3ecf8e; GitHub's #5fed83 glow and accent dots; Mintlify #00d4a4; Figma's lime block #dceeb1; Tailwind lime-400 oklch(84.1% 0.238 128.85). Dark text (#0e0f0c) on the acid, never white.
nodes.why: Acid green is high-energy and still uncommon in corporate palettes, so it gives tech brands a street or studio edge.
nodes.implementation: --acid:oklch(86% .22 125);--olive:oklch(48% .12 120); .btn{background:var(--acid);color:#0e0f0c}
nodes.pitfalls: Pure #39ff14 at large areas vibrates; keep chroma under 0.24 and use the olive (#5b6f00) for text-weight uses.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Teal and emerald (#10b981) are generated defaults; acid lime and olive are not.

nodes.name: Yellow highlighter as annotation
nodes.what: Marker yellow used only behind words or as a tag, never as a surface: Granola #febe29 behind action verbs in the hero; Notion's highlight banner #f9e79f and card tint #fef7d6; Clerk brand yellow #fff963; Supabase chart yellow #ffdb13; Teenage Engineering yellow #fab413 on product only; PostHog primary #f7a501. Rendered as a background gradient clipped to the text line with box-decoration-break so it wraps like a real marker.
nodes.why: A highlighter stroke reads as a human edit on top of finished type.
nodes.implementation: .hl{background:linear-gradient(transparent 55%,#febe29 55% 92%,transparent 92%);box-decoration-break:clone;-webkit-box-decoration-break:clone;padding:0 .1em}
nodes.pitfalls: More than one highlighted phrase per screen turns into a sale flyer.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Generated heroes colour a word with the accent via text colour; the background-marker form is distinct.

nodes.name: Pastel tinted cards instead of white cards
nodes.what: Each feature card gets its own low-chroma tint with no border and no shadow: Notion #ffe8d4 peach, #fde0ec rose, #d9f3e1 mint, #e6e0f5 lavender, #dcecfa sky, #fef7d6 yellow, #f8f5e8 cream, #f0eeec grey at 24px radius; Figma blocks #dceeb1, #c5b0f4, #f4ecd6, #c8e6cd, #efd4d4, #f3c9b6 and one navy #1f1d3d; Anthropic #e3dacc, #ebdbbc, #d4a27f kraft tones; Cursor timeline pastels #dfa88f, #9fc9a2, #9fbbe0, #c0a8dd. Tints sit at OKLCH L 88 to 94, chroma 0.03 to 0.07.
nodes.why: Tints separate cards by colour instead of by chrome, so the grid reads as a palette rather than a component list.
nodes.implementation: .card{background:oklch(92% .05 var(--card-hue));border:0;border-radius:24px;padding:32px} .card:nth-child(2){--card-hue:140}
nodes.pitfalls: Three identical tinted cards with an icon on top is still Krebs pattern 12; vary card size and content type, and drop the icons.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Pastel cards appear in generated 'friendly SaaS' pages; the handmade version uses warm, slightly dirty tints (kraft, olive, clay) and uneven card sizes.

nodes.name: Colour blocking by section
nodes.what: Full-bleed sections in flat, different colours with hard edges and no gradient between: Arc's #3139fb press band on a #fffcec page; Stripe's cream #f5e9d4 band and navy #1c1e54 pricing card on white; Anthropic's #000 inverse bands with ivory text; Notion's navy #0a1530 hero and #070f24 promo strip; Vercel's polarity-flipped #171717 bands; Mintlify's inverted startups page. Two to three blocks per page, each with its own text colour, never a tinted gradient.
nodes.why: Hard colour edges give a long page rhythm and make each section feel like a poster rather than a scroll.
nodes.implementation: section.band{background:#3139fb;color:#fffcec;padding-block:clamp(4rem,10vw,9rem)} section.band+section{margin-top:0}
nodes.pitfalls: Rounded section corners and soft shadows between blocks reintroduce the card look; keep the edges square and flush.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Generated pages alternate white and gray-50; a saturated flat band is a layout decision.

nodes.name: Two canvas tracks that never blend
nodes.what: Instead of a light/dark toggle, two fixed tracks assigned by page type: Shopify uses a #000 cinematic track (white text, outline pill buttons) for marketing and a #fbfbf5 transactional track (black ink, solid pills, mint accents #c1fbd4 and #d4f9e0 only here); Mercury keeps the top of funnel on #171721 and inputs and dashboard on #fbfcfd; Teenage Engineering themes per product (#000 body, #f6f8f7 product pages). The two tracks are never mixed on one page.
nodes.why: Each track is optimised for its job (atmosphere vs legibility) and the switch between them marks a change of intent.
nodes.implementation: html[data-track=cinematic]{--canvas:#000;--ink:#fff;--btn:transparent;--btn-border:#fff} html[data-track=transactional]{--canvas:#fbfbf5;--ink:#000;--btn:#000}
nodes.pitfalls: Accents must be re-specified per track (mint only on light at Shopify); reusing one accent across both looks like a theme toggle.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Generated sites add a dark-mode switch; fixed tracks by page type are a brand-architecture decision.

nodes.name: Duotone or monochrome imagery
nodes.what: Photography stripped to greyscale or mapped to two brand colours so the UI stays colourless: Nothing keeps dark tones only in photography while UI tokens are black, white and two greys; Teenage Engineering product shots on #e5e5e5 greys; Medium's single green editorial illustration on cream. Implement with filter grayscale plus a mix-blend-mode multiply tint, or an SVG feComponentTransfer duotone for exact brand colours.
nodes.why: Monochrome images let type and one accent own the colour budget, and they unify stock photos of different quality.
nodes.implementation: img.mono{filter:grayscale(1) contrast(1.05)} .duo{background:var(--accent)} .duo img{mix-blend-mode:multiply;filter:grayscale(1) contrast(1.1)}
nodes.pitfalls: Duotone in purple and teal is the 2016 Spotify look; use ink plus paper, or ink plus the single accent.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Generated pages use full-colour stock or gradient placeholders.

nodes.name: Opacity ramps instead of extra greys
nodes.what: Secondary text and subtle fills derived from the ink colour at fixed alphas rather than separate grey hexes: PostHog paragraphs at 90%, links 95%, hover 100%; Lovable charcoal #1c1c1c at .83 (strong), .82 (body), .40 (interactive borders), .04 (hover bg), .03 (overlays); Resend body rgba(252,253,255,.86) and .70; Raycast on-dark-mute at .72. The ramp travels with the ink across light and dark.
nodes.why: Alpha steps inherit the canvas tint automatically, so one ink token yields a coherent family of greys on any background.
nodes.implementation: --ink:#1c1c1c;--ink-82:color-mix(in oklch,var(--ink) 82%,transparent);--ink-40:color-mix(in oklch,var(--ink) 40%,transparent);--ink-04:color-mix(in oklch,var(--ink) 4%,transparent)
nodes.pitfalls: Alpha text over images or tinted cards changes colour unpredictably; use solid tokens where text sits on imagery.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Generated CSS uses text-gray-500; ink-at-alpha is a system choice that keeps hue consistent.

nodes.name: Warm hairline instead of shadow
nodes.what: Elevation comes from a 1px border whose hue matches the canvas, with shadows at 4 to 6% or none: Dub #e5e5e5 as 'the system's elevation mechanism'; Zed #e2e2de warm hairline with shadows at rgba(20,20,20,.04/.06); Anthropic #d1cfc5 on ivory; Supabase #dfdfdf; Vercel #ebebeb; Cursor #e6e5e0 on #f7f7f4; Raycast declares no drop shadows at all. Strong variant one step darker for inputs (#d4d4ce, #c7c7c7).
nodes.why: Hairlines keep the surface flat and print-like, while shadows push a page toward the generic card look.
nodes.implementation: --hairline:oklch(90% .008 80);--hairline-strong:oklch(84% .01 80); .card{border:1px solid var(--hairline);box-shadow:0 1px 2px rgb(20 20 20/.04)}
nodes.pitfalls: A cool #e5e7eb border on a warm canvas is the most common giveaway of a Tailwind default left in place.
nodes.ai_tell_note: shadow-md on cards is the generated default; a matched warm hairline is a correction a designer makes.

nodes.name: Dark-mode accent lightened, not reused
nodes.what: The brand colour shifts lighter and slightly less saturated on dark surfaces: Zed #004edb becomes #5a8bff in its dark variant with on-brand text #0a0c10; Linear #5e6ad2 with hover #828fff; GitHub links #8dd6ff on #0d1117 versus #4493f8 in product; Perplexity shifts toward #00a1ac in dark. Rule: raise OKLCH lightness by 15 to 25 points and lower chroma by about 10%, and swap text-on-accent to dark.
nodes.why: The light-mode accent fails contrast on black and looks dull; the lifted version keeps the hue identity and passes.
nodes.implementation: --accent:oklch(45% .24 262); @media (prefers-color-scheme:dark){:root{--accent:oklch(from var(--accent) calc(l + .2) calc(c * .9) h);--on-accent:#0a0c10}}
nodes.pitfalls: Lightening a purple accent lands at lavender and feeds the violet-CTA cliche; keep the hue honest and test on step-2 surface.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Generated dark modes reuse the same accent hex; the shift is a craft step.

nodes.name: Purple or indigo CTA on dark
nodes.what: A saturated violet or indigo primary button (#6c47ff Clerk, #7928ca Vercel violet, #c084fc, #8b5cf6) on a dark or white page, often with a matching gradient and glow. Krebs names 'VibeCode Purple' as a core pattern and counts purple/indigo/violet CTAs on 10.7% of Show HN sites; it is also the shadcn/ui default-adjacent look.
nodes.why: Purple once signalled 'creative tech' (Stripe, Twitch); saturation made it the path of least resistance for generators.
nodes.implementation: Replace with ink, International Orange, cobalt or acid lime; if purple is required use oklch(45% .12 300) and white or ink CTAs.
nodes.pitfalls: Included as a blacklist entry; if a violet brand colour is mandated, desaturate (Railway #553f83) and keep it off the primary button.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Named explicitly in the 2026 audit.

nodes.name: Gradient restricted to one stripe or illustration
nodes.what: Gradients allowed only as a single named artefact: Vercel's three brand gradients (#007cf0 to #00dfd8, #7928ca to #ff0080, #ff4d4d to #f9cb28) live on the 'Develop, Preview, Ship' words only; Raycast's red stripe #ff5757 to #a1131a is used once per page at most; Mintlify's hero sky #87a8c8 to #f5e9d8; Railway's hero #291839 to #3d2259 to #180d43; PostHog's handbook sets 'no gradients by default'. Never on buttons, borders, text or card backgrounds.
nodes.why: One gradient is an image; gradients on components are a theme, and the audit found gradients on 28% of generated sites.
nodes.implementation: .stripe{height:6px;background:linear-gradient(90deg,#ff5757,#a1131a)} /* and nowhere else: audit with grep 'gradient' */
nodes.pitfalls: Gradient text on the hero headline and gradient borders on cards are both on the tell list; one stripe, one place.
nodes.ai_tell_note: The constraint is the idea; the presence of any gradient raises suspicion, so budget exactly one.

nodes.name: Grain overlay on flat colour
nodes.what: A fine monochrome noise at 3 to 8% opacity over flat canvases and colour blocks, usually via an SVG feTurbulence filter or a tiled 256px PNG, with mix-blend-mode overlay or soft-light; paired with warm paper (#f4f1ea family) it reads as uncoated stock, and over a dark #0c0a09 it reads as film. Daylight's e-paper hardware site and many 2024 to 2026 studio sites use it; keep the noise static (no animation) and below 0.08 alpha.
nodes.why: Grain breaks the perfectly flat digital fill and makes colour blocks feel physical.
nodes.implementation: body::after{content:'';position:fixed;inset:0;pointer-events:none;opacity:.06;mix-blend-mode:multiply;background:url("data:image/svg+xml;utf8,<svg xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg' width='256' height='256'><filter id='n'><feTurbulence type='fractalNoise' baseFrequency='.9' numOctaves='2' stitchTiles='stitch'/></filter><rect width='100%' height='100%' filter='url(%23n)'/></svg>")}
nodes.pitfalls: Animated grain and grain over text at more than 8% hurt legibility and look like a 2019 Awwwards template.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Generators do not emit feTurbulence; it is a hand-authored texture, though it is also a known studio cliche when overdone.

nodes.name: Ruled paper lines
nodes.what: Horizontal rules every 32px at 8 percent alpha behind the hero and the feature section, like a ruled notebook, with the type sitting on the lines; nothing else is decorated.
nodes.implementation: background-image: repeating-linear-gradient(0deg, transparent 0 31px, color-mix(in oklab, var(--pf-color-text) 8%, transparent) 31px 32px); align the line step with the body line height.
nodes.ai_tell_note: A stationery reference tied to note-taking and writing products; not in any template kit.

nodes.name: Split-screen hero
nodes.what: Two full-height panels with no gutter: text bottom-left on the page colour, artwork centred on a panel in the primary colour; the fold is a hard vertical edge.
nodes.implementation: A two-column grid at 88svh; the art panel background primary and colour on-primary; text aligned to the bottom.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Hard edges and a solid colour panel; no gradient, no screenshot.

nodes.name: Diagonal marquee bands
nodes.what: Two marquee bands cross the first screen at opposite angles (about minus six and plus five degrees), one in ink, one in the primary colour, carrying the brand and the product nouns; the headline sits below them.
nodes.implementation: Absolutely positioned bands rotated with `rotate`, each with a duplicated track and a linear 30s animation, the second reversed; reduced motion stops them.
nodes.ai_tell_note: A festival device; one page, two bands, never on a product page.

nodes.name: Mosaic hero
nodes.what: The first screen is a four-column mosaic of artwork tiles with the headline and actions living in one dark tile that spans two columns and two rows.
nodes.implementation: CSS grid with span classes; the text tile inverts to ink with bg-coloured type; tiles have 1px hairlines.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Tiles of real work or product shots; the text tile is part of the grid, not floating over it.

nodes.name: Kinetic type hero
nodes.what: Three giant lines of the headline, the middle one outlined, each indented a little more; as the page scrolls the lines slide at different speeds, the middle one the other way.
nodes.implementation: Scroll-driven animation: `animation-timeline: scroll()` on each row with a translate keyframe, the middle row reversed; static when the feature or motion is off.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Kinetic type is a poster move; keep the lines to three and the motion to a few viewport widths.

nodes.name: Fanned cards hero
nodes.what: Five rotated cards fanned from one corner beside the headline, each with artwork and a mono index; hovering lifts a card.
nodes.implementation: Absolutely positioned cards with `rotate: calc(-10deg + var(--i) * 5deg)` and a bottom-centre transform origin; translate on hover.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Cards as objects, not as a grid; five, uneven, with real images.

nodes.name: Image mosaic features
nodes.what: Features as an image-led masonry: wide and tall tiles with a caption strip at the bottom carrying an index, a title and (on large tiles) one sentence.
nodes.implementation: Grid with `grid-auto-flow: dense`, 200px rows, span classes; captions over a translucent bg strip.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Imagery with captions instead of icon cards.

nodes.name: Poster band
nodes.what: A full-bleed band of artwork with the wordmark across it at 20vw in difference blend, and one mono line in the corner; sits between features and proof as a breath.
nodes.implementation: A 70vh section, artwork absolutely positioned, the word in `mix-blend-mode: difference` so it reads on any colour.
nodes.ai_tell_note: A poster moment, once per page.

nodes.name: Parallax giant word
nodes.what: The giant wordmark in the footer or poster band drifts a few viewport widths sideways as it scrolls through the viewport.
nodes.implementation: `animation-timeline: view()` with a translate keyframe on the word; nothing else moves; reduced motion disables it.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Scroll-linked, reversible, one element.

nodes.name: Hero art scales out
nodes.what: The hero artwork grows slightly and fades as it leaves the viewport, so the first screen releases into the page.
nodes.implementation: `animation-timeline: view()` with `animation-range: exit` and a scale and opacity keyframe.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Subtle, reversible, no library.

nodes.name: Skewed marquee
nodes.what: The marquee line skews a few degrees as it scrolls through the viewport, as if dragged by the scroll.
nodes.implementation: A second animation on the track driven by `animation-timeline: view()` with a skew keyframe.
nodes.ai_tell_note: A studio flourish for one marquee.

nodes.name: Tilted framed images
nodes.what: Images sit on a raised card with a hard offset shadow in ink, rotated a degree or two, like prints laid on a table.
nodes.implementation: `rotate: -1.5deg` and `box-shadow: 10px 12px 0 ink` on the artwork; alternate the angle per image.
nodes.ai_tell_note: A physical reference that depends on real photographs.

nodes.name: Lime velodrome
nodes.notes: Lando Norris's lime on near-black with cream for text panels; one hot colour at speed.

nodes.name: Poster red
nodes.notes: Don't Board Me's bone white with a signal red and a mustard second; festival energy without gradients.

nodes.name: Ultramarine & sand
nodes.notes: Exo Ape's sand with a deep ultramarine; cool, architectural, calm.

nodes.name: Pastel studio
nodes.notes: Craft's canvas with mint, butter and sky blocks; playful without a purple gradient.

nodes.name: Ink & mustard
nodes.notes: Warm black with a mustard primary and a bone second; poster contrast for events.

nodes.name: Marine & coral
nodes.notes: Maven's lapis navy with a coral accent on a cool white; confident and warm at once.

nodes.name: Sage & ink
nodes.notes: Causal's paint swatches: linen, sage, brick and ink.

nodes.name: Blush & navy
nodes.notes: Headspace's blush off-white with a saturated blue and a yellow highlight; playful consumer.

nodes.name: Big Shoulders / Mona Sans
nodes.notes: A condensed display face at 900 over a variable grotesque; the Lando Norris register with free faces.

nodes.name: Anton / Instrument Sans
nodes.notes: A heavy condensed gothic for one line per screen with a grotesque body that stays out of the way.

nodes.name: Unbounded / Geist
nodes.notes: A wide display face that fills a line with few words over a quiet grotesque.

nodes.name: Archivo Black / Hanken Grotesk
nodes.notes: The heaviest free grotesque for wordmarks and clipped type; Hanken for everything else.

nodes.name: Syne / Instrument Sans
nodes.notes: Syne widens as it gets heavier; at 800 it is a poster face. Kept to the H1.

nodes.name: Bricolage Grotesque / Geist
nodes.notes: Bricolage at its compressed optical sizes over Geist; character in the headline, neutrality below.

nodes.name: Fraunces / Instrument Sans
nodes.notes: Fraunces with its WONK axis for a headline that smiles, a plain grotesque body.

nodes.name: Parkinsans / Geist
nodes.notes: Soft terminals at display size over a neutral body.

nodes.name: Velodrome
nodes.summary: Lando Norris energy: near-black, lime and cream, a condensed display face at 900, kinetic type that slides with scroll, a marquee, a poster band and sourced count-ups. Speed as a design language.

nodes.name: Festival poster
nodes.summary: Bone white, signal red and mustard; a heavy condensed gothic; diagonal marquee bands crossing the hero; rays and stamps as artwork; a ticket for the call to action. Loud, flat, printed.

nodes.name: Ultramarine
nodes.summary: Exo Ape's sand and deep ultramarine, a hairline-weight display face, a split-screen first screen with the artwork on a solid blue panel, a torus of rings, mosaic features and a colophon. Architectural calm.

nodes.name: Pastel blocks
nodes.summary: Craft and Figma's tinted blocks: a warm canvas, sections in mint, butter and sky with hard edges, a geometric display with soft terminals, fanned cards, tilted framed images and stickers. Playful without a gradient.

nodes.name: Mosaic wall
nodes.summary: A poster wall: the first screen is a mosaic of tiles with the text as one dark tile, mosaic features, a wide display face, a marine palette with a coral counter; image-led from the first pixel.

nodes.name: Focus board
nodes.what: The main screen is the one number or object the product is about, set at display size with tabular numerals, the next action beside it and a short list of the other live items; no table above the fold.
nodes.implementation: A two-column grid: figure at clamp(6rem, 24vw, 22rem) on a surface panel, a hairline list on the right; count-up when the value changes.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Scoreboards, timers, balances and counters are read from a distance; the template dashboard is not.

nodes.name: Cards view
nodes.what: Items as cards with a small figure, an index, a title, one line and a status; the grid fills by available width.
nodes.implementation: An auto-fill grid at 240px minimum; cards use the direction's card edge; the figure is artwork or a thumbnail.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Fine when every item has an image or a figure; otherwise a list.

nodes.name: Kanban columns
nodes.what: Work laid out as three columns with counts in the headers and compact cards; the board is the primary view, not a tab.
nodes.implementation: Three equal columns on a surface tint; cards with an index, a title and a meta line; drag can come later.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Columns name real states (up next, in play, done), never placeholder lanes.

nodes.name: Activity feed
nodes.what: A chronological feed as the home view: avatar, actor, verb, object and time per row, hairlines between rows, newest first.
nodes.implementation: An ordered list with a three-column grid per row; times in mono; load more at the end.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Products about people and events open on what happened, not on a table.

nodes.name: Bottom tab shell
nodes.what: A phone-first shell: a slim app bar with the wordmark and the time, content, and a bottom tab bar with four destinations inside the safe area.
nodes.implementation: Sticky bottom nav with padding-bottom including the safe-area inset; the active tab fills its glyph with the primary colour.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Apps used standing up (scoring, timing, fitness) live in the thumb zone.

nodes.name: Focus shell with no chrome
nodes.what: No sidebar and no top nav: one slim bar with the wordmark, the current mode in mono and a Menu word; the view takes the whole viewport.
nodes.implementation: A single-column shell; detail panels are dropped; the menu word opens the overlay from the marketing draft.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Right for a live mode (a game in progress, a presentation, a kiosk); wrong for admin tools.

nodes.name: Dot-matrix headline
nodes.what: The headline is rendered as a field of round dots on a grid, like an LED board or a bead sign; near the pointer the dots swell and take the accent colour, then settle. Works with any heading face.
nodes.implementation: Draw the text to an offscreen canvas in the heading font, sample it on a grid of about one eleventh of the font size, draw a circle per lit cell; on pointermove scale and tint dots within a radius; redraw on palette change; the real text stays in the DOM for screen readers.
nodes.ai_tell_note: A rendering of the brand's own type; one headline per page, and only where a style asks for it.

nodes.name: Character reveal
nodes.what: Each character of the headline rises and sharpens in turn, 600ms per character with an 18ms stagger, once on load; nothing else animates.
nodes.implementation: Split text nodes into spans with a per-character delay variable; blur 2px to 0 with a quintic ease; respect reduced motion.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Common on studio sites; fine once per page on the first line.

nodes.name: Decode scramble
nodes.what: The headline resolves from a run of glyphs left to right over about 900ms; hovering a navigation link re-scrambles it for 400ms.
nodes.implementation: requestAnimationFrame loop replacing unresolved characters from a small glyph set; keep spaces; store the original text in a data attribute.
nodes.ai_tell_note: A terminal and hardware device; pairs with mono labels, never with a serif voice.

nodes.name: Weight follows the pointer
nodes.what: On a variable heading face the headline's weight slides between 300 and 900 as the pointer crosses the viewport, with a lag, so the type breathes.
nodes.implementation: Set font-variation-settings wght from pointer x with a lerp of .12; only on fine pointers; needs a variable face (Bricolage Grotesque, Fraunces, Big Shoulders, Mona Sans, Geologica).
nodes.ai_tell_note: A variable-font demonstration that belongs on type-led pages.

nodes.name: Scroll velocity skew
nodes.what: Marquees and giant lines lean a few degrees in the scroll direction and settle when scrolling stops.
nodes.implementation: Track scroll velocity; apply skewX clamped to 12 degrees with a decay of .86 per frame.
nodes.ai_tell_note: A studio flourish; one page, the marquee and ticker only.

nodes.name: Pointer dot grid
nodes.what: A lattice of small dots behind the hero that bulge and drift toward the pointer within a 180px radius; static at lower motion levels.
nodes.implementation: A canvas sized to the hero; 28px gap; radius and offset per dot computed from pointer distance; redraw on pointermove only.
nodes.ai_tell_note: A live stage without a library; reads as engineered.

nodes.name: Artwork trail
nodes.what: Small copies of the page's own artwork spawn under the pointer as it crosses the hero, drift up and fade in under a second.
nodes.implementation: Clone an SVG every 90ms at the pointer, rotate randomly, animate opacity and scale, remove after 900ms; fine pointers only, never in frames.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Portfolio and studio device; it must use the page's real imagery.

nodes.name: Diagonal stripe field
nodes.what: Fine diagonal hairline stripes behind the hero at 9 percent alpha, moving slowly at motion level 2 and above; a construction-tape register.
nodes.implementation: repeating-linear-gradient at 135deg with a 14px period on a pseudo element; a 2.4s background-position animation.
nodes.ai_tell_note: A texture tied to engineering and event brands.

nodes.name: Blinking caret on the action
nodes.what: The primary button ends with a block caret that blinks once a second, as a terminal prompt does.
nodes.implementation: A pseudo element of .5em by 1em in currentColor with a steps(1) blink; off at motion level 0.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Terminal brands only; one button.

nodes.name: Rotating badge
nodes.what: A circular stamp with text on a path turns once every 24 seconds, slowly enough to read.
nodes.implementation: rotate keyframe on the stamp artwork; paused under reduced motion and at level 0.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Everywhere on templates when fast; slow and once per page it still works for events and studios.

nodes.name: Pinned action bar
nodes.what: Once the hero scrolls away, a slim pill pinned to the bottom carries the one line and the primary action; it hides again at the top.
nodes.implementation: A fixed element toggled by an IntersectionObserver on the hero; sits above the safe-area inset; ink background, paper text.
nodes.ai_tell_note: Keeps the one action reachable on long pages without a sticky header.

nodes.name: LED board
nodes.notes: Black glass with bone-white dots and one green lamp colour; the register of a station board.

nodes.name: Broadcast
nodes.notes: Charcoal, chalk and a broadcast blue with an amber second; a live graphics register.

nodes.name: Workshop
nodes.notes: Kraft paper, soot and safety orange; a workshop tag.

nodes.name: Ink & bloom
nodes.notes: Paper white, ink and one magenta used like a highlighter.

nodes.name: Doto / Mona Sans
nodes.notes: A dot-matrix display face for the one line that matters, with a neutral variable sans for everything else; the dots are the picture.

nodes.name: Silkscreen / IBM Plex Sans
nodes.notes: A coarse pixel face at large sizes only; Plex keeps the body readable.

nodes.name: Rubik Mono One / Archivo
nodes.notes: A wide heavy mono display for scoreboards and lower thirds over a plain grotesque.

nodes.name: Bungee / Work Sans
nodes.notes: A sign-painter display face for one word per screen.

nodes.name: Big Shoulders Stencil / Mona Sans
nodes.notes: A stencil cut of a condensed display for crate-stamp headlines.

nodes.name: Bricolage Grotesque / Geist
nodes.notes: Bricolage across its weight axis, so the headline can move from 300 to 800 under the pointer.

nodes.name: Tiny5 / Geist
nodes.notes: A five-pixel face with a width axis for labels and one headline; Geist for text.

nodes.name: LED board
nodes.summary: A station departure board: black glass, bone dots, one green lamp colour. The headline is drawn as a dot matrix that lights up under the pointer, the figures are tabular, the buttons are brackets, a blinking caret marks the action.

nodes.name: Broadcast
nodes.summary: Live graphics: charcoal, chalk and broadcast blue, a wide heavy mono display, a focus board with the one figure at display size, tickers that lean with scroll speed, count-ups, a pinned action.

nodes.name: Workshop
nodes.summary: A workshop tag: kraft paper, soot, safety orange, a stencil display, diagonal stripe fields, stamps that turn slowly, object stand-ins on a seamless, a ticket to book.

nodes.name: Variable
nodes.summary: Type that moves: a variable grotesque across its whole weight axis, the headline's weight following the pointer, characters revealing one by one, ink on paper with one magenta highlighter; everything else still.

nodes.name: Pixel arcade
nodes.summary: A cabinet and a cartridge: a coarse pixel display face, pixel-art marks, a pointer grid behind the hero, scramble on the headline, stickers, one hot colour on black or paper; playful without being childish.
